jobs.title: Product Tester, Health
jobs.excerpt: At Forbes Advisor, our mission is to help readers turn their aspirations into reality.
jobs.description:
At Forbes Advisor, our mission is to help readers turn their aspirations into reality. We arm people with trusted advice and guidance so they can make informed decisions they feel confident in and get back to doing the things they care about most.

We are an experienced team of industry experts dedicated to helping readers make smart decisions and choose the right products with ease. Forbes Advisor boasts decades of experience across dozens of geographies and teams, including Content, SEO, Business Intelligence, Finance, HR, Marketing, Production, Technology and Sales. The team brings rich industry knowledge to Forbes Advisor's global coverage of consumer credit, debt, health, home improvement, banking, investing, credit cards, small business, education, insurance, loans, real estate and travel.

We pair journalism with original research: every “best of” list we publish sits on a dataset our own team has collected, scored and can defend line by line.

The Data Research and Product Testing teams own that evidence base. We decide what gets measured, how it gets weighted, and whether a claim survives scrutiny. It is the difference between an opinion piece and a recommendation a reader can act on.

About the Role

We want to stop writing “the manufacturer claims”. This role is the person who actually opens it, uses it for six weeks and finds out.

You will run hands-on testing of physical products from your own home testing space. Products arrive, you test them against a written protocol, you log what happened, and your scores go straight into the rankings readers see. For Health categories you will also run the lab pipeline, sending samples out for third-party analysis and bringing the results back in. This is a role for someone already deep in the health space, not someone who intends to learn it on the way.

We expect you to use AI in your day-to-day work to increase your output without compromising testing rigour. You should understand which AI techniques suit each task, put them into practice and demonstrate how they help you deliver more or work faster. Knowing what AI could do is not enough: using it effectively and checking the results is part of the role.

What you'll do

  • Run hands-on tests to a written protocol and record the results in a structured, comparable form. The output is a dataset, not an opinion.
  • Help design those protocols: decide what to measure, how to measure it repeatably, and what would make a result invalid.
  • Own the sample pipeline for your categories: sourcing, receipt, logging, retention, return and disposal.
  • Document testing as you go, including photography and video, so the editorial team can show readers the work rather than assert it.
  • Feed test scores into the Data Research scoring models, and flag loudly when a hands-on result contradicts what the spec sheet claims.
  • Re-test on a defined cadence so published verdicts do not quietly go stale as products and plans change.
  • Write findings up clearly enough for an editor to build an article on, and stand behind them as the person who ran the test.
  • Keep the testing log auditable: who tested what, when, on which version or plan tier, under what conditions.
  • Run the lab pipeline for Health categories to the Lead's protocols: source retail units, submit them blind with lot numbers and chain-of-custody records, chase turnaround, and log every certificate of analysis against the product it came from.
  • Arrange accuracy validation of health devices against reference instruments, in-house where we can and through a lab where we cannot.
  • Reconcile lab results against label claims and flag every discrepancy. That gap is often the story.
  • Write the first protocol for a category we have not tested before, and be honest in the retro about which parts of it did not survive contact with the products.
  • Build AI into your daily testing and reporting workflow. Identify, trial and refine techniques such as reusable prompts for protocol drafts, structured extraction of test notes, AI-assisted data checks and drafting findings from verified results. Choose the right technique for the task, demonstrate it in routine work and show the improvement in output or turnaround alongside your quality checks. AI must support hands-on testing, never replace it or invent evidence.

Your categories

Some examples rather than the full list. This set evolves constantly, and a good deal of what you test next year is not on this page yet.

  • Supplements and nutrition: peptides, collagen, protein powders, vitamins and the rest, assessed by third-party lab assay for label-claim potency and contaminants rather than on effect.
  • Medical alert systems: response times, fall detection, range, battery life, monitoring centre handling and the cancellation experience.
  • Hearing aids: fit, controls, app quality, battery and charging, and accuracy against reference instruments.
  • Long-run durability testing across all of the above, where a verdict needs weeks rather than an afternoon.

About you

  • Health-obsessed, and we mean that literally. You follow this sector for your own reasons rather than because a job asked you to. You have views on peptides, collagen and protein powders, you already know which claims are plausible and which are marketing, and you can hold a conversation with someone deep in the space without needing anything explained. We would far rather hire the person who reads the studies for fun than the person who will learn to.
  • A genuine user of these products. Testing something you have never had a reason to buy produces a worse review, every time.
  • Fluent in the vocabulary: bioavailability, clinical dosing, proprietary blends, third-party tested, NSF and Informed Sport certification. You should know what each of those means, which of them actually matter to a reader, and which are rigour-flavoured marketing.
  • 5+ years in hands-on testing, QA, product review, lab work, technician work or a comparable role where you were accountable for a measurable result.
  • Able to read complex lab results and interrogate them rather than accept them. The question is never only whether the data is correct, it is whether it answers what we set out to ask. If we assay collagen powders and the report does not say how much collagen is in them, it is worthless to an editor, and you should be the person who catches that before the samples go out.
  • A home with space suitable for testing and storing products, including some large items. We will fund the setup, and we will discuss the practicalities honestly at interview rather than after you accept.
  • An instinct for controlling variables in a home rather than a lab: same room, same time of day, same power source, logged conditions.
  • Methodical with paperwork and logistics. The lab side of this role is lot numbers, submission forms, chain-of-custody records and turnaround chasing, and an unlogged sample is a wasted one.
  • Comfort with basic instrumentation such as sound meters, power meters, thermal probes, timers and scales. You do not need to own them; you do need to be willing to use them properly.
  • Practical hands: you can assemble, calibrate and maintain equipment without waiting for someone else.
  • Appetite for the unfamiliar. You will sometimes be working out the method as well as running it.
  • Photography good enough to publish, or the willingness to get there quickly.
  • Rigorous by instinct. You control variables without being told to, and you notice when a result is too good to be true.
  • Confident in Excel: you will be building and filling structured scoring sheets every week.
  • You can write. Findings that nobody can read do not help an editor.
  • Genuinely detail-obsessed: you investigate the outlier before you publish it, not after a reader emails in.
  • Comfortable saying a product is bad, in writing, with evidence, when the commercial wind is blowing the other way.
  • Practical experience using AI to increase your output, not just an interest in its potential. You understand which techniques suit different tasks, can explain their limitations and can demonstrate how you use them in your day-to-day work. Bring concrete examples: the task, the technique, the improvement in output or turnaround, and how you verified accuracy and protected confidential information. You also know when the work needs your own judgement rather than AI.

Nice to have

  • Prior work in a testing lab, QA function, consumer reviews outlet or product team.
  • Comfort with measurement instrumentation: sound meters, power meters, thermal probes, timers.
  • Photography or video skills good enough that the images are publishable.
  • SQL, or the willingness to learn it. Your scores end up in the same models the analysts use.
  • Experience preparing or submitting samples to an external lab, in any sector.
  • A nutrition, sports science, physiology or related qualification, formal or self-taught.
  • A personal track record in the space: a blog, a newsletter, a podcast, a forum reputation, anything that shows you were doing this before anyone paid you to.
  • Audiology, assistive technology or medical device exposure.

Job Description:

Senior Designer

ProviderSoft

THE COMPANY

ProviderSoft has spent two decades building software for early childhood developmental therapy agencies, a stable and specialized niche where our customers serve children and families who depend on quality care. We are profitable and capital-efficient, with a loyal customer base and a 20-plus-year operating track record. Our mission is to empower Early Childhood Development providers with the software, service, and expertise they need to achieve operational excellence, so they can deliver the highest quality care to children and families in their communities.

POSITION

ProviderSoft builds the solution agencies use to run early intervention, preschool special education, and applied behavior analysis (ABA) programs: therapy and support for young children with developmental delays and their families. Clinicians and administrators are in our product for most of their working day. What we build decides how much of their day goes to that work and how much goes to paperwork.


Product management and design are both new functions here. This role combines them: a senior designer with product management depth who moves between discovery, product definition and design as the work requires. The current product is organized around the data it stores. The work ahead is organizing it around what our users actually do, and deciding what we build first.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Product discovery, customer research, competitive research, and the case for what we build.
  • Sequence which modules and features come first, and what we decline.
  • Product definition and a backlog engineering can build from, prioritized against client value, delivery cost and dependency order.
  • Our customer development partner program, where several customers help shape each module as it is designed.
  • Rollout and migration for existing customers, with our implementation and Client Services teams.
  • Workflow research with real users; observing how the work gets done, not only asking about it.
  • Interaction design for dense, high-volume professional workflows.
  • The design system, and the product's UI and UX standards as the surface area grows.
  • Partnership with engineering from discovery through release.
  • Use AI-directed workflows to move from discovery to definition and design, and help shape how we do that across the team.

JOB QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience designing professional or enterprise software that people use all day, every day.
  • Experience taking B2B or vertical SaaS products from discovery through release.
  • Experience with workflow management solutions is highly desirable: case management, scheduling, billing or compliance reporting.
  • Strength in interaction and information design; visual craft matters, and it is not the center of this role.
  • Skill at deciding what not to build, and at holding that decision.
  • Comfort working directly with customers and translating what you learn into a roadmap and designs engineering can act on.
  • A method for learning an unfamiliar domain quickly.
  • Hands-on use of AI in discovery, specification and prototyping.
  • Early Intervention expertise is not required; deep domain expertise is in house.

ProviderSoft

Job Responsibilities

Job Summary


This position is responsible for leading projects across multiple studies or programs. A Senior Biostatistician acts as the primary contact with the sponsor for all biostatistics related activities on assigned projects

Lead the planning and execution of clinical analytics for clinical studies on late clinical development, covering data transformation, statistical analysis, and delivery of high-quality outputs. Apply established and advanced statistical methods, including modern data science approaches, to design, analyze, and interpret clinical trial data. Translate complex results into clear, impactful insights that support decision-making and evidence generation across the development value chain.


Core Responsibilities

 Provides support across all assigned statistical tasks during the lifecycle of the project, from protocol to CSR.

 Prepares Statistical Analysis Plans (SAPs), including development of well-presented mock-up displays for tables, listings, and figures. Collaborate with the sponsor, if required.

 May be responsible for the statistical aspects of the protocol, generation of randomization schedule, publications and input to the clinical study report.

 Coordinates the activities of other biostatistics and statistical programming personnel on assigned projects to ensure timely completion of high quality work. Provides independent review of project work produced by other biostatisticians in the department.

 Createsor reviews programming specifications for analysis datasets, tables, listings, and figures.

 ReviewsSAS annotated case report forms (CRFs), database design, and other study documentation to ensure protocol criteria are met and all data is captured as required to support a high quality database and the planned analysis.

 Conductsand participates in verification and quality control of project deliverables, ensuring that output meets expectations and is consistent with analysis described in SAP and specifications.

 Implements company objectives, and create alternative solutions to address business and operational challenges.

 Serves as biostatistics representative on project teams, interfacing as necessary with other departmental project team representatives. This would include preparing in advance for internal meetings, contributing ideas, and demonstrating respect for opinions of others.

 Managesscheduling and time constraints across multiple projects, sets goals based on priorities from management, adapts to timeline or priority changes by reorganizing daily workload, and proactively communicates to biostatistics management any difficulties with meeting these timelines.

 Monitors progress on study activities against agreed upon milestones and ensures the study timelines for project deliverables are met. Identifies out of scope tasks and escalate to management.

 Provides statistical programming support as needed.

 May participate in Data Safety Monitoring Board and/or Data Monitoring Committee activities, including charter development and serving as an independent non-voting biostatistician.

 May lead projects involving integrated analyses, attend regulatory agency meetings or respond to questions, as needed, to support the statistical analysis results of clinical trials on behalf of the sponsor.

 Follows applicable SOPs, WIs, and relevant regulatory guidelines (e.g. ICH).

 Maintains well organized, complete, and up-to-date project documentation, and verification/quality control documents and programs; ensuring inspection readiness.

 Displays willingness to work with others and assists with projects and initiatives as necessary to meet the needs of the business.

 Supports business development activities by contributing to proposals, budgets, and attending sponsor bid defense meetings.

 Coaches and mentors other Biostatistics staff.

 Performs other work-related duties as assigned.

 Minimal travel may be required.

• Degree in Statistics, Mathematics or related field (BSc/MSc/PhD).

• Extensive experience in clinical trials or an equivalent combination of

education and experience, demonstrated by the ability to lead multiple

projects and programs of studies.

5+ years of relevant experience as a Biostatistician

• Strong knowledge of statistical methods, clinical trial design, and pharmaceutical development
• Experience with statistical software/tools (e.g., SAS, R)
• Ability to identify and solve issues and collaborate with internal and external stakeholders (e.g., CROs, experts)

We are looking for someone who can help keep those moving parts organized, connected, and running smoothly.

The role

We are seeking a proactive, highly organized, and analytical Operations Analyst – Workflow & People Operations to support the effective delivery of our client engagements and internal operations.

This role sits at the intersection of workflow management, team coordination, people operations, and process improvement. You will help maintain visibility into work across multiple client portfolios, monitor deadlines and commitments, identify operational bottlenecks, and coordinate follow-through on outstanding actions.

You will also support employee onboarding, performance management processes, learning and development activities, and other people-related initiatives.

This is not simply a task-tracking or administrative support role. We are looking for someone who can recognize when something is not working, ask the right questions, coordinate the appropriate response, and follow through until the issue is resolved. You will work closely with Client Leads and leadership to ensure the team has the structure, information, and support needed to deliver consistently.

Key Responsibilities

1. Workflow Management & Client Delivery Coordination

  • Monitor workflows, deadlines, and deliverables across multiple client portfolios.
  • Coordinate daily workflow and communication triage to ensure incoming requests are appropriately assigned and acknowledged.
  • Track outstanding commitments and follow up with responsible team members to support timely completion.
  • Identify overdue tasks, stalled workflows, competing priorities, and potential delivery risks.
  • Work with Client Leads to understand operational bottlenecks and coordinate corrective actions.
  • Maintain visibility into upcoming deadlines and ensure potential issues are escalated early.
  • Support consistent use of workflow management systems and established operating procedures.

2. Operational Reporting & Performance Visibility

  • Prepare weekly operational reports highlighting workflow exceptions, delivery risks, team capacity concerns, and outstanding actions.
  • Identify recurring patterns in missed deadlines, delayed responses, or incomplete workflows.
  • Track operational performance indicators and support improvements in team productivity and service delivery.
  • Provide leadership with concise, actionable updates rather than simply reporting completed activities.
  • Maintain action trackers and follow through on agreed improvement initiatives.

3. People Operations & Employee Development

  • Coordinate employee onboarding and offboarding activities, including documentation, schedules, and collaboration with IT and relevant team members.
  • Maintain employee records, onboarding checklists, and people operations trackers.
  • Coordinate performance review schedules, probation evaluations, and development plan follow-ups.
  • Support the planning and administration of internal learning and development activities.
  • Monitor completion of assigned training and development actions.
  • Help ensure people-related processes are completed accurately, consistently, and on schedule.

4. Process Improvement & Operational Excellence

  • Identify inefficiencies, recurring workflow issues, and opportunities to simplify internal processes.
  • Document and maintain standard operating procedures, workflows, and internal process guidelines.
  • Recommend practical improvements to team coordination, task management, and operational reporting.
  • Support the implementation of approved process changes and monitor their effectiveness.
  • Collaborate with team members to improve the consistency and reliability of internal operations.

5. Communication & Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Serve as a coordination point between Client Leads, team members, and leadership on operational matters.
  • Communicate clearly and professionally regarding deadlines, outstanding actions, and operational priorities.
  • Escalate significant risks promptly, providing relevant context, actions already taken, and recommended next steps.
  • Coordinate meetings, operational reviews, and follow-up actions where required.
  • Promote a culture of proactive communication, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications & Experience

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, Accounting, Finance, or a related discipline.
  • 2–4 years of relevant experience in operations coordination, project coordination, workflow management, or business operations.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, track commitments, and follow through on outstanding actions.
  • Experience using workflow, project management, or task management systems.
  • Strong Microsoft Excel and Microsoft 365 skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and escalate issues appropriately.
  • Comfortable working in a remote, deadline-driven, and collaborative environment.

Preferred

  • Experience supporting a professional services, accounting, finance, or consulting organization.
  • Familiarity with workflow management tools such as Karbon, Asana, Monday.com, or similar platforms.
  • Exposure to employee onboarding, performance management, or learning and development coordination.
  • Experience preparing operational reports, dashboards, or performance trackers.
  • Familiarity with process documentation and continuous improvement methodologies.

What Success Looks Like
Success in this role means:

  • Client delivery workflows are monitored consistently, with potential delays identified before deadlines are missed.
  • Outstanding actions are followed through, with clear ownership and visibility.
  • Client Leads receive timely information about workflow bottlenecks, capacity concerns, and operational risks.
  • Leadership receives concise operational reporting that highlights what requires attention and what is being done about it.
  • Onboarding, performance reviews, and employee development activities are coordinated on schedule.
  • Recurring operational problems are identified, addressed, and progressively reduced.
  • Team members experience clearer processes, better coordination, and fewer avoidable surprises.

What We Offer

  • Exposure to the operations of a growing strategic accounting and finance advisory firm.
  • Opportunities to work closely with experienced finance professionals and business leadership.
  • Hands-on experience in workflow management, people operations, and operational improvement.
  • Structured learning, mentorship, and professional development.
  • A collaborative, remote-first work environment.
  • Opportunities for career growth into operations management and broader business leadership roles.

Who Will Thrive at Fiscal 12?
You'll enjoy this role if you:

  • Naturally notice when something is falling through the cracks.
  • Enjoy bringing structure and clarity to complex situations.
  • Are comfortable following up with colleagues and holding commitments visible.
  • Take initiative rather than waiting for instructions.
  • Think beyond whether a task has been updated to whether the underlying issue has been resolved.
  • Communicate challenges early and come prepared with possible solutions.
  • Enjoy supporting people while maintaining clear expectations.
  • Take pride in making teams and processes work better.

At Fiscal 12, operational excellence isn't about keeping track of activities. It's about helping the right work get done, by the right people, at the right time.

POSITION SUMMARY


The Senior Business Development & Key Account Manager - Americas is responsible for winning and growing medium to large, multi-site customers for Tec4med's real-time condition monitoring solutions across the United States (Americas).


The role is primarily focused on new business: building qualified pipeline, leading consultative, multi-stakeholder sales cycles and closing. Once won, the role-holder owns these accounts long term, expanding usage across sites, lanes and products, while continuing to develop new business pipeline.


The position will be responsible for growing our US territory for Tec4med. About Direct Meds

At Direct Meds, we prioritize care, trust, and solutions that focus on the individual. Headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, we are a fast-growing national team passionate about transforming the way people access the care they need. If you're driven by purpose and excited by growth, Direct Meds is the place to be.

Telesales Representative – Full-Time W-2 | Remote - Weekends

Compensation: $41,600 Annual Base Salary + Uncapped Commission

Estimated Weekly Earnings: $2,000–$2,500 | Target: Approximately $2,300 Per Week (Base + Commission)

Full-Time • W-2 Employee • Remote • 40 Hours/Week

Note: The estimated weekly earnings range represents a performance-based earning opportunity and is not guaranteed. Actual earnings will vary based on individual sales performance and commissions earned.

MandatoryTrainingAttendance

Due to the accelerated nature of this training program and the limited training timeline, attendance at all scheduled training sessions is mandatory. Candidates who miss any required training session may be disqualified from continuing in the hiring and onboarding process. Schedule

Friday–Monday — Four 10-hour shifts (40 hours per week)

Employees will work four 10-hour shifts per week. Shift assignments will depend on team availability and business needs.

Note: The base salary listed above represents a good-faith estimate of the minimum and maximum target for this position. Actual compensation offered may vary depending on the candidate's geographic location, job-related skills, experience, and education.

Top Performers Wanted

If you're the kind of salesperson who thrives on goals, loves the sound of a successful close, and consistently finds a way to hit — and beat — your numbers, we want to hear from you.

Direct Meds is looking for a high-performing, competitive, and coachable Telesales Representative to join our rapidly growing team. This is a full-time W-2 sales position with a guaranteed base salary, uncapped commission, benefits, paid time off, and opportunities for career advancement.

Our target earnings for this position are approximately $2,300 per week, with estimated weekly earning potential ranging from $2,000–$2,500 through combined base salary and commission.Actual earnings will depend on individual sales performance.

This isn't a role for someone who simply wants to answer calls. It's an opportunity for a proven sales professional to take ownership of a pipeline, build trust with prospective customers, close business, and earn more through exceptional performance.

If you're motivated by results, comfortable with high-volume sales conversations, and hungry to grow your income, we want to meet you.

About Direct Meds

At Direct Meds, we believe accessing medication should be simpler, more convenient, and centered around the individual.

Headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, we're a fast-growing national company on a mission to transform how people access the care they need. Our sales team plays a critical role in that mission — combining exceptional customer experiences with exceptional sales performance.

We're building a team of people who want to win, grow, and make an impact.

What You'll Do

As a Telesales Representative, you'll own the sales process from the first conversation through the close.

  • Make high-volume outbound calls to prospective customers and qualified leads to generate sales opportunities.
  • Proactively engage prospective customers through phone, email, and other channels.
  • Respond quickly and professionally to inbound leads and maximize every sales opportunity.
  • Conduct discovery conversations to understand customer needs and recommend the right solutions.
  • Build trust and create a strong customer experience while confidently asking for the sale.
  • Consistently achieve or exceed weekly, monthly, and quarterly sales goals.
  • Manage a high-volume pipeline and maintain disciplined follow-up.
  • Overcome objections and turn challenging conversations into opportunities.
  • Accurately document customer interactions, sales activity, and pipeline updates in the CRM.
  • Partner with Customer Success, Operations, and Clinical teams to ensure a seamless customer experience.
  • Continuously develop your product knowledge, sales skills, and industry expertise.
  • Take coaching seriously and apply feedback quickly to improve performance.

What Success Looks Like

We measure performance by results.

Top performers in this role:

  • Consistently hit or exceed their sales targets.
  • Move quickly and decisively on qualified opportunities.
  • Follow up relentlessly without sacrificing professionalism.
  • Take ownership of their pipeline and results.
  • Know how to build rapport while maintaining control of a sales conversation.
  • Are comfortable asking for the sale.
  • Learn from both wins and losses.
  • Respond to coaching with action, not excuses.
  • Compete with themselves and their teammates to get better every day.

If you're looking for a comfortable role where you can simply meet the minimum expectations, this probably isn't the position for you. If you're looking for a full-time career opportunity where exceptional performance is rewarded, keep reading.

Our Culture & Expectations

At Direct Meds, we hold ourselves to a high standard — both in what we accomplish and how we accomplish it.

Integrity First

We win as a team.

Protecting customer relationships and respecting lead ownership is non-negotiable. Poaching, interfering with, or taking ownership of another team member's leads, customers, or sales is strictly against our values and will not be tolerated.

We believe the best teams compete hard without competing against each other.

Coachability

The best salespeople never stop improving.

You should be comfortable receiving direct feedback, asking questions, studying what works, and immediately applying coaching to your calls and performance. We invest in people who are serious about becoming better sales professionals.

Ownership

Your results are your responsibility.

We expect our sales representatives to take ownership of their activity, pipeline, follow-up, performance, and development. We don't make excuses — we identify what's not working and fix it.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for proven sales performers, not just people who have held a sales title.

Required

  • 3–5+ years of inside sales, telesales, telemarketing, or customer-facing sales experience.
  • Demonstrated history of consistently meeting or exceeding sales goals.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Exceptional phone presence and active listening skills.
  • Ability to confidently handle objections and close sales.
  • Comfortable making a high volume of outbound calls while maintaining quality conversations.
  • Highly self-motivated with a competitive, results-driven mindset.
  • Strong follow-up and time-management skills.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment.
  • Availability to work 40 hours per week, Friday–Monday, consisting of four 10-hour shifts.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
  • Proficiency with CRM platforms such as Salesforce, HubSpot, or similar.

Preferred

  • Healthcare, pharmacy, telehealth, or related industry experience.
  • Experience in a high-volume inbound/outbound sales environment.
  • History of exceeding quota rather than simply meeting it.
  • Experience selling products or services that require consultative selling.

We care more about what you've accomplished than what your previous job title said. If you've consistently been one of the top performers on your sales team, we want to know about it.

Compensation & Benefits

Full-Time W-2 Employment

This is a full-time W-2 employee position — not a 1099 contractor opportunity.

Compensation:

  • $41,600 annual base salary.
  • Uncapped commission on sales.
  • Estimated total weekly earnings: $2,000–$2,500 (base salary + commission).
  • Target weekly earnings: approximately $2,300, based on sales performance.
  • Both base salary and earned commissions paid weekly.
  • Performance-driven earning potential with no commission cap.

The estimated weekly earnings range represents a performance-based earning opportunity and is not guaranteed. Actual earnings will vary based on individual sales performance and commissions earned.

Benefits:

  • Health, Dental, and Vision benefits.
  • Paid time off.
  • Company holidays.
  • Fully remote work.
  • Career advancement opportunities within a rapidly scaling company.
  • Mission-driven culture focused on impact, integrity, and teamwork.

Full-Time Remote Work Requirements

This is a full-time, 40-hour-per-week W-2 position.

Candidates must be available to work the required Friday–Monday schedule, consisting of four 10-hour shifts.

Candidates must also have the following available prior to their start date:

  • Reliable personal laptop or desktop computer.
  • Quality headset suitable for high-volume sales calls.
  • High-speed, reliable internet connection.
  • Quiet, professional workspace suitable for customer conversations.

Schedule Requirement

To be considered for this position, candidates must confirm that they:

  • Are available to work 40 hours per week.
  • Are available to work Friday through Monday.
  • Can consistently work four 10-hour shifts per week.
  • Understand that shift assignment depends on team availability and business needs.
  • Can consistently maintain their assigned Friday–Monday schedule.

How to Apply

If you're a proven sales professional who wants a full-time W-2 career opportunity, wants to compete, and wants to be rewarded for exceptional performance, we'd like to meet you.

No algorithm can replicate a native Japanese speakers' understanding of how information is verified, contextualized, and communicated within Japan's cultural, linguistic, and professional landscape. When you evaluate it well, millions of users get reliable, relevant results.

In this role, you will research and evaluate machine-generated responses for accuracy and quality. You will help improve the overall experience for millions of users around the world, including yourself.

  • Research and evaluate machine-generated responses for accuracy and quality

  • Provide insightful evaluations across a wide range of domains

  • Apply consistent judgment to meet established quality standards

  • Deliver structured feedback to support the development of AI technologies

Qualifications to succeed in this project:

  • Native Japanese (Japan) speaker with a keen interest in linguistics and proficient level of English

  • Must have resided in Japan for a minimum of 1 year

  • Familiarity with current and historical business, media, sports, news, social media, and cultural affairs

  • Demonstrated research capability through professional background or strong track record of self-directed research and information verification

  • Subject matter expertise in one or more of the following domains: Popular Culture (Beauty, Fitness, Pop Music, Entertainment, Sports, Current Events, Travel), Social Sciences (Fine Arts, History, Anthropology, Political Science, Sociology, Education), STEM (Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Statistics), or Professional Services (Medicine, Law, Accounting, Engineering, Software Development)

  • Excellent attention to detail, strong time management, and the ability to work independently

  • Must own and actively use a Gmail account

  • Experience using web browsers to navigate and interact with a variety of online content

  • Daily access to a reliable broadband internet connection and a personal computer

  • Professional writing experience such as copywriting, journalism, technical writing, or editing (preferred)

  • High level of creativity and logical thinking with the ability to identify user needs (preferred)

Why join the project:

  • Flexible, self-directed schedule: Structure your contributions around existing professional, research, or personal commitments with no fixed shifts and no minimum weekly hours

  • Structured onboarding from day one: You will complete a self-led onboarding program covering research best practices and client guidelines before your first live task

  • Clear performance feedback: Evaluations are designed to help you understand your strengths and maintain quality calibration throughout the project

  • Intellectually demanding by design: If you are driven by accuracy, source verification, and the challenge of evaluating whether AI truly understands Japan, this work is built for that mindset

  • Expert-aligned compensation: Rates reflect the domain knowledge and analytical rigor this work requires

Qualification path

How to get started:

  1. Complete the Japanese (Japan) and English language assessments

  2. Complete ID verification (IDV)

  3. Pass an open-book qualification exam

  4. Complete a structured, self-led onboarding program covering research best practices and client guidelines

Compensation: Approximately 2,890 JPY per hour. Payment is based on completed, approved tasks.

Service Rates

Compensation is based on tasks completed and project availability. Estimated earnings may vary depending on task volume and program requirements including, quality, and productivity, in accordance with the program's quality standards and guidelines.

Independent Contractor Relationship

This opportunity is offered on an independent contractor basis. Contributors have the flexibility to choose when and how much they work, subject to project availability and quality requirements. This opportunity is not and should not be construed as creating an employment relationship with TELUS Digital.

Job Description & Summary

Our clients depend on expert advice when navigating tax and succession, that’s where your leadership matters most. Your expertise will help shape confident futures for privately owned businesses and families, navigating complex tax and succession challenges. As a Director, you’ll play a vital role in providing tailored tax advisory and planning services that support clients throughout their business lifecycle. You’ll be working with clients across private businesses, family offices, entrepreneurs, and start-ups.

Why PwC?

At PwC Australia, your skills meet purpose. We tackle big challenges across industries like finance, technology, energy, and health, giving you the chance to make a real impact. Here, your growth is our priority. You’ll work with leading teams, explore new technologies, and unlock your full potential.

Join a global community of more than 370,000 people who value bold ideas, collaboration, and lasting change. Together, we’re building trust and shaping the future.

That philosophy is brought to life in our Family Office Tax practice. Long‑term advice. Complex family groups. Decisions that span generations.

Family Office tax is not about volume‑driven work or short‑term engagements. It’s about trusted enduring relationships with families who own and control significant private wealth and businesses, and guiding them through complexity, change, and generational transition.

As a Director in PwC’s Family Office Tax team, you’ll be a senior adviser to some of Australia’s most sophisticated private families. You’ll lead complex engagements, shape long‑term client strategy, and work closely with Partners to grow PwC’s Family Office capability and market presence.

This is tax leadership with context, continuity, and consequences.


What Family Office Tax Actually Looks Like

You’ll operate at the highest level of complex private groups, advising across:

  • Highly complex private group and trust tax matters, including large multi‑trust and multi‑entity structures, with a focus on technical risk, governance and long‑term sustainability
  • Advanced trust taxation and distribution strategies, including:
  • Income and capital streaming at scale
  • Section 100A risk assessment and mitigation
  • Trustee powers, present entitlement issues and trust integrity considerations
  • Family‑owned business and investment group structuring, advising on:
  • Whole‑of‑group structuring across operating, holding and investment entities
  • Division 7A strategy, remediation and governance frameworks
  • Managing private group integrity and ATO focus areas
  • Capital gains tax and transaction leadership, including:
  • Business sales, succession‑driven exits and partial divestments
  • Small business CGT concessions
  • Complex restructures, rollovers and group reorganisations (including Divisions 615, 122‑A and 124‑M)
  • Intergenerational wealth, succession and governance planning, working closely with legal, private advisory and family governance specialists on:
  • Ownership and control transitions
  • Family governance frameworks and decision‑making structures
  • Balancing tax outcomes, risk management and family dynamics
  • ATO engagement and tax governance leadership, including:
  • Leading ATO audits, reviews and risk reviews
  • Managing private ruling strategies and high‑level technical submissions
  • Advising families navigating heightened regulatory, reputational and public scrutiny

What Makes Family Office Work Different

  • The relationships are generational: You advise families over decades, not transactions.
  • Judgement and leadership matter: Deep technical expertise must be paired with commercial insight and emotional intelligence.
  • The structures are deeply interconnected: Trusts, companies, investments, and operating businesses function as a single ecosystem.
  • The impact is lasting: Your advice influences legacy, stewardship, and long‑term wealth outcomes.

This is where tax leadership becomes true trusted advisory.

Your Role as a Director

  • As a Director in the Family Office Tax team, you will:
  • Lead and oversee PwC’s most significant and complex Family Office client relationships
  • Act as a senior trusted adviser to family principals, boards and key decision‑makers
  • Set long‑term tax, structuring and governance strategy for private family groups
  • Provide technical leadership on the most complex and high‑risk tax matters
  • Lead major structuring, succession and transaction engagements in partnership with PwC Partners
  • Own and direct ATO engagement strategies, including audits, reviews and negotiations
  • Review and approve high‑judgement technical advice and client deliverables
  • Develop and mentor Senior Managers and future leaders within the practice
  • Contribute to market profile, thought leadership and growth of PwC’s Family Office offering
  • Support Partner group initiatives and play an active role in shaping the future direction of PwC Private

What We Are Looking For

  • Extensive experience in family office private tax, business or corporate tax at a senior leadership level
  • Deep expertise advising complex private groups, trusts and family‑owned businesses
  • Proven ability to lead large, high‑risk engagements and senior client relationships
  • Strong technical authority across trust taxation, CGT, Division 7A and private group integrity
  • A strategic, commercial mindset with the ability to navigate family, governance and reputational considerations
  • A passion for leadership, mentoring and building a market‑leading Family Office practice

What you’ll gain:

  • Leadership development programs and executive coaching designed to help you inspire teams and accelerate your career growth.
  • A culture valuing diverse perspectives, empowering leaders to drive innovation and collaboration, learn more about our commitment to Inclusion and Diversity and First Nations Prosperity
  • A world-class parental leave policy offering up to 26 weeks of leave for caregivers, supporting your family and personal life.
  • Flexibility means trusting you to choose when, where, and how you work, balancing what’s best for you, your team, and your clients to grow and thrive together.
  • Being part of a community united by purpose, delivering impact that reaches clients, communities, and the future you’re shaping.

jobs.excerpt: Advanced Associate, Test Center Support The Advanced Associate, Test Center Support - Channel Care provides non-technical support to Pearson VUE third-party test centers in the Americas.
jobs.description:
Advanced Associate, Test Center Support

The Advanced Associate, Test Center Support - Channel Care provides non-technical support to Pearson VUE third-party test centers in the Americas. Your goal is to help test centers deliver a secure, consistent, high-quality exam experience for our clients’ candidates.

Are you a relationship builder who enjoys solving problems and helping people succeed? In this role, you'll support Pearson VUE test centers across North, Central and South America. You'll be their trusted point of contact for guidance, training and day-to-day support. You’ll do this by engaging proactively with test centers, building strong working relationships, monitoring operations and compliance, supporting training, and managing cases from start to finish.

You'll work with internal teams, including Program Coordinators, Sales and Regional Managers, to help test centers run smoothly, meet quality standards and deliver an excellent experience to candidates. This is not a technical support role. Its focus is customer service, quality and building strong partnerships.

What You'll Do

  • Build relationships with test centers: Call test centers regularly to check in, offer support, provide training and discuss opportunities to add capacity.
  • Onboard new test centers: Guide new test centers from approval to launch. Help them complete setup steps, training and readiness requirements so they can start delivering exams with confidence.
  • Support quality and compliance: Help test centers understand and follow Pearson VUE policies and exam requirements. When an issue comes up, document it, follow up and arrange retraining if needed.
  • Manage cases from start to finish: Answer incoming calls and emails, investigate questions and resolve issues quickly and professionally.
  • Review new site applications: Work with other teams to review applications from organizations that want to become test centers, and give clear feedback.
  • Meet service goals: Keep accurate records and meet response-time, quality and productivity targets.

You will support test centers that are run by independent partners, such as schools, colleges, training providers and other businesses. You'll build strong working relationships with these partners and serve as their trusted guide during setup.

Key Responsibilities

Test Center Operations and Engagement

  • Make regular outbound calls to Pearson VUE Test Centers to:

    • Build and maintain relationships

    • Provide support and training as needed

    • Request added testing capacity or expansion when needed

  • Maintain an up-to-date knowledge of test center policies, procedures, and exam sponsor requirements.

  • Work with other departments on new site applications – review applications and provide guidance and feedback.

  • Follow up with test centers on reported quality issues, create case reports, and assign retraining where needed.

  • Meet departmental key performance indicators (KPIs) and service standards.

Case Management

  • Answer incoming calls during scheduled department hours.

  • Respond to inquiries from test centers by phone, case, and email in a timely, professional, and accurate way.

  • Monitor shared mailboxes, voicemails, and unassigned case queues, and respond or reassign as appropriate.

  • Make sure every test center issue brought to the team has a case that is created, correctly assigned, prioritized, and kept up to date.

  • Follow assigned cases through to resolution, with complete and accurate notes on issues, escalations, decisions, and outcomes.

  • Use sound judgment to prioritize and reclassify cases and tasks so time-sensitive issues are handled first.

  • Document and follow up on complaints made against test centers.

  • Escalate security incidents and other critical issues promptly.

Audit and Compliance

  • Proactively monitor test center compliance with policy, procedure, and performance requirements.

  • Audit test center log sheets and other records to confirm operational compliance.

Test Center Onboarding

  • Help new Pearson VUE test centers get onboarded until they are ready to open their doors and deliver exams.

  • You'll be test center main point of contact through setup until activated. You'll register the test center in our systems, send welcome messages and track each onboarding step.

  • You'll guide the test center through receiving equipment, installing and testing our exam software, setting up its internal accounts and getting its staff certified to run exams.

  • Before the test center goes live, you'll confirm that everything is ready and then hand it over for final test center activation. After launch, you'll send the test center the information it needs to start testing candidates and continue to support them.

Qualifications and Experience

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree.

  • 3–5 years of experience in a customer-facing role such as customer service, operations, quality, or compliance.

  • Excellent written and spoken English, including confident phone communication with international customers.

  • Ability to build rapport with people at all levels, internally and externally.

  • Strong attention to detail, with the ability to follow detailed procedures and keep documentation and data accurate.

  • Ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks and projects in a structured way in a fast-paced environment.

  • Self-starter who takes ownership of their work and performs well both independently and as part of a team.

  • Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and web-based tools.

  • Willingness to ask thoughtful questions and research internal process documents and resources to find answers.

  • Ability to work overnight shifts consistently to match Americas business hours.

Preferred

  • Experience supporting customers or business partners in North or Latin America.

  • Experience with case management or CRM systems.

  • Familiarity with audit, quality assurance, or compliance monitoring.

  • Spanish or Portuguese language skills.

Core Competencies

  • Customer focus: Puts the test center and candidate experience first.

  • Effective communication: Communicates clearly and professionally in writing and by phone.

  • Collaboration: Works well across teams, functions, and time zones.

  • Quality mindset: Committed to continuously improving the quality of service.

jobs.description:
POSITION:Program/Operations Analyst II

TEAM:Compliance Services

SUPERVISOR:Compliance Services Manager or Director

LOCATION:Remote, with domestic travel <25%

STATUS:Exempt

SALARY RANGE:TBD[AO1][AO2]

SUMMARY:The position will be the Compliance Services department’s subject matter expert on the governing legal documents, as well as the Federal and local regulations they incorporate. The primary assignment is a compliance monitoring engagement, where the team monitors a residential property owner’s compliance with a federal Consent Decree (“CD”) covering the lead-based paint (“LBP”) inspection and abatement, substandard housing conditions, tenant relocation, rent abatement, and restitution. This is a hands-on generalist role. The position will interpret CD requirements, review compliance evidence, draft memos, test monitoring tools, and help launch special initiatives and programs.

The position will also support cross-department engagements and special projects as needed.

SUPERVISION RECEIVED AND EXERCISED: Operates under the direct general supervision of a Manager or Director.

ESSENTIAL DUITES AND RESPONSIBILITES:The below statements are intended to describe the general nature and scope of work being performed by this position. This is not a complete listing of all responsibilities, duties and/or skills required.

  • Consent Decree and Regulatory Expertise
    • Serve as the team’s expert on the CD, including its LBP, substandard conditions, relocation, rent abatement, restitution, and deliverable review provisions
    • Interpret how the CD interacts with incorporated related requirements including but not limited to:
      • EPA lead rules (40 C.F.R. Part 745, including abatement, clearance, and the RRP Rule)
      • HUD’s Lead Safe Housing Rule (24 C.F.R. Part 35) and related inspection standards
      • NYC Local Law 1 (Admin. Code §§ 27-2056.1–2056.18), the Housing Maintenance Code, Local Law 55 (indoor allergens), and NYC Health Code § 173
    • Answer internal questions with cited, written analysis, and flag where the CD is silent or ambiguous
    • Maintain the team’s reference library, FAQs, and requirement to citation crosswalks
    • Track regulatory changes and assess their impact on CD obligations
  • Compliance Monitoring and Review
    • Review submissions and deliverables against established requirements and regulations
    • Recommend whether to approve or disapprove submissions under the CD’s review process and track resubmission deadlines
    • Review special program claims for eligibility, condition severity, repair deadlines, start and end dates, and calculation accuracy
    • Request, track, and evaluate supporting documentation (e.g., tenant notices, EPA notifications, relocation records, contractor certifications, and approvals)
    • Draft Action Plans, corrective action follow-up, and report narratives
    • Support development of operational procedures
  • Memos and Other Written Work Product
    • Draft compliance memos, findings, deficiency notices, and correspondence to a variety of audiences
    • Contribute sections to periodic reports
    • Draft and redline program and operational policy language, reconciling competing drafts against established requirements and regulations
  • Monitoring framework and tools
    • Review and test compliance monitoring framework, checklists, trackers, and testing procedures for accuracy and completeness
    • Trace each monitoring step back to its established requirement or regulation, and close gaps
    • Test tools (e.g., Excel trackers, SharePoint lists and workflows, deadline calculations) with simple cases and document results
    • Recommend process improvements and help maintain document management and audit-trail standards
  • Program design and initiative support
    • Support the design and rollout of initiatives (e.g., rent abatement program), including eligibility rules, procedures, intake forms, notices, review workflows, and controls
    • Draft program guidance, FAQs and public-facing materials in plain language
    • Help refine reporting metrics and quality control checks for each program
  • Broader Compliance Services Support
    • Flex time to support cross-departmental engagements and special projects
    • Conduct compliance reviews, document and file testing, and data analysis for other monitoring, oversight, or regulatory engagements
    • Draft memos, reports, procedures, and deliverables for those engagements
    • Help build and maintain shared department tools, templates, trackers, and quality control procedures
    • Support scoping and onboarding for new compliance engagements, including research on applicable regulations
    • Share CD and housing regulation expertise with colleagues and support onboarding efforts of new team members

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in public policy, urban planning, public administration, law, environmental health, or a related field, or commensurate experience
  • 3-5 years of experience in compliance monitoring, regulatory analysis, program operations, audit or housing oversight
  • Demonstrated ability to read and apply legal documents (e.g., consent decrees, settlement agreements, regulations, contracts) and cite them accurately
  • Working knowledge of housing quality or lead-safety regulation (e.g., EPA, HUD, and/or NYC), and the ability to quickly learn other regulatory frameworks
  • Strong writing skills, with samples of memos, policy analysis, or compliance findings available upon request
  • Strong Excel skills (e.g., formulas, data validation, pivot tables) and comfort with large datasets
  • Experience with document review and evidence-based testing

About us

At Viasat, the work you do helps people stay connected in ways that matter, from everyday moments to critical missions across air, land, sea, and space.

We’re a place for people who are curious, bold, and motivated by meaningful work. Here, you'll have the opportunity to make an impact, explore new possibilities, and grow your career in ways that align with your interests and goals. When you're ready to take on something new, you'll find leaders who support your development and help you turn your ambition into action.


What you'll do

Viasat International Government (VIG) delivers secure space, cyber, and tactical network solutions to governments around the world working within the Viasat Government (VGOV) business. Within Viasat International Government (VIG) the Tactical Networks and high assurance Encryption team (TN&E) focus on Defence and Intelligence users and partners across governments right around the world.

We are seeking a highly motivated and results-oriented Tactical Networking Business Development Manager to drive growth from within the Tactical Networking portfolio across International Government accounts,, working in collaboration with our Regional Market Development team. This role is responsible for identifying, developing, and closing new business opportunities across EMEA and The Americas (excluding USA) within the Defence sector, with a focus on Viasat’s comprehensive portfolio of Tactical Networking products and services.

The scope includes systems supporting tactical crewed and uncrewed communications; Link 16 tactical gateways; narrowband SATCOM capabilities (UHF); terrestrial laser free-space optical communications; and tactical software-defined networking.

In addition, the role encompasses the delivery of integrated services that enable seamless connectivity, linking users to cloud-based mission data and applications, ensuring secure, resilient, and mission-critical communications.

You will be part of a team delivering mission critical capabilities to our partners and in a company that is leading the way with space and defence technology solutions.

  • Strategic Growth:Identify and capture new business opportunities for tactical networking products and services, such as the MOJO Next Tactical Gateway and Viasat’s NetAgility virtual Software Defined Networking (vSDN) platform .

Work in close collaboration with capture managers, proposal teams, and technical subject matter experts to develop compelling, compliant bids, white papers, and presentations that directly address defined military requirements and operational challenges.

  • Market Intelligence: Stay abreast of industry trends, competitor activities, new technologies, and changes in military doctrine, acquisition policies, and budget priorities. Provide regular market insights to senior leadership.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work as an integral part of the Viasat International Government team, particularly the Regional Market Development team and Operations, ensuring delivery of VIG’s ongoing & planned growth. Develop a strong relationship with other VIG and VGOV business areas, particularly the MC2 Business Area.
  • Representation: Represent the company at industry conferences, trade shows, and relevant military events to enhance brand awareness and generate

Objectives and Key Results (OKR’s)

  • Achieve Fiscal Targets: Capture and delivery of in year Awards and Revenue targets to support meeting the agreed in year budget for the TN&E pillar of the VIG business.
  • Pipeline Development:Research and identify International (5 EYES & NATO) programs of record to develop the tactical networking pipeline within EMEA and The Americas (exc. USA)
  • Long-term BD: Delivery of campaign plans for each large-scale capture program in your domain, successfully achieving campaign milestones within the year and maximising P-Win throughout the campaign cycle
  • Operational Excellence:Maintain accurate forecasts and CRM inputs to ensure business transparency.
  • MC2 Interlock: Act as a focal point for MC2 interlock to develop deep Subject Matter Expertise, including areas such as Export Control, ITAR, FMS, product capabilities, future roadmaps and the capturing of any specific International customer requirements.
  • Self-Development: Ensure personal and professional development is built into your objectives to align your skills to maximise market opportunity

What you'll need

  • 5+ years of progressive experience in business development, sales, or capture management within the International defence sector
  • Proven track record in business growth through building virtual teams that consistently win and deliver against multi-million-dollar revenue targets
  • Deep knowledge and experience of the tactical communications domain across technologies such as Link16 with demonstrable recent experience of relevant tactical networking communications programmes
  • Deep understanding of at least one of the 5 Eye Defence acquisition lifecycles, regulations, and government contracting vehicles
  • Knowledge of emerging technologies and their application to military challenges.
  • Bachelor’s degree in business management, Engineering, or equivalent.

  • Strong strategic thinking, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.

Collaborating closely with the Regional Senior Vice President/General Manager (SVP/GM) for the Americas Region and other commercial leaders, this role sets the vision and strategic direction for US market access and reimbursement and is accountable for translating that strategy into executable plans and measurable business results for payer and patient related marketing and account management teams.

In this capacity, the role advises commercial leadership on access-related portfolio, launch, pricing, reimbursement, and lifecycle decisions and ensures that US payer strategy is aligned with broader commercial and corporate objectives.

The incumbent is accountable for defining, building, and evolving the capabilities, structure, priorities, and resource allocation of the US Market Access & Reimbursement organization to support current and future portfolio needs.   • Leads budget and resource planning for the function and is accountable for performance against agreed access, reimbursement, and pricing objectives.
  • Manages, coaches and mentors direct reports.
  • Performs other tasks and assignments as needed and specified by management.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in related business or scientific discipline and a minimum of 10 years progressively responsible experience in commercial roles (marketing and/or sales) in a pharmaceutical, biotechnology or related environment and/or a minimum of 12 years of related professional experience in these same environments.

  • Demonstrated leadership experience across market access, reimbursement and related service models within the biopharmaceutical industry.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead, develop, coach, and mentor high-performing teams, including payer account management leaders and direct reports.

  • Strong executive presence with the ability to influence internal and external stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead through both direct and matrixed teams across a complex commercial organization.
  • Strategic and analytical mindset with the ability to anticipate market developments, solve complex problems, and adapt effectively to changing business priorities.

Special knowledge or skills and/or licenses or certificates preferred.

  • Minimum of 5 years of electrical power system analysis and design engineering experience in an industrial, utility, consulting, EPC, or similar environment.
  • Current Professional Engineer license in Electrical Engineering or ability to obtain PE registration within one year.
  • Ability to review confidential US security information.

Additional Qualifications:

  • Experience designing medium- and low-voltage electrical distribution systems, including power system modeling and analysis using ETAP, SKM PowerTools, or comparable software, preferred.
  • Experience with on-site power generation, including reciprocating engines, combustion turbines, solar PV, wind, battery energy storage systems, or other mixed-asset generation facilities, preferred.
  • Experience with microgrids, inverter-based resources, utility interconnections, and integrating generation resources with electrical networks, preferred.
  • Experience designing or managing the design of large-scale electrical power systems supporting data centers, Department of Defense facilities, or other mission-critical infrastructure, preferred.
  • Experience with PSCAD or other electromagnetic transient analysis software, preferred.
  • Experience with substations, SCADA systems, protective relays, metering, PLCs, VFDs, networking, industrial communications, SEL relays, or RTACs, preferred.
  • Experience preparing or reviewing equipment specifications, requests for proposal, technical bid evaluations, electrical equipment submittals, and engineer-of-record deliverables, preferred.
  • Experience with greenfield and brownfield electrical projects and familiarity with applicable NERC, NFPA, IEEE, ANSI, NEMA, and National Electrical Code requirements, preferred.
  • Experience with AutoCAD and Microsoft Office applications.
  • Strong written, verbal, and technical presentation skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with customers, engineers, vendors, contractors, and multidisciplinary project teams.

  • Ability to travel to project sites, customer meetings, vendor facilities, and commissioning activities as required.

In addition to base pay, employees receive a comprehensive benefits package, such as health insurance, retirement plans, and paid time off, and may be eligible for performance incentives, bonuses, commissions, or equity, depending on the role.

Actual pay will depend on factors such as internal equity, skills, experience, education, certifications, and location. This range supports our commitment to pay transparency and compliance with applicable laws. Compensation may vary by work location, including remote arrangements.

We disclose salary ranges and benefits in all required external and internal postings and will provide further details upon request at any stage of the hiring process. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Ameresco challenges the brightest, most talented, and creative individuals in the industry by providing an environment that fosters initiative and achievement. We are proud of our comprehensive and competitive employee benefits, including people-oriented insurance, investment, and incentive plans.

All official communications from Ameresco will originate from an @ameresco.com email address. Any correspondence from other domains should be regarded as fraudulent. jobs.title: Senior Data Product Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Who We Are: Power Digital is an AI-Native Growth Firm built at the intersection of world-class talent and proprietary technology.
locationRestrictions: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Power Digital is an AI-Native Growth Firm built at the intersection of world-class talent and proprietary technology. We help leading and emerging brands grow by combining deep vertical expertise, strategic thinking, and enterprise intelligence to drive measurable business outcomes.

For more than a decade, we have built our business around one belief: the best technology makes great people better. Our teams of strategists, creatives, analysts, and technologists use Omega, our AI operating system, to surface opportunities faster, investigate what is driving performance, and execute approved work with greater speed and precision. Behind Omega is Iris, our proprietary intelligence layer, built on years of real performance data, strategic frameworks, testing, and learnings from across our client portfolio. AI expands the capacity of our people to think, create, solve harder problems, and make better decisions. Human judgment, creativity, and accountability remain central to how we work.

As a people-first firm, we value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. We strongly believe our people and culture are key to our success. We partner closely with our clients as an extension of their teams, working across strategy, execution, and measurement to identify what is truly blocking growth and determine what to do next. Our culture is built on people who are curious, ambitious, accountable, and committed to delivering meaningful results for our clients and for one another.

At Power Digital, we believe the future belongs to teams that combine the best talent with the best technology. We are building that future today.

***Proficiency in spoken and written English at an advanced level is required for this role.

A day in the life:

You’ll join novaX, Power Digital’s innovation team, which builds internal and external products that help our teams and clients make decisions and get work done, such as Signal, Omega and Iris. You’ll sit in the AI/ML squad, which focuses on statistical modeling. This is a full-stack data role: you build the data systems our products run on, build predictive models on top of them, like scores that show which clients are ready to grow, and put both in front of the people who use them. One day you might trace why a number doesn’t match its source, fix the pipeline and add a test so it can’t drift again. The next you might sit with the people who use a model, learn how they make the decision, and ship a better version where they work. AI is how we build: you’ll use AI coding tools for most of what you ship, so you can take an idea from raw data to a production feature on your own. As an innovation team we move fast: we try ideas, keep what works, drop what doesn’t, and priorities can shift quickly. We’re looking for someone hungry to learn and grow with us along the way.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design, build and own the data systems our products and models run on: pipelines, services and APIs that bring together our warehouse, app databases, spreadsheets and third-party APIs.
  • Build predictive models and take them all the way to production: frame the question with users, build features, test against a baseline, ship the results where people work and keep them healthy.
  • Build with AI every day: use AI coding tools to move faster across the whole stack, and review and test what they produce before it reaches production.
  • Hold what you build to production standards (tests, code review, CI/CD, monitoring and alerts) so bad or late data is caught before a user sees it, and fix the root cause.
  • Turn vague asks into a clear problem, ship a first version fast and improve it from feedback.
  • Share what works (patterns, prompts, tools) so the whole team builds faster.
  • Work with sensitive data, including finance and people data, under strict access rules.
  • Employ AI technologies to enhance and optimize business processes
  • Utilize and leverage Power Digital's Nova ecosystem as it relates to your department
  • Design, build and own the data systems our products and models run on: dbt models, pipelines, services and APIs that bring together our warehouse, app databases, spreadsheets and third-party APIs.
  • Other applicable or related duties as assigned.

Role Requirements:

  • You have 5+ years in data engineering, data science or software roles, with hands-on work that ran in production.
  • You’re full-stack across data: you’ve built pipelines or data services, built predictive models, and connected them to something people use. You don’t need to be the deepest expert in each, but you’re comfortable in all of them.
  • You build with AI every day (Claude Code, Cursor or similar) and can show how it changed what you ship. You review, test and own what it writes.
  • You’ve built and experimented with predictive models, and you’re comfortable with work that needs modeling: framing the problem, building features and evaluating against a baseline.
  • You understand statistics well enough to set up a fair test, spot leakage and tell a real effect from noise.
  • You write strong SQL and Python, and you know good engineering basics: version control, testing and code review.
  • You can walk us through one thing you built end to end: the problem, the data, what you shipped, who used it, what failed along the way, and which parts AI wrote.
  • You start from the decision the user is trying to make, not from the data, and you ask until you understand it.
  • You’re a problem solver who learns fast and fails fast: you’d rather ship something small this week and learn from it than plan for a month, and you keep picking up new tools and methods.
  • You write clearly in English and work well async.
  • Nice to have: Snowflake (our warehouse); cloud deployment and orchestration (for example AWS); some Terraform or other infrastructure as code; marketing or client analytics such as churn or expansion; LLM apps or agents.
  • You have hands-on dbt experience in production: you've built and maintained models, tests, documentation and incremental builds. Most of our transformation work runs on dbt.
  • This is a remote role open to candidates in [the US or Latin America], at [senior, IC4–IC5].

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Reliability: the systems you own meet their agreed freshness and uptime targets, most issues are caught by your checks before a user reports them, and any that slip are resolved within a week.
  • Models in production: every model you ship is monitored, and a change ships only when it beats the current version on held-out data.
  • Adoption: everything you ship has a named user and a usage target agreed with your manager, and at the monthly review you’ve hit it or can explain why.
  • Engineering bar: what you build is tested, documented and reviewable, and a teammate can run it without you.

Most Important Things (MITs)

  • In your first 30 days, ship a fix to a production data flow or model.
  • By 90 days, be the go-to owner for one product’s data layer: you review its changes and resolve its issues without escalation. Put one model change into production with a measured before/after.
  • By 6 months, own the production path for a model end to end (data, deployment, monitoring) and have improved how the team builds and ships, with a pattern, test or tool others use.

Benefits & Perks (International):

  • Base salary paid in USD + commission opportunities
  • Unlimited Time Off available on day one
  • Fully flex work environment: full-remote, in-office, or hybrid
    • Offices in Buenos Aires, Medellin, San Diego, New York, Atlanta
  • Healthcare stipend: $50/month to support your healthcare or insurance costs
  • National Holidays + 2 Mental Health Recharge Days per year
  • Unlimited opportunities for growth & leadership within a rapidly growing firm
  • Ongoing employee development programs for personal and professional growth (Hedgehog and Vital 5s)
  • Quarterly awards including prize money and recognition for outstanding performance
  • Opportunities to be involved in company DEI initiatives

Power Digital’s people and culture are at the core of our success, which is why diversity in our team’s backgrounds and experiences are paramount. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, and backgrounds, who strive to make an impact inside and outside of the workplace. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employees' points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

Please be aware of fictitious job openings, consulting engagements, solicitations, or employment offers from suspicious sources. These engagements may be an attempt to obtain private information, or to induce you to pay a fee for services related to recruitment or training. Power Digital does NOT charge any application, processing, or training fee at any stage of the recruitment or hiring process. All genuine job openings will be posted on our careers page at . If you have any doubts about the authenticity of any messaging behalf of Power Digital, please send us an email at before taking any further action in relation to the correspondence.
