jobs.title: Technical Project Manager
jobs.excerpt: Chi siamo Siamo I MILLE, un'agenzia di comunicazione e studio di design.
jobs.description:
Chi siamo

Siamo I MILLE, un'agenzia di comunicazione e studio di design. Usiamo la creatività per trasformare il business sviluppando strategia, design e produzione in un unico processo.

Dal 2024 facciamo parte del Gruppo TXT, società quotata al segmento Euronext STAR Milan, specializzata in smart solutions, software engineering e digital advisory.

Da oltre vent'anni affianchiamo le aziende che vogliono rendere rilevante la propria comunicazione.

Un prodotto digitale, per noi, vale per come funziona davvero nelle mani di chi lo usa e per come continua a funzionare nel tempo. Perché questo accada serve qualcuno che conosca come è costruito, capisca cosa chiede chi lo usa e cosa serve a chi lo fa evolvere, e tenga insieme persone, tempi e qualità. In I MILLE crediamo in una gestione tecnica che non si limita a far girare le attività, ma crea le condizioni perché un sistema resti solido, misurabile e capace di migliorare, consegnato nei tempi e condiviso con il cliente. Se è anche il tuo modo di intendere il lavoro, conosciamoci.

Chi cerchiamo

Cerchiamo una persona con 4-6 anni di esperienza concreta nello sviluppo web che voglia spostare il proprio contributo dal codice alla gestione: del servizio, del cliente e degli interlocutori tecnici coinvolti.

La posizione nasce per prendere in carico il content management su CMS headless dei siti di un cliente internazionale, con più marchi e più mercati. Il lavoro è operativo per natura, richiede una lettura tecnica del sistema e per questo cerchiamo un profilo che venga da esperienze di sviluppo. Entro circa sei mesi la persona diventa il referente del cliente per il servizio e da lì estende il proprio ruolo ad altri progetti della unit come coordinatore tecnico, mantenendo una componente operativa proporzionata al volume di lavoro.

I MILLE è un'agenzia creativa e design studio con un team tecnico interno compatto. Le competenze tecniche del ruolo servono a dialogare con partner, fornitori e colleghi, a valutare le soluzioni proposte e a prendere decisioni fondate sui progetti in gestione.

È indispensabile la padronanza dell'italiano a livello madrelingua: il lavoro quotidiano con cliente, agenzie e colleghi si svolge in italiano e richiede precisione e naturalezza nella comunicazione scritta e orale.

La unit ha un'organizzazione lineare: si riporta al Tech Director e la responsabilità sui progetti si costruisce nel lavoro quotidiano con i colleghi. Il percorso di crescita è scandito dai livelli interni, che corrispondono a requisiti di competenze, responsabilità e retribuzione.

Cosa farai

Dall'inizio

  • Lavorerai direttamente sul CMS: inserimento e aggiornamento dei contenuti, caricamento del catalogo prodotti, gestione e adattamento degli asset, modifica delle pagine editoriali, verifica del funzionamento dei form e delle integrazioni con piattaforme esterne.

  • Prenderai decisioni e implementerai best practice SEO e di accessibilità all'interno del CMS, con il supporto dei colleghi interni.

  • Organizzerai e traccerai le attività del servizio, incluso il tempo organizzativo, tenendo sotto controllo il consumo delle ore rispetto al monte ore mensile concordato con il cliente.

  • Avrai l'affiancamento dei colleghi che oggi seguono il servizio, per assorbirne processi, contesto e storia.

  • Contribuirai secondo necessità ad altri progetti in corso all’interno della unit, familiarizzando con flussi e dinamiche interne.

Entro sei mesi

  • Sarai il punto di riferimento per il cliente e per le agenzie creative che propongono le attività e forniscono gli asset.

  • Coordinerai con il partner tecnico del cliente le verifiche su attività e componenti e seguirai definizione dei requisiti e verifica di nuovi componenti.

  • Segnalerai per tempo al cliente scostamenti e criticità e parteciperai alle revisioni periodiche del servizio.

  • Distribuirai parti operative ai colleghi quando il carico lo richiede.

In prospettiva

  • Coordinerai gli aspetti tecnici di altri progetti della unit, con fornitori e partner, e con una discrezionalità decisionale crescente.

  • Assumerai responsabilità su altri clienti, in base a interesse e risultati.

Una componente operativa di azione diretta sui CMS resta parte del ruolo in ogni fase, in misura proporzionata al volume di lavoro.

Lavorerai in un team multidisciplinare, a fianco di sviluppatori, content manager, designer e client manager.

Quali competenze ci aspettiamo che tu abbia

  • Padronanza dell'italiano a livello madrelingua, scritto e parlato.

  • Inglese a livello C1: il cliente opera su più mercati e parte degli interlocutori lavora in inglese.

  • Esperienza di alcuni anni nello sviluppo front end (HTML, CSS, JavaScript e almeno un framework come Vue o React), sufficiente a leggere il codice, individuare soluzioni tecniche e valutare l’impatto delle proposte di chi sviluppa.

  • Conoscenza operativa di back end e gestione sistemistica, tradizionale e cloud, maturata sul campo: un livello adeguato a valutare le soluzioni proposte da sviluppatori e fornitori, a dialogare con loro in modo competente e ad acquisire con rapidità le conoscenze richieste da ogni progetto.

  • Esperienza diretta e approfondita con almeno un CMS, con comprensione del content model e della logica di pubblicazione. Va bene un CMS headless (Contentful, Strapi, Sanity, Storyblok o simili) oppure un CMS tradizionale, purché l'esperienza non si limiti a progetti occasionali.

  • Conoscenza di base dei principi di SEO tecnica e accessibilità web, maturata e applicata a progetti reali.

  • Capacità di gestire più interlocutori con priorità diverse e di mettere ordine in richieste che arrivano in forma non strutturata.

  • Affidabilità e metodo nel lavoro operativo ricorrente, che resta una componente stabile del ruolo.

  • Attitudine a documentare, tracciare e rendicontare il lavoro svolto.

  • Conoscenza almeno di base delle piattaforme di intelligenza artificiale generativa.

Costituiscono un plus

  • Esperienza su Contentful.

  • Esperienza in agenzia o in contesti di servizio continuativo a clienti.

  • Capacità di scrivere script o piccoli interventi di codice a supporto dei progetti: non è richiesta, ma è benvenuta.

Cosa offriamo

  • Lavoro da remoto come assetto strutturale della posizione: la presenza a Milano è prevista per attività di formazione ed eventi aziendali, indicativamente 3-4 volte l'anno.

  • Un percorso di crescita: i primi sei mesi per prendere in carico il cliente e raggiungere l'autonomia, poi l'assegnazione di altri progetti con ruolo di coordinamento tecnico, in base alle competenze dimostrate. La crescita segue i livelli interni di I MILLE, a cui corrispondono responsabilità e fasce retributive, con momenti di verifica periodici.

  • Contratto a tempo indeterminato, CCNL Terziario Commercio.

  • RAL 28.000-32.000 €, in base a esperienza e livello di autonomia.

  • Piano di formazione interno, partecipazione a eventi di settore, momenti di knowledge sharing e team building.

  • Ticket restaurant da 7 € per ogni giorno lavorato, in presenza o da remoto.

  • Welfare aziendale 200 € all'anno.

  • Laptop aziendale e kit di benvenuto.

Come si svolge la selezione

  • Screening del CV e del messaggio di presentazione.

  • Colloquio conoscitivo con il Tech Director, responsabile della unit Tech & Operations, per conoscere I MILLE, il contesto e valutare il reciproco interesse.

  • Colloquio tecnico durante il quale discutere impostazione e gestione di uno o più scenari di servizio con cliente, agenzia e partner tecnico.

  • Eventuale colloquio finale con il COO.

Sede

Lavoriamo prevalentemente da remoto, con uffici a Milano e Roma. La posizione è full remote: la presenza a Milano è prevista per formazione ed eventi aziendali.

Pari opportunità

In I MILLE valutiamo le candidature in base a competenze, esperienza e potenziale. Accogliamo candidature da persone di qualsiasi genere, età, origine, orientamento, identità, background culturale o condizione di disabilità. Se durante il processo di selezione hai delle esigenze specifiche, segnalacelo: adatteremo le modalità del colloquio.

Trattamento dei dati

I dati personali dei candidati sono trattati ai sensi dell'art. 13 del Regolamento UE 2016/679 (GDPR), esclusivamente per le finalità di selezione del personale.

Your Impact

The Director, GTM Enablement builds and leads the enablement function that turns DISCO’s strategy into field performance. Working with Sales, Customer Success, Product Marketing, Strategy, Operations, and Product, they own enablement for the full revenue organization: SDRs, AEs, RSEs, and CSMs. They are measured by business results, not training adoption or volume: faster ramp, higher win rates, shorter sales cycles, stronger retention and expansion, and consistent execution in the field. As DISCO moves from its software foundation to its next phase of growth, they help the field keep up with what we sell.

What You'll Do

  • Enablement Strategy and Priorities: Sets a clear, outcome-based enablement roadmap across content, training, and measurement. Decides the strategy for the enablement function including what to build and what to stop, based on revenue impact, field feedback, and performance data.
  • Onboarding and Ramp: Owns the onboarding and certification path for new revenue hires, with a defined target ramp time and measured productivity. Partners with Product, Marketing, and Operations so new hires reach fluency on the platform, personas, and positioning quickly.
  • Manager-led coaching: Equips frontline managers to coach continuously, with coaching guides, monthly manager kits, and reinforcement after training. Success means behavior change that managers can see, not completed courses.
  • Sales and CS content: Works with Product Marketing to maintain a focused set of assets, including pitch decks, battlecards, playbooks, and talk tracks, and retires what the field doesn’t use.
  • Methodology and process adoption: Drives adoption of DISCO’s sales methodology and processes, and shows whether they improve qualification, forecast accuracy, and win rates. Raise concerns early when something isn’t landing with the field.
  • AI and tools: Uses AI to build content, practice scenarios, and scalable coaching, and make the current sales tech stack work before recommending new tools. Brings a business case for any new platform, including call recording and conversation intelligence.
  • Measurement and reporting: Defines the metrics that show enablement impact (ramp time, win rate, cycle time, adoption, and the business outcomes behind them) and reports them to leadership each quarter, including what isn’t working.
  • Team leadership: Leads and develops an enablement team, sets clear expectations and goals, delegates real ownership, and builds a high-accountability, high-trust culture. Owns hiring, workforce planning, and headcount decisions for the enablement function in partnership with leadership.

Who You Are

  • 15+ years in sales, field, or revenue enablement (or a related GTM role) in B2B SaaS, enterprise software, or a similar high-growth environment.
  • 2+ years of people management, with experience building or scaling an enablement function.
  • A track record of measurable revenue impact, such as shortening ramp time, improving win rates or cycle times, or driving real adoption of a methodology or program.
  • Experience rolling out a sales methodology (MEDDPICC or similar) and showing it changed field behavior and outcomes, not just completion.
  • Practical experience using AI to improve content creation, coaching, or enablement workflows and driving AI adoption across the team
  • Experience with revenue tooling, including Salesforce CRM, conversation intelligence, Outreach, and Learning Management Systems
  • Strong analytical and storytelling skills (and a bias for simplifying and prioritizing) with the ability to translate data into business impact for executives and senior leaders
  • Ability to work across functions with Sales, CS, Product Marketing, Product, and Operations, including influencing senior leaders
  • Experience with MEDDPICC, other selling methodologies, Chorus, Salesforce
  • Ability to design content, playbooks, and training from real customer conversations and complex enterprise sales cycles
  • Knowledge of instructional design frameworks applied pragmatically for fast field adoption
  • Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate across all levels of the organization and align team on company goals
  • Excellent project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and drive them to completion on schedule
  • Outstanding creative skills for crafting engaging and compelling learning content
  • Proficiency in sales enablement technologies and tools, such as CRM systems, sales engagement platforms, and content management systems

Authorization to Work in the U.S.:Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship now or in the future. DISCO is not currently sponsoring visas, including, but not limited to, H-1B, TN, or EAD, and we are not accepting visa transfers.

Perks of DISCO

  • Open, inclusive, and fun environment
  • Benefits, including medical, dental and vision insurance, as well as 401(k)
  • Competitive salary plus RSUs
  • Flexible PTO
  • Opportunity to be a part of a company that is revolutionizing the legal industry
  • Growth opportunities throughout the company

About DISCO

DISCO provides a cloud-native, artificial intelligence-powered legal solution that simplifies ediscovery, legal document review and case management for enterprises, law firms, legal services providers and governments. Our scalable, integrated solution enables legal departments to easily collect, process and review enterprise data that is relevant or potentially relevant to legal matters.

At DISCO, we believe AI is a core enabler of how work gets done. All employees are expected to proactively adopt and responsibly use AI tools to drive efficiency, improve outcomes, and continuously evolve how they operate in their role.

Are you ready to help us fulfill our mission to use technology to strengthen the rule of law? Join us!

jobs.excerpt: Notice to applicants: We have seen a rise in recruitment scams.
jobs.description:
Notice to applicants:

We have seen a rise in recruitment scams. Please note that outreach from Khan Academy recruiters will only come from the @khanacademy.org domain. Our team does not use Gmail or other personal accounts for contacting potential candidates. Khan Academy will never solicit money, equipment fees, or sensitive financial information at any stage of the hiring process. We also do not work with external recruiting agencies, so outreach from headhunters presenting opportunities on behalf of Khan Academy is illegitimate. Please always check the email domain and cross-reference the position with the official Khan Academy Careers page to confirm an opening is valid.

ABOUT KHAN ACADEMY

Khan Academy is a nonprofit with the mission to deliver a free, world-class education to anyone, anywhere. Our proven learning platform offers free, high-quality supplemental learning content and practice that cover Pre-K - 12th grade and early college core academic subjects, focusing on math and science. We have over 181 million registered learners globally and are committed to improving learning outcomes for students worldwide, focusing on learners in historically under-resourced communities.

OUR COMMUNITY

Our students, teachers, and parents come from all walks of life, and so do we. Our team includes people from academia, traditional/non-traditional education, big tech companies, and tiny startups. We hire great people from diverse backgrounds and experiences because it makes our company stronger. We value diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging as necessary to achieve our mission and impact the communities we serve. We know that transforming education starts in-house with learning about ourselves and our colleagues. We strive to be world-class in investing in our people and commit to developing you as a professional.

THE ROLE

We're looking for an experienced AP or high school business and finance educator to join Khan Academy as a Sr. Content Creator, AP Business and Personal Finance (12-Month Fixed Term). Your focus will be helping us build a free, high-quality course aligned to College Board's new AP Business with Personal Finance framework.

Khan Academy's Financial Literacy course already reaches students and adult learners across the country. The AP Business with Personal Finance course goes deeper than our current foundational content, and about half of it covers business and entrepreneurship. You'll bring the subject expertise and AP classroom perspective to help us get there.

You'll work side by side with our Senior Content Creator for Financial Literacy, who will scope the course with you and guide the work. You'll be a primary creator of content for the AP course, and you won't be working alone: you'll collaborate with other members of the content team, and possibly with external reviewers.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Partner with our Senior Content Creator to map the AP Business with Personal Finance course framework against existing Khan Academy content, and shape a scope and sequence of units, lessons, and assets.
  • Design and write AP-aligned exercises, articles, and lesson video scripts across business, entrepreneurship, and personal finance topics, building on our current Financial Literacy content where it fits.
  • Write practice questions that reflect the style and rigor of AP assessments, including the misconceptions and reasoning students need to work through.
  • Review and edit content from teammates and reviewers, and help with peer review of other Financial Literacy projects as timing allows.
  • Learn and use our content management system to build and publish the course.
  • Keep work on schedule against shared milestones, and share progress clearly with the content team and our Philanthropy partners.
  • Bring your classroom perspective to our course planning, so the course works well for AP teachers and their students.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN YOUR YEAR

Over your 12-month term, you and our Senior Content Creator will publish at least four units of the AP course, giving teachers and students a strong start on the full course.

  • First 30 days: Learn our content tools and style standards, study the AP framework, and help finalize the course scope and sequence.
  • First 3 months: Publish your first lessons and exercises, with a clear plan and timeline for the rest of the year.
  • By the end of your term: Four units are complete, published, and available to the public.
  • Throughout: Content you create meets our quality bar for accuracy, rigor, and accessibility, and leaves a clear foundation for the remaining units.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • At least 3 years of classroom experience teaching high school business, entrepreneurship, marketing, economics, or personal finance, with AP experience strongly preferred.
  • Deep knowledge of both business and personal finance concepts, from business planning and marketing to budgeting, credit, investing, and taxes.
  • Familiarity with College Board's AP course and exam design, and an understanding of how students prepare for AP-style questions.
  • Proven ability to create clear, rigorous learning materials such as lessons, assessments, or curriculum.
  • Strong intuition for how students learn and where they commonly get stuck.
  • Excellent writing skills and careful attention to detail.
  • Comfort working independently against deadlines, while collaborating closely with a small team.
  • Fluency with Google Docs and Sheets, and a willingness to learn new tools, some of which leverage AI for scaling.
  • A working knowledge/1-2 years experience with LLM-enabled workflows
  • A passion for education and for helping every student take charge of their future.
  • Motivated by the Khan Academy mission “to provide a free world-class education for anyone, anywhere."
  • Proven cross-cultural competency skills demonstrating self-awareness, awareness of other, and the ability to adopt inclusive perspectives, attitudes, and behaviors to drive inclusion and belonging throughout the organization.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience teaching or piloting AP Business with Personal Finance, or completing College Board professional development for the course.
  • Experience as a DECA, FBLA, or similar advisor, especially leading students to state or national competitions.
  • An advanced degree in business, finance, economics, or education, such as an MBA.
  • Relevant teaching experience at an undergraduate level.
  • Professional experience in finance, business, or entrepreneurship outside the classroom.
  • Experience writing assessment items for AP, state exams, or published curriculum.
  • Experience creating digital or online learning content.

ABOUT THE TERM

  • Term: This is a full-time, salaried, fixed-term role for 12 months, expected to begin in January 2027.
  • Reports to: Director, US Content, working day to day with the Senior Content Creator for Financial Literacy.
  • Location: Remote, within the United States.
  • Renewal: Extension beyond the 12-month term depends on funding and business needs. Fellows are welcome to apply for other open roles at Khan Academy during their term.

PERKS AND BENEFITS

We may be a non-profit, but we reward our talented team extremely well! We offer:

  • Competitive salary
  • Ample paid time off
  • Generous parental leav
  • 401(k) with 4% matching, plus medical, dental, vision, and life insurance
  • Affinity groups and a supportive, mission-driven team
  • The chance to put your talents toward work that reaches millions of learners

At Khan Academy we are committed to fair and equitable compensation practices, the well-being of our employees, and our Khan community. This belief is why we have built out a robust Total Rewards package that includes competitive base salaries, and extensive benefits and perks to support physical, mental, and financial well-being.

HOW TO APPLY

Along with your resume, please include a brief cover letter that tells us why you're interested in this role and describes your most relevant experience, using 1-2 specific examples.

The compensation band for this role is $96,800 - $108,900 USD annually for candidates based in the United States.

The pay range for this position is a general guideline only. The salary offered will depend on internal pay equity and the candidate’s relevant skills, experience, qualifications, and job market data.

MORE ABOUT US

  • Sal’s TED talk from 2011
  • Sal’s TED talk from 2015
  • Sal's TED talk from 2023
  • Our team:

OUR COMPANY VALUES

Live & breathe learners

We deeply understand and empathize with our users. We leverage user insights, research, and experience to build content, products, services, and experiences that our users trust and love. Our success is defined by the success of our learners and educators.

Take a stand

As a company, we have conviction in our aspirational point of view of how education will evolve. The work we do is in service to moving towards that point of view. However, we also listen, learn and flex in the face of new data, and commit to evolving this point of view as the industry and our users evolve.

Embrace diverse perspectives

We are a diverse community. We seek out and embrace a diversity of voices, perspectives and life experiences leading to stronger, more inclusive teams and better outcomes. As individuals, we are committed to bringing up tough topics and leaning into different points of view with curiosity. We actively listen, learn and collaborate to gain a shared understanding. When a decision is made, we commit to moving forward as a united team.

Work responsibly and sustainably

We understand that achieving our audacious mission is a marathon, so we set realistic timelines and we focus on delivery that also links to the bigger picture. As a non-profit, we are supported by the generosity of donors as well as strategic partners, and understand our responsibility to our finite resources. We spend every dollar as though it were our own. We are responsible for the impact we have on the world and to each other. We ensure our team and company stay healthy and financially sustainable.

Bring out the joy

We are committed to making learning a joyful process. This informs what we build for our users and the culture we co-create with our teammates, partners and donors.

Cultivate learning mindset

We believe in the power of growth for learners and for ourselves. We constantly learn and teach to improve our offerings, ourselves, and our organization. We learn from our mistakes and aren’t afraid to fail. We don't let past failures or successes stop us from taking future bold action and achieving our goals.

Deliver wow

We insist on high standards and deliver delightful, effective end-to-end experiences that our users can rely on. We choose to focus on fewer things — each of which aligns to our ambitious vision — so we can deliver high-quality experiences that accelerate positive measurable learning with our strategic partners.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, or Veteran status. jobs.excerpt: About the Role As an Engineer, Enterprise Platforms, you will be a hands-on owner of the collaboration tools our employees use all day.
jobs.description:
About the Role

As an Engineer, Enterprise Platforms, you will be a hands-on owner of the collaboration tools our employees use all day. You will administer, automate, and improve them, working alongside identity, endpoints, and the wider SaaS stack.

This is a role for someone who sees a problem, figures out the fix, and ships it. Our team is small and the scope is broad. You will have real ownership early, a lot of autonomy, and few layers between you and the people you support. You will turn policies, runbooks, and employee needs into reliable configurations, scripts, and self-service experiences. We use AI tools where they make us faster or more accurate, and we expect good judgment about when to trust them.

This role reflects Abnormal VOICE values. You move with velocity, design for long-term ownership and governance, use data with intellectual honesty, stay close to customer needs, and aim for excellence in reliability and simplicity.

What You Will Do

  • Administer Google Workspace: users, groups, org units, shared drives, Drive sharing and DLP, Gmail routing and policies, Calendar and room resources, Meet, and audit and security investigation tooling.
  • Administer Slack (Enterprise Grid): workspaces, channels, user groups, permissions, app approvals, Slack Connect, retention, export and eDiscovery, workflows, and audit logs.
  • Build and maintain automation for joiner, mover, and leaver flows, access requests, deprovisioning, and common employee needs, using SCIM, APIs, webhooks, Apps Script, and scripting.
  • Work with identity (Okta SSO, MFA, group-based access) so Google and Slack access follows least privilege and birthright rules.
  • Support endpoints and other SaaS platforms as needed, including macOS device management and long-tail SaaS administration.
  • Create self-service experiences, runbooks, and enablement content so employees can resolve common needs without escalation.
  • Participate in Tier 2/3 incidents, perform root cause analysis, and feed what you learn back into automation, runbooks, and standards.
  • Add logging, dashboards, and reporting so changes are monitored and audit questions can be answered quickly.
  • Use AI tools where they help (documentation, troubleshooting, request triage, analysis), with human review and appropriate access controls.
  • Partner with Security, GRC, Legal, People, Finance, and IT Service Delivery to deliver changes safely.
  • Triage incoming requests and incidents by impact and urgency, route them to the right owner or queue, and resolve or escalate within agreed response targets.
  • Turn vague or incomplete requests into clear requirements: ask clarifying questions, identify stakeholders and constraints, and confirm the desired outcome before building.
  • Set clear expectations with employees and stakeholders about scope, timelines, and tradeoffs. Give status updates proactively, and flag risks or delays early.

Governance and Compliance

  • Define and enforce standards for external sharing, Slack Connect, guest access, and third-party and OAuth app approval in Google Workspace and Slack.
  • Run regular access and license reviews, using systems and audit logs to find unused, orphaned, or over-privileged access.
  • Keep configuration baselines documented, changes tracked in ServiceNow, and evidence ready for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and FedRAMP audits.
  • Review audit logs and investigate suspicious activity with Security.
  • Document requirements, risks, and approvals for changes so they pass change review and can be audited later.

Scripting and Automation

  • Automate first. If a task happens more than a couple of times, you script it, build a workflow, or turn it into self-service.
  • Write scripts and tools (Python, Apps Script, and shell) against the Google Workspace, Slack, and Okta APIs.
  • Build and maintain integrations and workflows in Workato, connecting identity, HR, collaboration, ticketing, and SaaS systems.
  • Use Torii workflows to automate app discovery, onboarding and offboarding, and license reclamation.
  • Build ServiceNow catalog items and flows so requests are routed, approved, and fulfilled with minimal manual touch.
  • Keep scripts and configuration in version control, with logging, error handling, and clear documentation so others can run and maintain them.

Our Tooling

  • Collaboration: Google Workspace, Slack (Enterprise Grid)
  • Identity: Okta
  • Automation and integration: Workato, Torii, Python, Apps Script
  • Service management: ServiceNow
  • Endpoints and other: Jamf, Zoom, and a long tail of SaaS applications

You don't need experience with every tool. Strong experience with comparable platforms, and a record of learning new ones quickly, is what matters.

How We Work

  • Automation-first: We remove repetitive work rather than absorbing it, and we measure success by manual touches eliminated.
  • Customer-first: Employees are our customers. We respond with urgency, communicate clearly, and fix root causes so the same problem doesn't come back. We do what we say we'll do, or we tell people early when that changes.
  • Fast-paced: Priorities shift quickly and requests arrive from every direction. We move fast, ship in small steps, and iterate.
  • Time management and triage: You juggle incidents, requests, and project work. You sort what comes in by impact and urgency, handle what's urgent first, and protect focused time for project work and for the root-cause fixes that prevent tomorrow's tickets.

What We're Looking For

  • You find the problem before someone assigns it, and you follow through to a documented, working fix.
  • You are comfortable with ambiguity: unclear requirements, incomplete documentation, and shifting priorities don't stop you.
  • You prioritize well when everything feels urgent. You set expectations early and honestly: you say no or "not yet" clearly and kindly, and you explain the reason.
  • You learn new platforms quickly and teach what you learn.
  • You ask the right questions up front: who needs this, what problem it solves, what 'done' looks like, and what could go wrong. You propose a recommended approach rather than waiting to be told.
  • You communicate proactively: status updates, change notices, and honest post-incident write-ups.

Must Haves

  • 2+ years of experience in IT engineering, systems administration, or a similar role supporting business-critical technology.
  • Hands-on administration of Google Workspace (Admin console, groups, Drive and sharing controls, Gmail, Calendar).
  • Hands-on administration of Slack (workspace and channel management, user groups, app management, permissions). Enterprise Grid experience is a strong plus.
  • Working knowledge of identity and access concepts: SSO, MFA, least privilege, directory and group management, and SCIM or standards-based provisioning.
  • Ability to script and integrate systems using APIs, webhooks, Apps Script, Python, or similar tooling.
  • Experience with incident and change management, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and documented follow-through.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including documenting technical processes and explaining complex systems to non-technical audiences.
  • A track record of working independently and taking ownership without close direction.
  • Experience writing scripts or building workflows that automate repetitive IT work, and a habit of automating before doing something manually a third time.
  • A customer-first approach to supporting employees: responsive, clear, and focused on fixing root causes.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment and manage your time across incidents, requests, and project work, prioritizing by impact.
  • Ability to set and manage expectations with stakeholders, including saying no or negotiating scope and timelines while keeping trust.

Nice to Have

  • Experience at a startup or high-growth company, where you wore multiple hats, built processes from scratch, or scaled IT through rapid headcount growth.
  • Experience with acquisitions, tenant or domain migrations, or workspace consolidation.
  • Experience with data governance in collaboration tools: retention, legal hold, eDiscovery, DLP, and audit log analysis.
  • Google Workspace or Slack administration certifications, or involvement in their admin communities.
  • Experience with Okta, Jamf, Zoom, or other enterprise SaaS administration.
  • Experience in remote-first, SaaS-first, or zero-trust environments.
  • Familiarity with version control, configuration-as-code, or CI/CD for platform automation.
  • Experience building self-service workflows, or using AI tools to improve support, troubleshooting, and documentation.
  • Awareness of security and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP) as applied to collaboration and end-user platforms.
  • Experience with Workato or a similar integration platform (Zapier, Tray.io, Boomi, or Okta Workflows).
  • Experience with Torii or another SaaS management platform, such as Zluri or BetterCloud.
  • Experience with ServiceNow (catalog items, flows, incident, request, and change) or a similar ITSM platform.
  • Experience administering Microsoft 365 (Entra ID, Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint/OneDrive, or the M365 admin center), especially in a mixed Google and Microsoft environment.

A note on AI in our process: Abnormal AI uses AI-assisted tools to help our recruiting team prepare for candidate interviews. These tools analyze resume content and role requirements to suggest interview questions and areas for the interviewer to explore.They do not make hiring decisions or screen candidates automatically. Every decision about a candidacy is made by a person. About Augment

Private markets hold some of the most valuable and innovative companies in the world, yet trading their equity still runs on email chains, PDFs, and wire instructions. We believe that with the right infrastructure, private markets can work like markets. Augment is building that infrastructure, end to end, to make buying and selling private company exposure simple.

  • Raised $16.5M to date from investors including Builders VC, Neo, and Golden Section

The Role

Augment is growing quickly, and the systems that power the business are fundamental to supporting that growth. As the Senior Product Manager, you'll own the internal tools, admin system, and workflows our operations, compliance, finance, and sales teams use every day. You'll decide where automation will have the most impact as volume grows. Not every problem needs engineering: you'll often implement the solution yourself using AI, automation, or the right tools. You'll also support our partnerships team as needed, bringing a product perspective to partner conversations.

This is a hands-on role reporting directly to our COO. You'll work closely with engineering, design, and the business teams who use what you build.

What you'll work on

  • Own execution of the roadmap for our admin system and operations tooling, such as account and fund administration, compliance workflows, order book and sales funnel optimization, and data interfaces

  • Spend time with sales, operations, legal, compliance, and finance to understand how work actually gets done, find the bottlenecks, and decide the right fix for each

  • Solve problems directly where you can, using and combining AI, automation, or software, and allocating developer resources when a problem truly needs it

  • Support the partnerships team as needed: join partner conversations, answer product questions, and bring what partners need back into the roadmap

  • Work with compliance and legal so products meet our regulatory obligations from day one

  • Use AI for research, specs, and data work, and to build internal automations, prototype ideas, and explore the codebase

  • Write clear problem statements and product requirements

You'd be a great fit if you

  • Like getting into the details of how a team actually works and fixing what's slowing it down

  • Work like an internal consultant: you diagnose the real problem, pick the simplest solution, and have built automations or AI workflows yourself (strong plus)

  • Work hands-on with data, writing your own queries or dashboards to find problems and prove what worked

  • Are comfortable with APIs and integrations: you can read API docs and talk through an integration with engineers

  • Are comfortable in regulated, operationally complex environments such as fintech or financial infrastructure

  • Use data to find problems, set goals, and judge whether a launch worked

  • Make clear decisions with incomplete information, and turn ambiguous problems into a focused plan

  • Can say no, and explain why in a way stakeholders accept

  • Communicate clearly with technical and non-technical people alike

  • Take pride in the details, because in finance they matter

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree

  • 5-7 years of product management experience, ideally on internal tools, operations, or B2B products

  • Experience in brokerage, wealth management, or financial operations (strong plus)

How we think about AI-assisted work

We use AI throughout our work: for research, writing, and analysis across every team, and for development and AI-assisted code review. We want everyone here to be fluent with these tools and to have real opinions about how to use them well. What we care about most is judgment. AI can make great people much faster, but it can also produce work that looks right and is subtly wrong. We want people who can tell the difference, and who use these tools to move faster, not to think less.

What we are looking for

  • Experience with data contracts and schema validation.

  • Infrastructure as code (Terraform or CloudFormation) and CI/CD pipelines
  • Expert-level Python and advanced SQL, including query optimization
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to troubleshoot complex data issues and design solutions for ambiguous requirements.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication in English, with experience working with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred Requirements:

  • Streaming with Apache Kafka or AWS Kinesis.

Information Technology oversees the effective development, delivery, and operation of computing and information services. This function anticipates, plans, and delivers Information Technology solutions and strategies that enable operations and drive business value.

The Manager, Cyber Risk, is responsible for executing and continuously enhancing the cybersecurity risk management program to ensure risks are effectively identified, assessed, prioritized, and managed in alignment with organizational objectives. Reporting to the Director, Cyber Risk Services, this role plays a key part in operationalizing risk frameworks, maintaining risk visibility, and enabling risk-informed decision-making across the enterprise. This role leads cybersecurity risk capabilities including risk framework and taxonomy implementation, risk register management, risk assessments, and risk response & remediation oversight. The Lupus Foundation of America is seeking an exceptionally compassionate, culturally competent Registered Nurse to serve as the Lupus Clinical Trial Navigator in support of a bi-directional partnership with between the Lupus Foundation of America and several academic medical centers conducting lupus clinical trials to support programmatic grant work as a contractor within the LFA. The contractor will be a member of the research team at will report directly to the VP of Research.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

This grant-funded role is central to our mission of advancing health equity and improving the lives of all people living with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) by improving access to clinical research opportunities that have historically excluded their communities. The Navigator will serve as the primary liaison between our Research Accelerated by You (RAY) Lupus Patient Registry and active lupus clinical trials currently enrolling at selected academic medical centers. Working at the intersection of clinical care, patient advocacy, and research operations, this individual will guide registry participants through the education, screening and enrollment stages of the clinical trial process, from initial consultation and eligibility screening through enrollment and ongoing support where needed. This is a unique and mission-driven opportunity to directly impact clinical research diversity while building meaningful, longitudinal relationships with patients from underrepresented communities disproportionately affected by lupus.

The nurse-navigator must maintain great work ethic and display productivity, working both independently and as part of a team in a hybrid and/or remote environment. The individual will work in cooperation with the research team to facilitate collaboration across academic partners and people living with lupus. This individual must also be comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and managing protected health information (PHI) in accordance with HIPAA.

POSITION REQUIREMENTS

Registry Consultation & Patient Engagement

  • Conduct structured intake consultations with new RAY registry participants who have indicated interest in participating in a clinical trial to assess disease history, medication profile, research readiness, and participation barriers
  • Maintain ongoing, longitudinal relationships with registry participants through regular outreach by phone, video, or secure messaging through screening and enrollment periods
  • Provide culturally sensitive education about clinical trials, informed consent, and participants’ rights in plain, accessible language using previously curated educational materials developed by the Lupus Foundation of America
  • Address common barriers to participation including transportation, scheduling, language access, childcare/caregiver responsibilities, and historical medical mistrust where appropriate

Clinical Trial Screening & Matching (Outbound Flow)

  • Maintain current, detailed knowledge of eligibility criteria for active lupus clinical trials at selected academic institutions
  • Systematically review registry participants against trial eligibility criteria and flag potential matches
  • Conduct pre-screening interviews and coordinate baseline assessments as appropriate
  • Prepare warm, informed hand-offs to academic medical center research coordinators with relevant clinical summaries and participant consent

Retention & Ongoing Participant Support

  • Maintain contact with enrolled participants throughout trial duration to support adherence and address concerns
  • Serve as a trusted first point of contact for non-medical questions, triaging and communicating with the research site as appropriate
  • Document participant-reported barriers and solutions to inform ongoing program improvement

Partnership Coordination & Reporting

  • Participate in monthly touchpoint meetings with academic medical center research coordinators to review referral pipeline, enrollment status, and protocol updates
  • Maintain accurate records in alignment with the RAY Registry database and document all navigator interactions
  • Contribute data and narrative content to quarterly and annual grant progress reports and organizational board reports
  • Assist in preparation of IRB submissions, data use agreements, and partnership documentation as needed

EDUCATION AND LICENSE REQUIREMENTS

  • Active, unrestricted Registered Nurse (RN) license in the state(s) of practice
  • Minimum 5 years of clinical nursing experience; rheumatology, immunology, oncology, or research experience strongly preferred
  • Demonstrated experience working with underrepresented communities in healthcare settings with knowledge related to navigating healthcare access complexities due to social determinants of health
  • Strong knowledge of clinical trial processes, including informed consent, eligibility screening, and Good Clinical Practice principles along with Institutional Review Board requirements
  • Exceptional interpersonal communication skills with the ability to build trust with patients navigating complex healthcare systems
  • Experience partnering with academic medical centers and clinical trial teams to coordinate referrals, support enrollment workflows, and manage ongoing stakeholder communication related to clinical research participation
  • Comfort working independently in a remote or hybrid environment with minimal day-to-day supervision
  • Proficiency with electronic health systems, registry databases, CRM platforms, and maintaining HIPAA compliance while collecting/managing PHI

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Prior experience as a patient navigator, research nurse, or clinical research coordinator (CRC)
  • Bilingual fluency in Spanish, or another language representative of the served community
  • Familiarity with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) clinical presentation, treatment landscape, and patient experience data
  • Knowledge of NIH inclusion policies and FDA guidance on diversity in clinical trials
  • OCR Certification or completion of ACRP/SOCRA credentialing
  • Experience contributing to grant reporting, complex data capture and academic publications
  • Remote; preferred location in the South Atlantic region, DMV or South Carolina

Other Details

  • Ability to interact with people of all ages and cultural backgrounds.
  • LFA participates in E-Verify.
  • Background checks are required.

JOIN US
If you’re a dynamic, mission-driven individual passionate about driving positive change and improving lives, we encourage you to apply! At LFA, your contributions will help solve the mystery of lupus and create a world where people with lupus can live healthier, fuller lives while making a lasting difference.

About Us

Care New England Health System (CNE) and its member institutions, Butler Hospital, Women & Infants Hospital, Kent Hospital, VNA of Care New England, Integra, The Providence Center, and Care New England Medical Group, is a trusted, integrated health care organization that fuels the latest advances in medical research, attracts the nation’s top specialty-trained doctors, hones renowned services and innovative programs, and engages in the important discussions people need to have about their health and end-of-life wishes. Care New England is helping to transform the future of health care, providing a leading voice in the ongoing effort to ensure the health of the individuals and communities we serve.

Job Summary

The role of a Certified Outpatient Coder at Care New England is to ensure accurate assignment of ICD-10 CM, CPT and HCPCS codes on a wide range of patient medical records for outpatient services. Outpatient services include, but are not limited to observation, surgical, provider-based visits, interventional radiology, emergency room, oncology, and other specialty services. A proficient understanding and execution of coding guidelines to ensure accuracy of coding and maintain records in accordance with accepted medical and legal standards.

Adherence and compliance to various regulatory guidelines from CMS, AHA and AMA.

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Analyze medical records, extracting clinical, pathological, therapeutic and epidemiologic data in accordance with established ICD-10-CM coding principles and guidelines
  • Assigns Codes and codes all diagnostic and operative information from the medical record using ICD-10-CM/ICD-10-CM, ICD-10 PCS, CPT, HCPCS coding classification systems and independently quality checks own work
  • Assigning ICD-10 diagnosis codes, CPT validation, modifier assignment
  • Ensures that all data abstracted is consistent with guidelines outlined by JCAHO, and CMS, regional and local policy
  • Evaluating, addressing and understanding CCI, LCD and NCD edits
  • Ensure data is optimally coded for documentation capture, financial reimbursement, care planning, statistics and regulatory reporting
  • Reviews medical records to determine accurate required abstracting elements (facility/client specific elements) including appropriate discharge disposition to ensure accurate reimbursement
  • Demonstrates a comprehensive, expert-level of knowledge of all procedures concerning the sequencing of diagnoses, procedures such as but not limited to those outlined in ICD-10-CM, CPT, Uniform Hospital Discharge Data Set, Medicare guidelines and other appropriate classification systems
  • Demonstrates knowledge of anatomy, physiology pharmacology and pathophysiology to interpret general medical classifications for coding discharge data.
  • Ensures timely record availability by meeting established coding and abstracting CNE productivity and accuracy standards
  • Communicates and resolves coding issues around documentation for appropriate follow-up and education
  • Interacts and communicates with department lead and manager to clarify and accurately document patient diagnostic and procedural information
  • Maintains and complies with policies and procedures for confidentiality of all patient records
  • Performs other related duties as assigned

Requirements

  • High School or GED Required
  • Minimum 6 Months to 1 Year of experience.
  • This position has a preferred certification as a Certified Coding Specialist (CCS). A Certified Professional Coding certification will also be considered with additional years of experience.
  • Completion of classes in medical terminology, anatomy and physiology, ICD-10 and CPT coding conventions, and disease process from an accredited program.
  • Coding certification must be maintained
  • Ability to demonstrate knowledge of and utilize auditing skills related to coding quality and compliance.
  • Ability to understand the clinical content of a health record, including the most complicated records.
  • Must also be able to communicate with others in order to clarify diagnoses/procedures and sequencing of diagnoses.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy is necessary.
  • Will abide by the AHIMA coding code of ethics.
  • Must be able to maintain department productivity and accuracy standards.

What You Bring

By 3 to 12 months

How You Work

jobs.excerpt: If you’re passionate about helping people protect what matters most to them at a Fortune 100 company with nearly $70 billion in annual sales, as well as innovating and simplifying processes and operations to provide the best customer value, then Nationwide’s Property and Casualty team could be the place for you!
jobs.description:
If you’re passionate about helping people protect what matters most to them at a Fortune 100 company with nearly $70 billion in annual sales, as well as innovating and simplifying processes and operations to provide the best customer value, then Nationwide’s Property and Casualty team could be the place for you! At Nationwide®, “on your side” goes beyond just words. Our customers and partners are at the center of everything we do and we’re looking for associates who are passionate about delivering extraordinary care.

This is a unique role within Contract Underwriting that is responsible for leveraging strong partner relationships, a solution-oriented mindset, and technical underwriting acumen to drive profitable growth across the Alternative Distribution portfolio.


In this role, you will partner with Contract Underwriting appointed Wholesale Managing General Agents to vet, operationalize, manage, and grow new and existing alternatively distributed products. Alternative Distribution refers to business that is solicited through wholesale binding distribution and generally falls within Contract Underwriting appetite but is transacted via non-traditional channels, i.e. digital storefronts and non-API supported placement (i.e. bordereaux).


You’ll be responsible for vetting, developing, and actively managing these solutions and collaborating with partners to analyze, develop, implement, and refine underwriting guidelines and pricing as appropriate. You will manage the P&L of each individual solution and handle individual account underwriting for referral business that falls outside prescribed authority. You will also provide operational support and oversight to ensure non-API supported solutions such as bordereaux-managed business is captured and ingested appropriately as well as ensuring the risks within the greater portfolio fall within prescribed authority, mix of business targets, and other predefined underwriting parameters. In order to be successful in this role, you will need to build and maintain effective relationships with internal business liaisons as well as external partners.


Additional expectations associated with this role:

Portfolio & Profitability Management:

  • Monitor program and portfolio performance, including profitability, growth, and loss trends; develop and implement corrective action plans as needed.
  • Analyze results across programs, classes of business, and geographies to optimize underwriting strategy.
  • Participate in and support bi-annual underwriting audits as needed to ensure guideline adherence; provide detailed analysis and recommendations based on findings.
  • Produce and deliver monthly and ad hoc performance reports to underwriting leadership and other internal/external stakeholders.

Product Development & Strategy:

  • Conduct research, development, and implementation of new and existing solutions, including underwriting guidelines, forms and rate structures.
  • Collaborate with external partners as well as internal business liaisons to design and deploy product-specific tools and enhancements.
  • Recommend and implement updates to underwriting guidelines based on product performance, market trends and emerging risks.
  • Identify and capitalize on new business opportunities through market analysis and strategic insight.

Relationship Management & Business Development:

  • Establish and maintain strong relationships with wholesale managing general agents and internal stakeholders to drive profitable growth.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor and technical underwriting resource to partners, resolving complex issues and supporting deal execution.
  • Conduct regular communication with partners to assess market conditions, profitability, and pipeline opportunities.
  • Travel as needed for agency visits, audits, marketing meetings, and relationship-building activities.
  • Represent the organization at industry events and contribute to marketing initiatives that promote underwriting capabilities and generate new business opportunities.

Ideal Candidate Will Possess:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Risk Management, or related field preferred.
  • Approximately 6+ years of experience in specialty, program, or contract underwriting.
  • Strong understanding of underwriting guidelines, insurance law, contract structures, and coverage design.
  • Knowledge of reinsurance principles and placement strategies preferred.

*This role does not qualify for employer-sponsored work authorization. Nationwide does not participate in the Stem OPT Extension program*


Job Description Summary

Are you a critical thinker who can analyze complex risk and find insurance solutions that balance customer needs with business goals? If you can take initiative, use both your analytical and creative abilities to make sound decisions and have a desire to help people solve real challenges, we want to hear from you!

Our Excess & Surplus/Specialty (E&S/S) lines allow us to provide insurance that other carriers may not offer. It’s a fast-paced environment in a collaborative, team-oriented culture, working in an always-changing, growing industry.

As an Underwriting Specialist in Contract you determine individual risk acceptability, pricing, coverage, terms and conditions, by developing, analyzing and evaluating information and exposures on risks of a complex technical nature for the assigned line of business. In addition, you’ll achieve production and loss ratio goals with assigned general agents or program managers by reviewing and analyzing claims, loss history and taking appropriate action on accounts. General agent assignments are more complex in terms of coverage and general agent relationships. It’s important to establish and maintain effective relationships with general agents to generate premium dollars and profitability. You will work independently with a high level of authority and judgment. Determining appropriate reinsurance placement, if any, on individual accounts is an important element of this role. We will count on you to foster positive business relationships with co-workers, general agents and reinsurers. You will also assist with research, development and presentation of new products, forms and manuals and have opportunities to assist in the training and mentoring of Underwriters and Underwriting Assistants.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

  • Reviews individual risks with assigned agents or programs within assigned territory and either declines or accepts business based upon information necessary to make the decision. The underwriter analyzes, with a high level of technical expertise, exposures to loss, develops an adequate premium charge for the exposure and determines appropriate endorsements and exclusions to address loss exposures for the insurance contract. Within department guidelines, places reinsurance, if any, for the account.

  • Achieves individual production and loss ratio goals within assigned territory through sound territory management and marketing. Achieves production, profitability and service objectives. Quotes, prices and underwrites new and renewal policies and endorsements, primarily for complex or service sensitive accounts. Monitors risk selection and pricing decisions for entire agency plant, both on a book of business and individual account level basis. Works with more complex issues concerning coverage, programs, agents and program managers. The underwriter continually analyzes premium and loss results in their territory or assigned agents by agency, state, major class of business and by program. Continually assess quality of submissions and makes corrective action recommendations. Development and implementation of specific action plans may be required

  • Handles policy maintenance items and other mid-term requests. Reviews endorsement requests and processes necessary changes to the policy. Reviews loss control reports and makes recommendations to the agent and/or changes to the policy. Follows up on outstanding information as required. Reviews claim activity and takes appropriate action. May review agency books of business as well as profit/growth results and trends to recommend and implement action plans.

  • Fosters positive business relationships with general agents through daily contact with assigned agents by developing and maintaining good rapport and resolving agency conflicts. Travels to agency offices as required for audits, training or marketing visits. Entertains agents visiting the Company as required. Assists with development of marketing ideas and strategies for underwriting seminars and other marketing campaigns.

  • Places reinsurance per department guidelines based upon the appropriate use of all reinsurance facilities used by the department, including various treaty semiautomatic and facultative reinsurance. Maintains good working relationship with reinsurers.

  • Markets Nationwide products and services to help drive agency and company results, including all enterprise products that may enhance offerings. Assists agency with strategies for pipeline management, producer development and to develop new business in targeted industries and preferred markets. Responds effectively to assess accounts and develop business propositions that win the business.

  • Other responsibilities as assigned may include program research and development, form development, rate development, technical assistance to Agents, Underwriting Assistants, and other Underwriters. Proactively develops technical and business knowledge through internal and external venues

May perform other responsibilities as assigned.

Reporting Relationships: Reports to Department Manager

Typical Skills and Experiences:

Education: Undergraduate degree preferred. Equivalent work experience will be considered in lieu of a degree.

License/Certification/Designation: Completion of general insurance courses such as CPCU, CIC, AU, ARM, CPIW, CWIS, or ASLI is preferred.

Experience: Six years related experience or five years as an underwriter, excess & surplus lines preferred.

Knowledge, Abilities and Skills: Knowledge of lines underwriting policies, practices and procedures, insurance law and underwriting marketing principles and techniques, rating plans and plan concepts, Treaty & Facultative reinsurance concepts, general agency system and company operations, regulatory issues, the general agency system, market conditions and company operations. Ability to communicate effectively, orally, and in writing, interpersonally with individuals and groups via telephone, fax, e-mail and in person. Demonstrates advanced negotiation skills. Ability to manage the assigned line or lines of business, which may include monitoring of aggregates. Ability to work with the wholesale/general agency distribution system. Ability to analyze insurance risks to determine acceptability including policy language, various commercial rating plans and methodologies, reinsurance. Ability to use/learn job related computer software. Ability to devise business solutions to problems, implement the most appropriate, and monitor its effectiveness. Ability to make decisions with minimal supervision.

Other criteria, including leadership skills, competencies and experiences may take precedence.

Staffing exceptions to the above must be approved by the hiring manager’s leader and HR Business Partner.

Values: Regularly and consistently demonstrates Nationwide Values.

Job Conditions:

Overtime Eligibility: Not Eligible (Exempt)

Working Conditions: Normal office environment. Travel out of state as required several times a year. In-town entertaining required as necessary after 5:00 P.M.

Benefits

We have an array of benefits to fit your needs, including: medical/dental/vision,life insurance, short and long term disability coverage, paid time off with newly hired associates receiving a minimum of 18 days paid time off each full calendar year pro-rated quarterly based on hire date, nine paid holidays, 8 hours of Lifetime paid time off, 8 hours of Unity Day paid time off, 401(k) with company match, company-paid pension plan, business casual attire, and more. jobs.description:
Job ID: 18910

Alternate Locations: Remote

Newell Brands is a leading consumer products company with a portfolio of iconic brands like Graco®, Coleman®, Oster®, Rubbermaid®, Sharpie® and Yankee Candle® - and 24,000 talented teammates around the world. Our culture is built on values in action: Integrity, Teamwork, Passion for Winning, Ownership, and Leadership. We work together to win, grow, and make a real impact—supported by a high-performing, inclusive, and collaborative environment where you can be your best, every day.

Reports To

Director, Global Reliability

Department

Engineering, Reliability & Automation (ERA)

Organization

Global Supply Chain and Procurement (GPSN)

POSITION SUMMARY

The Sr. Manager, Reliability is a senior technical contributor and program manager within the ERA Global Reliability team, responsible for executing reliability improvement programs across a portfolio of Newell Brands manufacturing sites and distribution centers within the global network of 40+ manufacturing facilities, 60 DCs, and markets in 140 countries. Reporting to the Director, Global Reliability, this role is a field-level executor of the Newell Brands Strategic Equipment Management Policy (SEMP) — the company's governing framework for how assets are planned, acquired, operated, maintained, and retired across the global supply chain network. The Sr. Manager translates SEMP requirements into site-level programs, assessments, and improvement plans, ensuring policy intent is operationalized consistently across assigned sites. This role owns hands-on reliability engineering deliverables: asset criticality assessments, fleet management analysis, condition monitoring program builds, PM optimization, failure mode investigations, and reliability KPI reporting. The Sr. Manager acts as a working technical lead, supporting the fleet management strategy by executing site-level programs that feed network-wide asset intelligence — guiding site-level reliability engineers and maintenance teams through structured improvement initiatives while managing multiple concurrent workstreams and site engagements. This role is a key execution engine for the Global Reliability Program within the ERA Strategic Master Plan.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Reliability Program Execution

  • Execute site-level reliability assessments using the ERA reliability framework: asset registry validation, criticality ranking (FMECA-based), PM plan audit, and condition monitoring gap analysis across manufacturing sites and DC facilities.
  • Develop and implement PM optimization plans using RCM principles, condition-based triggers, and failure mode data; establish PM intervals grounded in equipment OEM data and operational history.
  • Lead condition monitoring program deployment at assigned sites, including vibration analysis routes, oil sampling schedules, thermographic inspection programs, and ultrasound surveys.
  • Execute the Tribo Program at assigned sites: conduct Tribo Scorecard assessments, develop site-level lubrication improvement plans, support development of on-site tribology SMEs, and track progress against network Tribo standards defined by the Director, Global Reliability.
  • Conduct and lead root cause failure analysis (RCFA) investigations for chronic failures and high-impact asset events; own corrective action tracking through closure.
  • Build and maintain failure mode libraries and asset-specific maintenance task lists within MicroMain CMMS.

Fleet Management Execution

  • Execute fleet management assessments within assigned site portfolios: document asset populations by class (motors, drives, compressors, conveyors, automation equipment, etc.), validate fleet criticality ratings, and identify fleet-level PM standardization gaps.
  • Contribute fleet performance data to network-level benchmarking; identify poor-performing assets within a fleet class and recommend lifecycle interventions (condition-based replacement, refurbishment, or standardization).
  • Support the Director in developing capital replacement schedules for critical fleet segments; provide site-level asset condition inputs to long-range capital planning.
  • Implement fleet-based spare parts strategies at assigned sites, including kitting standards and critical spare identification aligned to fleet criticality tiers.

CMMS & Data Management

  • Drive asset data quality within MicroMain: asset hierarchy integrity, PM plan completeness, labor hour capture, and work order classification accuracy.
  • Generate reliability KPI reports including PMR, MTBF, MTTR, planned vs. unplanned maintenance ratio, and backlog analysis at site and regional levels.
  • Support development of reliability analytics dashboards in coordination with the ERA AI & Digital Enablement team.
  • Identify data gaps in CMMS cost fields and labor actuals; develop site-specific data governance improvement plans.

Site Engagement & Coaching

  • Partner with site Engineering Managers and Maintenance Supervisors to build local reliability ownership and PM discipline at the front line.
  • Execute PEAK EFO pillar assessments at assigned sites, evaluating AM and PM pillar maturity against global standards; document gaps, develop site-level improvement plans, and track progression through defined maturity stages in alignment with the Director's network-wide EFO program.
  • Facilitate reliability-focused kaizen events, PM standardization workshops, and condition monitoring training at assigned sites.
  • Support development of site Reliability Engineers through on-site coaching, structured work plans, and technical mentorship.
  • Travel to assigned manufacturing sites (domestic and international) on a regular cadence to assess program execution and drive improvement.

Program Management & Reporting

  • Manage concurrent reliability improvement projects across a portfolio of 4-8 manufacturing sites; maintain project plans, milestone tracking, and risk logs.
  • Report site-level PMR, OEE, and condition monitoring adoption metrics to the Director, Global Reliability on a regular cadence.
  • Participate in PEAK operating reviews, contributing reliability KPIs and site action plans to the monthly/quarterly cadence.
  • Support development of reliability investment business cases, cost avoidance analyses, and capital justification documentation.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Coordinate with ERA Automation and OT teams to integrate condition monitoring sensors and edge devices into the site OT network architecture.
  • Partner with Operations to align reliability program priorities with production scheduling, planned outage windows, and capital projects.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • 7+ years of experience in reliability engineering, maintenance engineering, or asset management in a manufacturing environment.
  • Hands-on experience with condition monitoring technologies: vibration analysis, oil analysis, thermography, or equivalent.
  • Experience with CMMS platforms for asset management, PM planning, and work order execution.
  • Working knowledge of RCM, FMECA, PM optimization, and root cause failure analysis methodologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple workstreams and site engagements simultaneously.

Preferred

  • CMRP, CRL, or Category I/II vibration analyst certification (ISO 18436 or equivalent).
  • Experience with MicroMain or similar CMMS platforms.
  • Familiarity with PEAK, Lean, or Six Sigma methodologies.
  • International manufacturing site experience; LATAM or EMEA exposure preferred.
  • Experience integrating condition monitoring data with industrial analytics or AI platforms.

COMPETENCIES

  • Strong hands-on technical capability in reliability engineering disciplines
  • Structured problem solver with a data-driven approach to failure analysis
  • Effective communicator with site-level teams and program leadership

We're growing the sales team, so you'd be adding to it, not replacing anyone.

Why intent?

We've been designing and co-creating connected devices since 2008, and the mobile app is where most people actually meet them. We build the iOS, Android, and Flutter apps that pair with wearables, smart audio, and health-tech hardware over Bluetooth, turn raw sensor data into something a person can use, and keep the device worth wearing long after the unboxing, together with the firmware and cloud behind them. We do it for clients like Oura and BOSE, backed by investors like a16z and Founders Fund. We're 60+ people, fully remote, and AI-native in actual work, not just in company decks. It's also not for you if you want someone to tell you exactly what to do each morning. We look for people who say "I had a spare hour and an idea, so I tried it" or "here's my plan for tomorrow, tell me if it makes sense". If AI tools and notetakers feel like a gimmick to you, or you need to build every deck by hand to trust it, we're not the right fit. Finally: US buyers work US hours. What you'll do

  • Use AI tools as part of your daily workflow, not as a party trick

What we're looking for

  • 4-5+ years in B2B sales, with proven experience selling to the US market (not "we had one American client once")

  • Real consultative sales skills: you uncover what the client needs, which is often not what they first asked for

  • Experience selling to enterprise clients, including long sales cycles and multiple decision-makers

  • Experience selling complex B2B services, ideally software development or consulting

  • An understanding of how selling software development services differs from selling a SaaS product

  • A track record of creating and closing large new business opportunities ($1M+)

  • The ability and the appetite to prospect, not just manage inbound

  • Basic tech literacy: you don't need to write firmware, but IoT, embedded, and software shouldn't sound like a foreign language

  • Fluent English, written and spoken

  • AI-native habits: you already use AI in your sales work and can show how

  • Proactivity, discipline, and accountability for results, plus the kind of communication where people don't have to guess what you meant

Nice to have

  • A background in software development or technology consulting sales

  • Enterprise SaaS experience where the sale was truly consultative: understanding needs and proposing solutions to large organisations, not managing renewals

  • Experience with hardware, IoT, or connected device clients

  • An existing network among US product and technology leaders

  • Genuine curiosity about the devices our clients build, not just the contracts behind them

How we work

Fully remote, with an office in Warsaw. We're flexible about when you work: nobody expects eight hours in one block. What isn't flexible is showing up for meetings, and that matters most. 10:00-18:00 CET is the window for meetings with the rest of the team, engineers included. The sales team has two fixed ones every day: at 12:00 CET a more technical session on tools, automations, and the sales process, and at 16:00 CET a daily on live deals and sales projects.

Now the honest part. Client calls follow the client's clock, not ours. We always try to book the earliest slot we can, but calls at 21:00 CET happen, and sometimes later ones too. The team rule is simple: you do what you gotta do. You'll be part of the Business Development team, working directly with our Head of Business Development and close to the C-lvl.

What you'll get

  • On-target earnings up to 28,000 PLN a month net B2B: a fixed base salary plus commission

  • 26 days of paid leave

  • 10 days of paid sick leave

  • Saltus medical care

  • Training budget

  • Open ground: no carved-up territories, no inherited account lists, and real influence on how we sell

Your first weeks

You'll start by getting to know what we actually build: the projects, the technical teams, and the stories behind our best work, so you can sell it with a straight face. You'll work closely with our Head of Business Development and get into real conversations with prospects early. Feedback comes early and often, in both directions; no one waits three months to tell you something isn't working. We'll be watching for the same things this ad is about: initiative, discipline, and a pipeline that starts to take shape.

Recruitment process

The entire process is in English. All interviews are recorded for internal evaluation purposes.

  1. Application with a few screening questions

  2. HR call (~45 min)

  3. Short task: a 5-minute video about the $1M deal you're most proud of and how consultative sales got it closed

  4. Interview with our Head of Business Development (~60 min)

  5. Conversation with our C-level (~30 min, for finalists)

Once we're in touch, you'll hear from us fast. We don't ghost and we don't drag.

intent is an equal opportunity employer. We care about what you can do, not where you come from. Send us your CV and a few words about why this caught your eye. Bonus points if you tell us about a deal that made you proud.
