jobs.description:
Sprinklr is the definitive, AI-native platform for Unified Customer Experience Management (Unified-CXM), empowering brands to deliver extraordinary experiences at scale — across every customer touchpoint.

By combining human instinct with the speed and efficiency of AI, Sprinklr helps brands earn trust and loyalty through personalized, seamless, and efficient customer interactions. Sprinklr’s unified platform provides powerful solutions for every customer-facing team — spanning social media management, marketing, advertising, customer feedback, and omnichannel contact center management — enabling enterprises to unify data, break down silos, and act on real-time insights.

Today, 1,900+ enterprises and 60% of the Fortune 100 rely on Sprinklr to help them deliver consistent, trusted customer experiences worldwide.

Job Description

Role Purpose

Acts as an expert individual contributor for the most strategic partnerships and transformation programmes, defining objectives with broad direction.

What You'll Do

  • Understand customer objectives, processes, teams, technical architecture and use of Sprinklr.
  • Build success plans with agreed outcomes, adoption goals, key performance indicators and measures of value.
  • Use customer health, adoption and consumption data to identify risks, opportunities and actions.
  • Conduct customer cadences and business reviews to align priorities, demonstrate value and maintain sponsorship.
  • Guide customers on product capabilities, use cases, releases, roadmap context and adoption practices.
  • Coordinate Product, Support, Services, Sales, Solutions Consulting and Partnerships resources.
  • Identify adoption blockers, consumption risks and workflow inefficiencies and drive corrective action.
  • Advocate for customer needs internally and shape practical paths to resolution.
  • Identify retention and expansion opportunities based on customer priorities and realised value.
  • Build customer champions who can articulate the value achieved through Sprinklr.
  • Lead strategic, high-impact customers involving executive sponsors, multiple business units and regional or global stakeholders.
  • Define long-range partnership strategies linked to enterprise operating model, customer experience and artificial intelligence priorities.
  • Create success methods, governance models or scalable programmes usable beyond the immediate portfolio.
  • Provide expert insight to regional strategy, product priorities and customer risk decisions.
  • Mentor Customer Success colleagues without formal people management.
  • Adapt success plans to ANZ business priorities, operating models and technology environments.

Who You Are and What Makes You Qualified

  • Broad Customer Success, consulting or transformation expertise demonstrated through highly complex enterprise outcomes.
  • Sustained success leading executive-sponsored, multi-year or organisation-wide programmes.
  • Expert executive advisory, value realisation, programme leadership, adoption strategy and risk-management capability.
  • Ability to define objectives and influence across organisational boundaries.
  • Recognised credibility with senior customer stakeholders.
  • Deep expertise across customer experience, marketing automation, contact centre, artificial intelligence, analytics or data platforms.
  • Typically 12+ years of relevant experience, or equivalent experience.
  • Professional fluency in English is required.
  • ANZ Customer Success or technology consulting experience is highly valued.
  • Ability to travel within Australia and New Zealand.

How This Role Operates

  • Receives broad direction and defines objectives for strategic assignments, influencing customer and internal approaches through expert judgement.
  • This is an individual contributor role without formal people management responsibility.

We focus on our mission: Sprinklr was founded in 2009 to solve a big problem: growing enterprise complexity that separated brands from their customers.   • Lead a new category of enterprise software that we call Unified-CXM.

  • Empower companies to deliver next generation, unified engagement journeys that reimagine the customer experience.

  • Create a culture of customer obsession, with trust, teamwork, and accountability.

We believe in our product: Customers who value exceptional customer experiences have what they need on our single unified platform, built with an operating system approach on a single codebase. That means that everything — and everyone — can work together to service, respond, sell, and market to customers on the channels they prefer. While Unified Customer Experience Management (Unified-CXM) as a category is just getting started, we are well on our way to creating a no-compromise, unified approach to better customer experiences for the world’s leading enterprise brands.

jobs.title: Senior Sales Development Representative - 4 Day Week + Remote
jobs.excerpt: Still get a buzz from a cold call?  Good.  So do we.
jobs.description:
Still get a buzz from a cold call? Good. So do we.

Our SDRs call commercial, project and operations leaders at some of the UK's biggest construction firms. They're busy, they're blunt, and they've heard every software pitch going (some of them twice before lunch). Earn their two minutes, find a genuine problem on a live project, and you'll hand over a meeting your Account Executive can actually win.

You've done this before, so you know a full calendar isn't the same as a good one. Here, quality wins every time, and you'll have a playbook that works, coaching from people who know construction, and a team that backs you to do it properly.

If you want your experience to count for more than your dial count, keep reading.

(this will be a long write up but we like to give you all the details before you spend your time applying)

We are Shape.Construction!

We are digitising the largest and most fundamental industry in the world, the industry that literally builds the foundations of the civilisation we all depend on to spare us from a brutal hunter-gatherer life: CONSTRUCTION

It is one of the least digitised industries in the world but also the largest – 1 in 9 people globally work in the construction industry and it constitutes 11% of global GDP.

Improving construction strengthens the very foundation of human civilisation. (Watch our short film about it).

We got our start as a high-end construction project management consultancy. As a consultancy, we are focused on genuinely upgrading the way construction projects are delivered. We then take the deep understanding of the projects we work on to develop construction management software products that anyone can use to deliver their projects better.

We are building a full suite of products one module at a time – kind of like office 365 but for construction management - Check out Shape, our construction management tech

The core of all this is our true secret sauce; people. We only recruit the very best both in capability and personality. We are deeply focused on designing a new type of organisation that is optimised for the flourishing of the people in the team first and foremost. People that join us develop fast as a whole person in ways they never imagined.

This approach has allowed us to grow from just 2 people in 2017 to over 220 today (including consultancy) and we are still very much at the beginning! Joining us isn't just some "job", it is a transformative educational experience. We challenge you to be your best self in all aspects of life.

4 core values for a good life

We believe a life of human flourishing is all about meaningful relationships with others and challenging yourself to create a positive impact. So our values reflect the 4 levels of relationships that each of us has:

  • Grow yourself – Your relationship with yourself
  • Care about people – Your relationship with others around you
  • Execute to greatness – Your relationship with your team
  • Build civilisation – Your relationship with humanity and the world

This goes much deeper but for the sake of brevity, we will keep the summary version!

We enshrined our values in our vision

We exist so that everyone in our team can thrive in a high-impact community that:

  • Connects us with meaningful relationships
  • Inspires us to develop ourselves to become better humans
  • Empowers us to pursue our own learning adventures

We believe that, by first doing this, we can achieve the highest levels of value for the world.

And enable the achievement of our vision through our dual missions:

  1. To fully digitise the construction of human civilisation
  2. To create a new type of organisation that enables human flourishing while delivering a huge positive impact on society

The Role

Purpose of the role

You're where every Shape deal starts, and one of the people who sets the standard for how we prospect. As you grow, you'll shape our messaging and set the bar for the SDRs who join after you.

What the job actually is

You know the job. Most of your day is on the phone, and you'll hear "no", "not now" and "just send me an email" more than anything else. Here, you'll be calling commercial, project and operations leaders at tier 1 and tier 2 construction firms (main contractors and the subcontractors who work for them). They're running live projects, their time is precious and they're wary of anyone selling software. Almost all of our pipeline is outbound, apart from customer referrals, so the meetings you book are ones you've created yourself.

You also know that to be good at cold calling, you have to genuinely love it. If you don't, and you plan to go through the motions, it's a boring job, and it shows on every call. We're looking for someone who still gets a buzz from turning a cold "who's this?" into a real conversation.

Quality over quantity, always. We care about the work we do and take pride in doing it properly, and we want people who feel the same. You'll know a booked meeting isn't the same as a good one. Here, it means understanding their problem properly: being curious enough to ask the second and third question, listening more than you talk, and knowing by the end of the call what's actually going wrong for them, on which project, and why it matters now. It also means only offering a solution to people who genuinely want or need to fix it. If they don't, you thank them and move on. Get that right and the meeting follows naturally, and it's one worth having.

How the team is set up

You'll sit in the UK sales team, working day to day with an Account Executive who takes your meetings forward to a free launch and then a contract. You open the door, they win the deal, and you succeed together. You'll work with a CRM, a dialler and call recording, plus a playbook, a library of calls that have actually won, and AI call-prep tools built for how we sell.

Where you'll work

Remote, anywhere in the UK, with the chance to attend industry events in person in the near future.

Why it's worth it

  • A career in a market that's only just going digital:around $10 trillion is spent on construction every year, yet it's one of the least digitised industries in the world, and spending on construction management software is forecast to nearly double by 2030. People who can sell software and genuinely understand construction are rare. Learn both here, and you'll have skills that stay in demand for years as the industry catches up, and you'll be helping it work better along the way.
  • Senior conversations from the start: you'll be speaking directly to leaders at some of the UK's biggest construction firms, not working your way through gatekeepers.
  • Coaching that knows the industry: weekly reviews and coaching from people who've lived and breathed construction, on site, not just on the phones.
  • A playbook that works: built from calls that have won, so you're not starting from scratch.
  • Progression on merit: a proper conversation about your next step within a year, based on what you've shown.
  • You'll shape how we sell:what you learn and suggest makes it into the playbook.
  • A 4-day week:the same standards and targets, delivered in four days.

Your top responsibilities

  • Open doors:start proper conversations, every day, with the people who feel the problem and can decide.
  • Qualify properly: test the problem early, dig in before you pitch, and keep qualifying after the "yes".
  • Hand over cleanly:your CRM notes tell the story, so your Account Executive picks up exactly where you left off.
  • Be obsessed with your numbers: know them every day, track them weekly and act on what they tell you.
  • Raise the bar: once you're up to speed, share what's working, contribute to the playbook and help newer SDRs get better faster.

Your roadmap: your first 30 days and beyond

You bring the experience. We'll make sure you're selling the Shape way, with confidence, by week 3 or 4.

  • Before day 1, ready to go: your CRM, dialler, call recording and your own Shape login set up, so week 1 is spent learning.
  • Week 1, understand the why: the problems we solve, who for, and why it beats how contractors work today, with the product shown in action by Customer Success.
  • Week 2, build your pitch:write your first-call pitch, compare it with the winning calls in our library, get it reviewed, and make your first live calls if you're ready.
  • Weeks 3–4, up and running: calling daily with call reviews, booking your first meetings and handing them over properly.
  • By day 30:signed off as ready to call, every call in the library listened to, and your first measures reviewed with your manager.
  • Months 2–3, ramp:half the full target, with your own quality scorecard.
  • By the end of month 3, full target: the same target every SDR carries, in line with your probation period.
  • 6–12 months, step up:own a set of key accounts or a segment, help refine our messaging and set the bar for newer SDRs, with a clear path to Account Executive or SDR Team Lead.

Why three months is realistic: it's quick by industry standards, and that's deliberate. You won't be figuring it out alone. You'll have a playbook built from calls that have won, regular call reviews, weekly 1:1s and your own scorecard. Our best have been fully up to speed in a month. Training never stops at day 30, however experienced you are.

How you'll be measured

Good numbers come from good conversations. You'll have your own monthly scorecard, built around three questions: are you reaching the right people, are those calls turning into real conversations, and are those conversations turning into meetings worth having?

Your main target is qualified meetings attended: meetings that actually take place, where your Account Executive agrees there's a genuine opportunity. You'll know your numbers from day one, and we'll go through them with you every week.

No grey areas: you and your Account Executive are partners. What makes a meeting qualified is written down and shared, so you'll both know where the bar is. If you ever see one differently, you talk it through with the call recording in front of you. Decisions come down to facts, never opinion or politics.

What our best are doing:booking around 20% more meetings than target, turning conversations into meetings at nearly double the minimum rate, and keeping more people on the phone than our standard asks for, with almost every meeting qualified (92%) because they do the basics properly. That's the bar, and we'll help you get there.

A start-up at a pivotal point

If you've ever wanted to join a start-up right as it takes off, this is that moment. We're past the early days: our sales process is working, customers are launching with us and we know what good looks like. Now we're growing, and the people who join now will shape what comes next.

You get the start-up stuff, the exciting and the real: things move fast, you'll build as you go, your ideas get heard (and actually used), and you'll see the impact of your work every week. We hold ourselves to a high standard, back each other up and enjoy it along the way.

We're looking for people in it for the long term, and that works both ways. We'll invest in you with weekly coaching, structured training and progression on merit. In return, we want people who want to build something with us over years, not a stepping stone.

Your Capabilities

Must haves:

  • Proven outbound experience at a senior level: 2+ years of phone-led B2B prospecting into directors and heads of department, in a complex sale where several people are involved in each decision and sales cycles are longer.
  • A track record:you've been at or above target for most of the last 12 months, and you can show it.
  • Your own toughest critic:you can listen back to your own call and say what worked, what didn't and what you'd change.
  • A forever learner: however good you get, you never feel you know enough. You're always looking for the next thing to learn, and you go after it.

What we look for in you

  • Numbers-obsessed:you know why your numbers are what they are: not just dials and meetings booked, but how many showed, how many qualified and what you changed when one dipped.
  • Quality over volume:you'd choose a better conversation over a faster one. You test the problem before you pitch and keep qualifying after the "yes".
  • Quick on your feet, and a genuine listener:calls rarely go word perfect. You think creatively, react to what's actually been said, and listen to understand. Construction people can spot a fake a mile off, and so can we.
  • A strategist who takes action:you plan who to call, when and why, run your own day and keep your CRM honest. Then you act, without waiting to be told.
  • You've done your homework: you understand the problems construction teams face, and you can say clearly why construction and why this job.
  • A sponge, with no ego:however good you are, you soak up how we do things here and take feedback on your calls. Egos stay at the door, on both sides.

Why experience alone isn't enough

Experience gets you an interview, but it isn't what gets you the job. We've seen numbers-first sales cultures produce full calendars and empty pipelines, so we're looking for experience that's still coachable.

Nice to have (if you don't have it now, you will after joining)

  • Experience selling into construction, engineering or infrastructure.
  • Having helped build or improve a playbook, sequence or messaging.
  • Start-up or scale-up experience.
  • Experience managing your own pipeline in a CRM and using diallers and other sales tools.
  • Construction site experience, or time working in the industry.
  • Full-cycle (360) sales experience, from first call through to close.

Shape isn't the place for you if any of the following is true:

  • You'd rather set the strategy and have someone else build the campaigns
  • You'd rather report on activity than be measured on booked demos
  • You want an easy role without much challenge
  • You like to be the smartest person in the room
  • You don't like continuously receiving honest candid feedback
  • You prefer to do your own thing rather than work with a team

Benefits

The Standard Stuff

  • Health Insurance Scheme. Comprehensive private health coverage - for you and your family. Because your well-being is our priority
  • Bonus Scheme. As a permanent member of the team, you’ll share in our success. Our annual bonus is designed to reward both the now and the future - with a flexible mix of cash and high-growth equity that you choose. Bonuses are discretionary and based on performance
  • Professional body membership. One fee covered per year - so you can stay connected to your field and develop your craft

The Life-Changing Stuff

  • In-house coaching: Regular 1:1 coaching sessions, fully confidential, to help you navigate challenges, build self-awareness, and grow intentionally - professionally and as a human being
  • Flexibility: Getting things done is what really matters, not what time of day you do it. That means you don’t have to ask permission for things like picking up your kids or going to the doctor, just keep your team in the loop if you think they will be affected.
  • Grow your whole self: Our leaders are more like coaches and one of our main objectives is to give 5 years’ worth of learning and development for every 1 year with us. You have a coach, mentor, well-being therapist and a development-orientated environment: That’s literally what our vision is all about and the primary reason Laminar exists.
  • Be surrounded by the best: We only hire and retain the very best people. You might be used to being the smartest in the room but that won’t be the case in Laminar. You will be surrounded by people you can learn from. We are 100% meritocratic so fast progression is the norm. You will be supported to excel in whichever areas you are most interested in! With Laminar, development is unbounded
  • Long-term impact: We are focused on solving the biggest issues in construction project delivery in a way that can spread and outlast us

Important! Applying properly

Apply with your CV and a cover letter answering these three questions:
  1. Why construction, and why this job?
  2. What do you think are the biggest problems facing the people we'd have you calling?
  3. What's the number you're most proud of from your current or last role, and why?

A note on AI: yes, we use it every day, and you're welcome to use it to research or sharpen your thinking. But right now this is about getting to know you, so make sure your answers sound like you. There are no wrong answers. We'd rather hear what you really think, even if it's not completely accurate.

What happens next

Every application is read by the people you'd work with. We move quickly, and you'll hear back at every stage. After an initial screen, there are three stages:

  • Meet and greet:we get to know each other and make sure we're aligned on expectations, both yours and ours.
  • Mock call with feedback:a role-play cold call. We'll give you feedback and see how you use it. We'll prepare you for this, and nobody expects it to be perfect.
  • Meet the team, then a decision:meet the people you'd be working with every day. Then we'll give you a clear answer either way, with feedback.

jobs.title: Finance Analyst
jobs.excerpt: Flex is building AI-native financial services for business owners.
jobs.description:
Flex is building AI-native financial services for business owners.
We’re re-architecting the entire financial system for entrepreneurs—from the first dollar a business earns to how that value compounds, moves, and is ultimately spent in real life. Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, and financial operations—rebuilt from the ground up as a single, intelligent system. Flex is the full financial home for ambitious owners.
Since launching publicly in September 2023, Flex has scaled from zero to nine-figure annualized revenue, with a clear path to profitability by late 2026. We move fast, ship relentlessly, and operate with extreme ownership.
Our customers are affluent business owners ($3–$200M in revenue)—the backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. They’re stuck with outdated banks and fragmented tools. We’re replacing all of it. The opportunity is massive: a ~$1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. Our ambition is to build a $100B+ company by delivering a product that is fundamentally better—not incrementally improved.
Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt.
- Mission-critical problems: We build software that directly controls how money moves at scale.
- High bar, low ego: Small teams, exceptional people, real ownership.
- Speed over comfort: We prioritize execution, quality, clarity, and results.
- Enduring impact: What we’re building will define how a generation of owners runs their businesses.

Team & Locations

We hire exceptional people who want to build hard things and see their work matter immediately. Roles are available in: San Francisco, Miami, New York, and fully remote.

Flex Fuels Ambition.

About Us

    This is a ground-floor seat on a small finance team, and it's a genuinely embedded one. Most of your week will be spent with our go-to-market org — reporting on what our growth spend is actually returning, and acting as the finance counterpart on deal structure and pricing. The rest goes to the budget cycle, where you'll sit with department leads to build and defend their plans.

    We're hiring for judgment and speed, not years served. If you're two years out of a banking analyst program, or a strong new grad who models well and writes clearly, you're the profile. You'll report to our Director of FP&A and get real exposure to the exec team.

What You'll Do

    Be the finance partner to go-to-market

  • Own reporting on the ROI of our growth investments — by channel, campaign, and segment — so the team knows what's working and what to cut

  • Run Deal Desk: serve as the finance liaison on pricing, deal structure, and non-standard terms, and be the person go-to-market pulls in before a deal gets committed

  • Build and maintain the customer and growth economics that inform how we invest in acquisition

  • Sit in go-to-market's meetings, not just their inbox — translate their questions into analysis and hand back a recommendation instead of a spreadsheet

    • Run the budget cycle with the teams

  • Partner with department leads through quarterly budget and headcount planning — collect inputs, pressure-test them, and translate them into the plan

  • Track spend against budget, surface drift before it compounds, and flag what needs a decision

  • Build the analysis behind headcount, vendor, and resourcing calls — payback, cost-to-serve, build-vs-buy

    • Support forecasting and reporting

  • Support the monthly forecast cycle: pull and reconcile actuals, build the variance analysis, and draft the commentary that explains what moved and why

  • Maintain the schedules and drivers that feed the company operating model, working alongside the Director of FP&A

  • Help assemble the monthly and quarterly reporting packages for leadership, the board, and lenders

    • Automate anything you do twice

  • Replace recurring manual work with something durable — AI workflows, queries, dashboards, templates — so next month it takes minutes

  • Bring rigor to automated output: reconcile it, stress it, and know where it breaks before someone else finds out

Requirements

  • 0–2 years in FP&A, strategic finance, investment banking, consulting, Big 4, or a comparably analytical role — exceptional new grads welcome

  • Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, accounting, engineering, mathematics, or another quantitative field

  • You build financial models from a blank sheet. Advanced Excel or Google Sheets is table stakes here, not a bullet point

  • Hands-on exposure to a real budgeting or forecasting cycle

  • AI is already the default in how you work, and you have the judgment to go with it: a reliable instinct for when a machine-generated answer is wrong, and the discipline to check before you forward it

  • You write clearly. You can compress a 40-tab model into three sentences a founder can act on

  • Extreme attention to detail, and comfort operating in ambiguity at speed — priorities here change faster than the plan does

  • Based in the US

    • Nice to Haves

  • SQL — you can pull your own data instead of filing a ticket

  • Python, or comparable scripting for analysis and automation

  • BI and analytics tooling (Looker, Tableau, Power BI, Hex) and modern planning tools (Pigment, Cube, Aleph, NetSuite)

  • Fintech, banking, or lending background

Why Join Us

Build something generational — Capture the full lifecycle of money for ambitious business owners.
Work on real money, real risk — Payments, credit, and banking at serious scale.
Solve hard problems — AI, underwriting, compliance, and global finance from first principles.
True ownership — Small teams, high trust, real accountability.
Founder-level exposure — Direct access to leadership, customers, and investors.
High bar, high taste — Move fast without cutting corners.
Elite peers — People here are builders, not tourists.
Real upside — Meaningful equity if you help build something big.

jobs.title: AI Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Newsweek is the global media organization that has earned audience time and trust for more than 90 years.
jobs.description:
Newsweek is the global media organization that has earned audience time and trust for more than 90 years. Newsweek reaches 100 million people each month with thought-provoking news, opinion, images, graphics, and video delivered across a dozen print and digital platforms. Headquartered in New York City, Newsweek also publishes international editions in EMEA and Asia.

Frontend Software Engineer
(React / Next.js)

Company: Newsweek

About the Role

Newsweek is looking for a Frontend Software Engineer to help build, maintain, and enhance the digital experiences that serve our readers across our publishing platforms.

In this role, you will focus primarily on React, Next.js, TypeScript, and modern frontend engineering, developing fast, responsive, accessible, and scalable web applications that deliver content to a large and diverse audience.

You will work on a modern, API-driven frontend architecture, building reusable components, integrating content and backend services, and optimizing the performance and reliability of our digital products.

We are looking for an engineer who combines strong frontend fundamentals with a modern, AI-assisted approach to software development. You should be comfortable leveraging AI tools to accelerate development, improve code quality, solve problems, and streamline engineering workflows while maintaining ownership of the solutions you deliver.

The ideal candidate has solid experience building production-grade applications with React and Next.js, understands modern web performance and frontend architecture, and can collaborate effectively with design, product, backend, and engineering teams.

What You'll Do

Frontend Development & Architecture

  • Develop, maintain, and enhance modern web applications using React, Next.js, and TypeScript.
  • Build modular, reusable, and maintainable UI components that follow established design systems and engineering best practices.
  • Implement responsive layouts and intuitive user experiences across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.
  • Integrate frontend applications with backend APIs, including REST and GraphQL, to deliver dynamic, content-driven experiences.
  • Work with server-side rendering (SSR), static generation (SSG), and other modern rendering techniques to optimize application performance and content delivery.
  • Collaborate with backend engineers to define efficient API contracts and data requirements.
  • Contribute to frontend architecture decisions, ensuring scalability, maintainability, and consistency across digital products.

Performance, Accessibility & User Experience

  • Optimize frontend performance, including page load times, rendering efficiency, and resource utilization.
  • Monitor and improve Core Web Vitals, including loading performance, responsiveness, and visual stability.
  • Apply modern performance optimization techniques such as code splitting, lazy loading, image optimization, and caching.
  • Build accessible interfaces following web accessibility standards and best practices.
  • Ensure consistent functionality across modern browsers and devices.
  • Implement frontend solutions that support technical SEO, structured data, and search engine discoverability.
  • Identify and resolve frontend performance issues, rendering problems, and user experience inconsistencies.
  • Collaborate with product and design teams to translate requirements and designs into polished, reliable user interfaces.

AI-Assisted Development & Engineering Productivity

  • Effectively leverage AI-powered development tools to accelerate coding, debugging, testing, documentation, and code reviews.
  • Use AI to assist with component development, refactoring, performance analysis, technical research, and implementation of new features.
  • Critically evaluate, test, and validate AI-generated code to ensure correctness, security, accessibility, performance, and maintainability.
  • Identify opportunities to improve engineering productivity through AI-assisted development workflows and automation.
  • Continuously explore emerging AI development capabilities and adopt practical approaches that improve software delivery without compromising engineering standards.
  • Follow company security and data privacy policies when using AI tools, ensuring sensitive information and proprietary code are handled appropriately.

Engineering & Collaboration

  • Write clean, maintainable, well-documented, and testable frontend code.
  • Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and architectural decisions.
  • Develop and maintain automated tests to improve application reliability and prevent regressions.
  • Follow established CI/CD, version control, and deployment practices.
  • Collaborate closely with backend engineers, designers, product managers, and other stakeholders.
  • Take ownership of assigned features and technical improvements from initial development through production release.
  • Troubleshoot production issues and contribute to ongoing improvements in code quality, development workflows, and application reliability.

Required Qualifications

  • Strong professional experience developing and maintaining production web applications using React and Next.js.
  • Strong proficiency in JavaScript (ES6+), TypeScript, HTML5, and modern CSS.
  • Solid understanding of React fundamentals, including hooks, component composition, state management, and rendering behavior.
  • Experience with Next.js routing, data fetching, server-side rendering, static generation, and modern application architecture.
  • Experience integrating frontend applications with RESTful APIs and GraphQL.
  • Strong understanding of responsive design, cross-browser compatibility, and accessibility best practices.
  • Experience optimizing web applications for performance, including Core Web Vitals, asset loading, and rendering efficiency.
  • Familiarity with modern styling approaches such as CSS Modules, SCSS, or utility-first CSS frameworks.
  • Experience building reusable components and working with shared design systems.
  • Familiarity with frontend testing frameworks and tools such as Jest, React Testing Library, Playwright, or Cypress.
  • Experience with Git, code reviews, and CI/CD development workflows.
  • Practical experience using AI-assisted development tools, such as GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or equivalent solutions, to improve development efficiency and code quality.
  • Demonstrated ability to critically review, validate, and improve AI-generated code rather than relying on it without verification.
  • Understanding of responsible AI usage in software development, including security, intellectual property, and data privacy considerations.
  • Strong troubleshooting, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced development environment.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building applications using headless CMS platforms, particularly WordPress.
  • Familiarity with WPGraphQL, WordPress REST APIs, or other content delivery APIs.
  • Experience with high-traffic, content-heavy websites or digital publishing platforms.
  • Knowledge of advanced Next.js features, including server components, streaming, incremental static regeneration, and caching strategies.
  • Experience with CDN technologies, edge caching, and frontend content delivery optimization.
  • Experience with frontend monitoring, error tracking, and performance analysis tools.
  • Familiarity with SEO requirements for news and publishing websites, including structured data and metadata management.
  • Experience integrating analytics, advertising, subscriptions, or audience engagement technologies.
  • Knowledge of web security best practices, including content security policies, XSS prevention, and secure API integration.
  • Experience with visual regression testing, component libraries, or Storybook.
  • Familiarity with cloud platforms and containerized application deployments.
  • Experience improving engineering processes through AI-assisted automation, testing, or development workflows.
  • Previous experience working with digital publishing, media, or other large-scale consumer-facing web applications.

What Success Looks Like

  • You deliver fast, reliable, and engaging frontend experiences that serve Newsweek's readers across devices.
  • You build reusable, maintainable components that accelerate development and support consistent user experiences.
  • You continuously improve application performance, accessibility, SEO, and Core Web Vitals.
  • You integrate frontend applications effectively with backend APIs and content management systems.
  • You effectively use AI-assisted development tools to improve productivity, accelerate delivery, and maintain high code quality.
  • You demonstrate sound engineering judgment, including the ability to recognize when AI-generated solutions require modification or should not be used.
  • You take ownership of your work and collaborate effectively with product, design, backend, and engineering teams.
  • You contribute to a high-quality codebase through testing, documentation, code reviews, and thoughtful engineering practices.

Newsweek is an equal opportunity employer. We seek employees of diverse backgrounds and are committed to providing an inclusive, equitable and respectful workplace.

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

As the Cardiology Medical Director, you will oversee the strategic direction of GE HealthCare's Americas Medical Affairs cardiology related activities, including society partnerships, advisory boards, coordination with Global Medical team and contribution to the cardiology and imaging portfolio. You will partner with Global Medical Directors, Medical Science Liaisons, Medical Information Officers, and other personnel to serve as medical experts and points of contact for cross-functional stakeholders in the Americas region and ensure execution of tactical plans. You will explore and develop new opportunities for collaboration, in addition to managing existing partnerships. You will work closely with your Medical Affairs colleagues, cross-functional colleagues, and external key opinion leaders (KOLs) to gain an understanding of the scientific landscape, glean clinical insights, and communicate information to key stakeholders.

GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

Job Description

Essential Responsibilities

    • Lead, develop, and implement overall medical strategy and associated activities for GEHC’s cardiology products throughout product lifecycles, primarily iodinated contrast media.
    • Serve as a leader in aggregating scientific, clinical, and technical customer-focused insights and strategic perspectives related to PDx imaging products and initiatives for the Americas region
    • Drive scientific exchange related to GEHC’s products in the clinical community by forming networks between KOLs to generate clinical evidence
    • Identify external clinical opinions, perceptions and trends that influence GE Healthcare’s product and innovation strategies, and where warranted, develop appropriate mitigating strategies in partnership with applicable GEHC functions
    • Provide medical leadership to the cross-functional brand and product teams
    • Align with medical affairs colleagues on cross-functional team representation with the goal of developing and implementing integrated clinical and commercial strategies for GEHC’s products
    • Engage key scientific societies and establish strong relationships that enhance our corporate image, as well as increase understanding of GEHC’s cardiology products
    • Based on product priorities and research strategies, establish and drive a scientific agenda, by engaging researchers through GEHC’s activities and partnerships, including where appropriate, conducting studies that lead to publications in support of GEHC’s product objectives
    • Work with key internal stakeholders to ensure GEHC is sufficiently engaging external KOLs, academics, research partners, societies, and other organizations as we create strategies for product development, innovation, evidence generation and research
    • Coordinate and manage advisory boards to gather clinical insights as well as round tables to enable the sharing of clinical knowledge with and between external stakeholders
    • Lead review and provide medical input on promotional and other materials in accordance with appropriate regulations
    • Partners cross-functionally with Commercial, Marketing, Market Access, Regulatory Affairs, R&D, Quality, Pharmacovigilance and Medical Information to drive compliant execution and support business objectives
    • Must live in the United States and be willing to travel extensively (up to 30% of the time), based on needs of the business
    • As part of US Medical team, occasional weekend or extended work hours may be required

Qualifications/Requirements


    • Advanced scientific or clinical degree required, such as MD, DO, PharmD, PhD, or other terminal doctorate; relevant Cardiology clinical experience preferred
    • Minimum 7 years of combined clinical and/or pharmaceutical or healthcare industry experience, including at least 5 years in Medical Affairs or related scientific roles
    • Demonstrated leadership experience, including line management or functional leadership of medical teams, is strongly preferred
    • Strong understanding of Medical Affairs, Pharmacovigilance, Medical Information, compliance, regulatory requirements and local healthcare systems
    • Experience in budget management, stakeholder engagement, scientific communication, material review and evidence-generation activities

Eligibility Requirement


GE will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States for this opening. Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen (as applicable).

Job Description

A bit about this role:

As a Community Guide Case Manager, you will play a vital role in supporting our most vulnerable members, many dual-eligible for Medicare and Medicaid, through their most complex and serious situations, such as housing loss, safety concerns, and suspected abuse or neglect. When these challenges arise, cross-functional teams refer members to us for comprehensive support. As a Case Manager, you will build trusting, ongoing relationships with members and caregivers, create person-centered care plans, and remove barriers until goals are met. Reporting to a Community Guide Supervisor, you will use sound judgment and deep knowledge of community, behavioral health, and benefits resources to help members stay safe and stable, and you will strengthen the whole team by consulting on complex cases and coaching peers. This role is ideal for those dedicated to walking alongside members through their hardest moments as they navigate complex healthcare networks, community initiatives, and support resources.


Your Responsibilities and Impact will include:

  • Manage a caseload of members with complex, ongoing needs, building person-centered care plans with members and caregivers and following through until goals are met.
  • Independently handle serious situations, including members expressing suicidal ideation, chronically unhoused members, housing loss or facility discharge, and suspected abuse, neglect, or exploitation that requires an APS referral, following crisis and safety protocols.
  • Lead emotionally complex conversations with members and caregivers, guiding them toward decisions rather than only sharing information.
  • Remove barriers by connecting members directly to housing, behavioral health, long-term care, community, and benefits resources, and confirm that services were received.
  • Coordinate with providers, teams across the health plan and Devoted Medical, community organizations, and government agencies so members don’t have to repeat their story.
  • Anticipate risks before they become crises, look for root causes of recurring issues, and bring member patterns and proposed solutions to team leadership.
  • Strengthen the team by leading or joining case conferences, consulting on complex cases, and coaching teammates on uncovering members’ underlying needs.
  • Support the team’s core work, including common needs and benefit applications, during high-volume periods.
  • Document thoroughly and track your own caseload outcomes, adjusting your approach before a leader needs to ask.

Required skills and experience:

  • 2+ years of case management, care coordination, or social services experience supporting people with complex needs.
  • Sound judgment in high-risk situations (crisis, safety concerns, suspected abuse or neglect), including knowing when and how to escalate.
  • Strong verbal and written communication: you break down complex information clearly and handle emotionally sensitive conversations with composure.
  • Strong organization to manage an ongoing caseload, competing priorities, and accurate documentation across multiple systems.
  • Resilience and a growth mindset: you seek feedback, stay steady through change, and keep showing up for members when resources are limited, ability to work outside your job description in some instances, including the potential for taking inbound calls.
  • Comfort with technology, including learning new systems and AI-enabled tools quickly.
  • Ability to work an assigned schedule within hours of operation (8:30am–8:00pm Eastern), supporting the Mountain or Pacific time zone if needed.


Desired skills and experience:


  • Degree in social work (BSW, MSW, LSW, LMSW, or LCSW) or a related field preferred but not required; equivalent demonstrated experience is considered.

  • Experience working with older adults, Medicare Advantage, or Medicaid programs.

jobs.title: Retention Specialist
jobs.excerpt: Summary of Job: Reporting to the Chief Delivery and Experience Officer, the Retention Specialist drives family retention across Valenture Institute's online offerings.
jobs.description:
Summary of Job:

Reporting to the Chief Delivery and Experience Officer, the Retention Specialist drives family retention across Valenture Institute's online offerings. Their mandate is to reduce withdrawals and retain families, making sure the families who join us choose to stay enrolled.

The Retention Specialist owns the turnaround of withdrawal requests. They engage guardians who are considering withdrawal, understand what is driving the decision, and deliver a credible solution that enables the learner to stay enrolled. They take personal ownership of each case, from reaching out and rebuilding confidence to agreeing the right solution, coordinating support and following through until the outcome is confirmed. They also act early, using data to spot families at risk and reach them before they decide to leave.

Across all families, the Retention Specialist uses data to find what drives withdrawals, and works with leaders across the business to address it at scale. Success means fewer withdrawals, and more families choosing to continue their journey with us.

Key responsibilities:

Early indicators and proactive retention

  • Partner with the Data team to identify the early indicators of withdrawal and build retention dashboards and reporting that track risk, trends and outcomes, refining both over time.
  • Monitor this data closely to identify every at-risk family early, and engage each one meaningfully to understand their concerns and strengthen their connection with us before they decide to leave.
  • Design and test proactive interventions, measure which ones reduce withdrawals, and scale what works.
  • Document clear, repeatable processes for identifying and supporting at-risk families, so that early intervention happens consistently throughout the year.

Withdrawal requests and retention conversations

  • Own every withdrawal request submitted by a family through to a confirmed outcome, responding promptly and keeping a clear next step in place for every open case.
  • Partner closely with the Support team, who often hear first when a family is thinking of leaving: agree workflows that route any intention to leave to you quickly, including one flagged by our AI support assistant, and equip Support Advisors to help retain families.
  • Engage guardians by phone, email, WhatsApp or video, choosing the most effective channel, and review the family's account, previous interactions and learner engagement before each conversation.
  • Use thoughtful questioning and active listening to uncover the real reasons a family wants to leave, considering both the guardian's priorities and the learner's circumstances, so that every family feels heard, understood and valued.
  • Explain the value of our offerings clearly, and address concerns and objections with accurate, relevant information that is consistent with our policies, so that families can make an informed decision.
  • Work proactively with leaders across the business to agree on the retention levers available to families, based on what you learn about why families leave.
  • Agree the right solution with each family, drawing on these levers within your agreed authority. Where a family’s concern needs another team’s input, work with that team to shape a solution, for example with Finance where affordability is driving the decision, or with the Delivery team where there is a concern about the learner’s experience.
  • Where leaving is the right outcome for the learner, recognise it and make sure the family has a respectful exit.
  • Keep accurate, confidential case records in line with POPIA, covering reasons for leaving, communication history, support offered and outcome, and update the withdrawal request whenever a family's decision changes.

Complaints management and follow-through

  • Handle any complaints raised in retention conversations calmly, using effective de-escalation techniques to turn difficult conversations into constructive ones.
  • Take ownership of every complaint raised with you: log it, take it to the right team (for example Finance, Well-being & Engagement or Learner Success), and follow it through to resolution.
  • Escalate unresolved issues with clear context, a recommended action and a required response date.
  • Coordinate the support agreed with each family across the relevant teams.

Insights and improvement at scale

  • Help build and refine our retention strategy, using data and what families tell us to decide where to focus.
  • Track and analyse withdrawal reasons, retention outcomes, complaint themes, unresolved barriers and the effectiveness of interventions, and report on them regularly to leadership.
  • Bring the voice of families to leadership, sharing clear feedback on what families need and where their experience falls short.
  • Identify the recurring themes behind withdrawals and work with the leaders responsible, for example in Product, Support or Finance, to agree how to fix the underlying causes.
  • Follow each agreed improvement through to completion, and measure whether it reduces withdrawals.

AI and retention tools

  • Own and continuously improve the AI tools and agents that support our retention work, shaping how they work alongside human follow-up so that every family gets the right response at the right time.
  • Test new AI tools against specific use cases, such as predicting risk or personalising outreach, and build those that work into our retention strategy.
  • Use AI to work efficiently day to day, checking its output and keeping human judgement for sensitive conversations and decisions.

Realities of the role:

  • Valenture Institute is a fast-paced startup. We are not a traditional school! We are reimagining schooling and precedent needs to be adopted only where it has proven to have great results. If you think that traditional schools have it all figured out, this is probably not the right role for you.
  • Collaboration is the name of the game. We operate in highly specialised teams, and our ability to deliver an excellent student experience is premised on our team’s ability to collaborate, value the contributions of their teammates (including those in other teams) and see the value in the “rubbing of minds”. If you do not find value in having your ideas interrogated or others weighing in on how things could foreseeably be done, you are unlikely to enjoy the role. Similarly, if you are not comfortable with other teams being accountable for different parts of the learning experience, you are unlikely to find this environment to be a good fit for you.
  • This role works at two levels. In one day you may spend the morning in conversation with guardians who are weighing up whether to stay, and the afternoon studying a dashboard for the patterns behind those calls or agreeing a fix with another team. You need to stay calm and warm in difficult conversations, and to follow through on every commitment you make. You also need to step back from individual cases and see the bigger picture. If you prefer to work at only one of these levels, you are unlikely to enjoy this role.

jobs.description:
About Tires-Easy

Every day, Tires-Easy ships more than 10,000 tires across the United States, changing how people shop for tires and reshaping the $60B replacement tire market through a faster, smarter approach to automotive e-commerce. We pair deep coverage of top-name and budget-friendly brands with a nationwide drop-ship network, and we use technology, automation, and AI to make every step faster and easier for our customers.

Our leadership team comes from outside traditional tire retail, and it shows. We operate in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment with a strong emphasis on operational excellence, accountability, and disciplined growth. Decisions take days, not quarters. We’re building a team that owns results, sees its impact quickly, and drives execution at scale. If you’re curious, action-oriented, and ready to help build a fast-growing business, apply now.

About the role

Turn promising ideas into products and features that improve the Tires Easy customer experience and business performance. You’ll work closely with senior stakeholders to prioritize the roadmap, and with our Data, Development, and Design teams to turn those priorities into delivered results.

You’ll take an idea from a napkin sketch or product requirements document through a proposal process that establishes the customer and market need, expected business impact, and resources required. With the team, you’ll validate assumptions, define scope, estimate effort and cost, and secure agreement on what to build. You’ll then own execution against the approved schedule, budget, and impact targets, through launch and follow-up measurement.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with broad ownership and direct access to senior stakeholders. You’ll become the day-to-day product partner for engineering and design, keeping decisions moving, resolving ambiguity, and surfacing the choices that need leadership input. Your work will give leaders the space to focus on higher-level strategy and planning.

We’re looking for someone who takes initiative, sets a high standard, and follows through. You notice what is missing, bring the right people together, make a clear recommendation, and stay accountable for the outcome. This role offers the scope and responsibility to appeal to a former founder or product leader who enjoys building with a small team and making a visible business impact.

Key responsibilities

  • Build and maintain a prioritized roadmap with senior stakeholders, balancing customer needs, market opportunity, expected impact, dependencies, and team capacity.
  • Turn early ideas and PRDs into decision-ready proposals covering the problem, target users and market, supporting evidence, alternatives, expected impact, assumptions, and success measures.
  • Partner with Data, Development, and Design to assess feasibility, estimate effort and cost, identify required resources, and define scope, milestones, and dependencies before committing to delivery.
  • Guide proposals through review and approval; make tradeoffs explicit and obtain agreement on scope, budget, resources, schedule, and the outcomes the investment should deliver.
  • Own day-to-day execution with engineering and design: clarify requirements, maintain priorities and acceptance criteria, unblock decisions, and coordinate work across teams.
  • Track delivery against the approved schedule and budget. Identify risks early, recommend scope or resource tradeoffs, and secure approval for material changes before they become surprises.
  • Use customer research, operational feedback, and analysis to improve requirements and user experience across e-commerce and internal workflows.
  • Partner with the Data team to establish baselines, define trustworthy metrics, instrument features, and evaluate results against the impact proposed.
  • Coordinate testing, release readiness, stakeholder communication, and adoption; follow through after launch and drive iteration when results fall short.
  • Give leadership concise updates on progress, spend, risks, decisions needed, and realized impact while taking ownership of routine product decisions within the agreed plan.

What success looks like in the first six months

  • Establish a roadmap agreed with senior stakeholders, with clear priorities, success measures, and a realistic view of team capacity.
  • Put a repeatable proposal process into use so investment decisions are supported by customer or market evidence, expected impact, and credible development estimates.
  • Take ownership of day-to-day product coordination with Data, Development, and Design, with clear decision boundaries and less routine escalation to leadership.
  • Deliver agreed priority features against approved schedules and budgets, measure their impact against the proposal, and act on gaps between expected and actual results.

Eligibility requirements

  • Able to conduct stakeholder discussions, read technical and business material, and write clear product documentation in English.

Skills & experience

  • 4+ years of product management or equivalent founder/operator experience, with a record of independently leading complex software initiatives from discovery through launch and measurable results.
  • Strong commercial judgment: assess customer and market needs, quantify expected impact, and recommend where to invest limited time and resources.
  • Experience partnering with senior stakeholders to prioritize a roadmap, challenge assumptions constructively, and reach decisions when priorities conflict.
  • Proven ability to turn ambiguous ideas into clear proposals, product requirements, acceptance criteria, and executable plans.
  • Hands-on delivery ownership across engineering, design, and data teams, including scope, schedules, budgets, dependencies, and release coordination.
  • Technical fluency sufficient to discuss feasibility, systems, data dependencies, and implementation tradeoffs with engineers.
  • Strong usage of AI tools such as Claude and Codex to analyze data, build prototypes, and accelerate work. Strong understanding of when to use AI, when not to, and how to use it to accelerate high-quality work.
  • Comfort working with analytics and the Data team to establish baselines, evaluate experiments, and distinguish shipped features from demonstrated business impact.
  • High initiative and persistence: identify problems, make progress without detailed direction, close decisions, and take responsibility for results.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain tradeoffs and secure cooperation without direct management authority.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience.

Nice to have

  • Founder, early-stage product leader, or comparable experience taking a product from an initial idea to customers with limited resources.
  • Experience in e-commerce, marketplaces, distribution, or other businesses with complex catalog, pricing, inventory, supplier, or order workflows.
  • Experience using SQL, product analytics, experimentation, or prototyping tools to test assumptions and accelerate decisions.
  • Practical use of AI tools to support research, analysis, prototyping, or product delivery, with independent verification of outputs.

L’école d’art appliqué EDAA, établissement privé d’enseignement à distance, crée une nouvelle formation complète en motion design.

Notre ambition : permettre aux élèves de comprendre les principes du mouvement et de les appliquer à des productions graphiques et à des personnages animés, grâce à des exemples concrets et à des démonstrations progressives.

Nous recherchons un animateur ou une animatrice 2D pour créer les animations de référence de la formation et transmettre sa pratique d’After Effects et de l’animation de personnage.

🚀Vos missions

En collaboration avec le coordinateur pédagogique, vous concevez les exemples et les exercices qui permettront aux élèves de comprendre, de reproduire et d’analyser un mouvement.

Vous serez chargé de :

  • Créer des exemples animés illustrant la pesanteur, le poids, la matière et l’intention d’un personnage : rebonds, sauts, appuis, déformations et actions courtes.

  • Livrer les scènes de départ, les poses principales, les étapes intermédiaires et les animations de référence dans des projets éditables et organisés.

  • Préparer des personnages articulés avec Duik et concevoir des actions adaptées à un apprentissage progressif.

  • Enregistrer des démonstrations commentées dans After Effects, en décomposant les manipulations et en montrant l’effet des réglages sur le mouvement.

  • Rédiger des analyses de mouvement et relire les passages techniques préparés par le coordinateur pédagogique pour en valider l’exactitude et la clarté.

  • Animer les plans du générique et de la vidéo explicative à partir des storyboards, animatiques et illustrations conçus avec la direction artistique.

  • Concevoir les exercices et devoirs d’animation, les fichiers élèves, les références de correction et les critères d’évaluation.

  • Définir avec la direction artistique les critères d’évaluation des projets communs.

Vous avez animé des éléments graphiques et des personnages dans des productions finalisées. Vous savez donner du poids et une intention à une action par les poses, le rythme, les espacements, les trajectoires, les appuis et les déformations.

Vous maîtrisez After Effects, en particulier les images clés, l’éditeur de graphiques, le parentage et les contrôleurs. Vous savez préparer un personnage articulé et réaliser une action courte avec Duik.

Vous avez l’habitude de travailler à partir d’un storyboard, d’une animatique et d’illustrations fournis par une direction artistique. Vous savez conserver les étapes de fabrication, organiser un projet et rassembler les médias nécessaires à sa reprise.

Vous savez repérer une erreur de mouvement, proposer une correction précise et en expliquer l’effet à un débutant. Une expérience d’accompagnement, de tutoriel commenté ou de correction de travaux d’animation est appréciée.

L’EDAA intègre les outils d’intelligence artificielle lorsque leur usage est pertinent. Votre regard sur leur place dans la production et l’apprentissage de l’animation pourra également nourrir les échanges avec l’équipe pédagogique.

  • Volume, calendrier et rémunération : à définir selon le périmètre de la mission, en intégrant les essais, les reprises et les temps de collaboration.

Vous souhaitez transmettre votre pratique et contribuer à la création d’une formation complète en motion design ? Nous serions ravis de découvrir vos animations.

About Wellspring

Wellspring is the global leader in innovation management and technology scouting software. Leading corporations such as J&J, SoftBank and Panasonic, along with many of the world's top universities, use our platform to scout disruptive technologies, find co-development partners, manage their innovation and R&D portfolios, and run R&D operations globally.

We're a VC-backed enterprise software company headquartered in Chicago, with teams across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Japan. We've grown more than 25% year over year, mostly through direct sales. Now we're investing in a far more sophisticated sales and marketing engine to aim much higher.

That's why we're hiring a Senior Growth Account Executive. If you're driven by results and want to do well in a fast-paced, achievement-oriented environment, you'll find the scope and support here to do the best work of your career.

This role is open to candidates based in the United States.

About the role
The world's most innovative companies, in consumer goods, food and beverage, chemicals, manufacturing and life sciences, use Wellspring to decide which ideas to fund, manage their product and R&D portfolios, and get new products to market faster. As a Senior Growth Account Executive on our Innovation Management team, you'll own a portfolio of seven-figure named enterprise accounts. You'll become a trusted advisor to the leaders responsible for their growth pipeline.

This is not a maintenance role. You'll help customers extend Wellspring across more business units, regions and stages of the innovation lifecycle, from idea capture and front-end innovation through stage-gate execution, portfolio management and resource planning. You'll build the business case, close the expansion, and give customers a single connected view of their innovation investments. A collaborative Customer Success, Presales and Product team will back you.

What you'll do

  • Own executive relationships. Be the senior Wellspring voice for Chief Innovation Officers, CTOs, VPs of R&D, Heads of Product Portfolio Management, PMO and Strategy leaders. Earn a seat at the table where innovation investment decisions are made.
  • Drive account growth. Hit ambitious targets through upsell, cross-sell, renewals and adoption of new modules across your installed base. That includes idea management, portfolio and pipeline management, stage-gate/NPD governance, resource capacity planning and analytics.
  • Expand the footprint. Take Wellspring from one division or region to an enterprise-wide innovation standard, and find new use cases such as sustainability portfolios, technology roadmapping and open innovation.
  • Sell consultatively, end to end. Lead account planning, discovery, solution presentations and ROI-driven business cases built on outcomes customers care about: faster time to market, higher portfolio ROI, better resource allocation and fewer stalled projects. Then carry the deal through negotiation and close.
  • Partner with Customer Success. Work closely with CSMs to make sure customers see measurable value, and act early on expansion signals.
  • Run a disciplined business. Keep a clean, accurate pipeline in Salesforce, forecast with confidence, and use data to shape account strategy.
  • Rally the team. Work with Product, Marketing, Presales and Executive leadership to align messaging, campaigns and technical expertise behind your deals.
  • Know the market. Stay ahead of trends in product portfolio management, stage-gate and agile-hybrid NPD, AI in innovation, and R&D investment strategy. Articulate clearly why Wellspring wins against point solutions, spreadsheets and homegrown tools.
  • Be a visible industry voice. Represent Wellspring at customer user groups and at innovation and product development forums such as PDMA, Front End of Innovation and IRI, plus webinars and peer communities.

What success looks like

  • First 90 days: you've mapped the innovation stakeholders and processes across your top accounts and have a growth plan for each.
  • First 6 months: you've built and progressed meaningful expansion pipeline into new business units or modules.
  • First 12 months: you've met or exceeded your growth target, and customers see you as a strategic partner in how they run innovation.

What you bring

  • 5–8 years of enterprise SaaS sales or strategic account management, with a track record of closing deals over $100K ARR.
  • Experience selling to innovation, R&D, product management, PMO or strategy buyers. Knowledge of PPM, stage-gate/NPD or innovation management software is a strong plus.

  • Executive presence: you communicate, present and negotiate comfortably with senior leaders and build ROI cases that land.
  • Strategic, analytical thinking and a knack for solving complex, cross-functional customer problems.
  • Proficiency in Salesforce or an equivalent CRM; experience with Gong or HubSpot is a plus.
  • Bachelor's degree in business, engineering, science or a related field, or equivalent experience. An MBA or advanced degree is a plus.
  • Willingness to travel domestically, with occasional international trips.

How you work
You put the customer first and stay curious about how their business innovates. You bring creativity to complex problems and stay persistent and positive through long enterprise cycles. Wing offers drone delivery as a safe, fast, and sustainable solution for last mile logistics. In this role, you will provide comprehensive legal counseling across the entire employee lifecycle, including multi-state remote workforce compliance, recruiting, wage and hour, performance management, leaves of absence, accommodations, and employee relations. You will also spearhead Wing's contingent workforce and TVC (Temporary, Vendor, Contractor) governance strategy, partnering with Operations and Sourcing to mitigate co-employment risk across ground operations and technical staffing vendors, and advising on FAA/DOT Part 135/107 safety-sensitive workforce compliance and OSHA safety standards.

  • Author, maintain, and audit Wing’s employee handbooks, remote work policies, and disability/leave accommodation workflows, delivering engaging training programs for people managers.
  • Provide specialized counseling on FAA/DOT Part 135 and Part 107 employment standards, mandatory DOT drug and alcohol testing programs for safety-sensitive flight operations, and OSHA safety protocols across flight facilities.

jobs.description:
D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NASDAQ: QBTS) is a leader in the development and delivery of quantum computing systems, software, and services. It is the world’s first commercial supplier of quantum computers, and the first and only to offer dual-platform quantum computing products and services, spanning both annealing and gate-model quantum computing technologies. D-Wave’s mission is to help customers realize the value of quantum today through enterprise-grade systems available on-premises and via its Leap™ quantum cloud service, which offers 99.9% availability and uptime. More than 100 organizations across commercial, government, and research sectors trust D-Wave to address complex computational challenges using quantum computing. Learn more about realizing the value of quantum computing today and how D-Wave is shaping the quantum-driven industrial and societal advancements of tomorrow: .

About the role

An exciting opportunity for a Senior Solution Architect! In this role, you will build and deliver quantum optimization solutions for customer applications while working with delivery leads, applications developers, and other solutions architects within the professional services department. Additionally, you will work with our internal teams and external customers to review customer business problems, map these problems to D-Wave’s hybrid solvers and advanced quantum systems, formulate solutions, build and test prototypes, and build applications that run-in production for our customers.

What you'll do

  • Build customer applications on the D-Wave quantum computer and internal tools
  • Ensure successful delivery of projects to achieve business value for customers
  • Communicate capabilities with customers and ask probing questions to understand the problem and propose solutions
  • Gather requirements on customer use cases, lead brainstorming sessions, consult with customers on potential solutions, model use cases mathematically, and design and develop quantum hybrid applications
  • Build and maintain relationships with leaders across various groups within D-Wave
  • Share customer and project-related insights with D-Wave's tools and product teams and help prioritize new product features
  • Organize, prepare, and present technical information in a clear and effective manner
  • Participate in the development of an inclusive, helpful, fun environment

About You

  • Masters, PhD, or equivalent in Operations Research, Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, or related technical field preferred
  • A professional with 5+ years experience with Python. Knowledge of NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn, and Networkx is an extra bonus!
  • Experienced working directly with external customers (ideally in a consulting role) to identify requirements and consult on solutions to complex business problems
  • Experienced using leading optimization tools and techniques including Gurobi, CPLEX, genetic algorithms, and simulated annealing
  • The ability to obtain a Top Secret or Higher clearance is preferred with an active clearance being a plus.
  • Practical with a view of what it means to solve customer problems, with a strong sense of urgency and an understanding of project delivery requirements
  • Strong knowledge of mathematical modeling and optimization solution techniques
  • Experience with a version control software such as Git
  • Experience building applications to solve complex business problems for customers in a production environment
  • Collaborative mindset and solid interpersonal skills
  • Passionate for writing state-of-the-art Python code
  • Experience providing technical leadership from business problem definition, functional requirements specifications, to solution design and implementation
  • Proven record of successful on-time delivery of projects with a high degree of predictability and quality
  • Preferably experienced within industries such as Manufacturing, Logistics, Retail, Services

A D-Waver's DNA

  • We look at the future and say “why not”; we see possibilities where others see problems or routines. We show the way ahead and are committed to achieving ambitious goals.
  • We practice straight talk and listen generously to each other with empathy. We value different opinions and points of views. We ensure that we connect outside as well as inside to learn from others and inspire each other.
  • We hold ourselves accountable for delivering results. We make decisions & take responsibility so that we can act & support each other.
  • As leaders we motivate & engage our teams to undertake beyond what they originally thought possible, by developing our teams & creating the conditions for people to grow and empower themselves through enabling & coaching.

Our Compensation Philosophy is Simple but Powerful:

We believe providing D-Wavers with company ownership, competitive pay, and a range of meaningful benefits is the start of creating a culture where people want to give the best they’ve got — not because they’re simply making money, but because they’ve fallen in love with our vision, mission, values, and team.
