Title: Director, Advancement

Department: Advancement

Status: Exempt

Reports To: Vice President of Advancement

Remote position, Preference given to New York City and/or Metro

Summary

The Director, Advancement is a key member of the National Psoriasis Foundation’s Advancement team, responsible for building and growing relationships with individual donors and prospects to expand philanthropic support for NPF’s mission. This position manages a portfolio across annual, major, and planned giving, with a strong emphasis on developing meaningful donor relationships, securing significant philanthropic commitments, and building a robust pipeline for future growth.

The Director combines frontline fundraising with strategic planning and collaboration, working closely with Advancement leadership, executive leadership, board members, health care professionals, volunteers, and colleagues across NPF to connect donors with the programs, research, and priorities that are most meaningful to them.

As NPF prepares for a future capital campaign and seeks to significantly expand philanthropic investment in its mission, the Director will play an important role in strengthening donor relationships, developing the philanthropic pipeline, and advancing the fundraising practices and infrastructure needed to achieve ambitious organizational goals.

Portfolio Management & Relationship Building

  • Manage and grow a portfolio of individual donors and prospects across annual, major, and planned giving.
  • Identify and qualify prospective donors with the capacity, inclination, and connection to make meaningful philanthropic investments in NPF.
  • Build strong, personalized relationships by understanding each donor’s connection to NPF, philanthropic interests, and motivations for giving.
  • Conduct meaningful donor visits, virtual meetings, and personalized outreach to deepen engagement and advance relationships.
  • Develop and execute strategic moves management plans that guide donors and prospects through cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Build and maintain a robust pipeline of qualified prospects to achieve current revenue goals and support long-term individual giving growth.

Major & Planned Giving

  • Cultivate, solicit, and secure significant philanthropic commitments from individuals and families, including five-, six-, and seven-figure gifts, as appropriate.
  • Partner with the Vice President of Advancement, Chief Development Officer, CEO, board members, health care professionals, and volunteers to develop and execute strategies for key donors and prospects.
  • Identify and promote planned and legacy giving opportunities, including bequests, beneficiary designations, charitable gift annuities, and other appropriate giving vehicles.
  • Leverage NPF events, programs, and mission experiences as strategic opportunities to cultivate relationships, advance solicitations, and deepen donor engagement.
  • Develop compelling giving opportunities that connect donor interests with NPF’s mission, programs, research, and strategic priorities.
  • Support NPF special events through strategic donor and honoree engagement, particularly when honorees, event leaders, or key participants are part of the Director’s portfolio or donor relationships.

Donor Engagement & Stewardship

  • Develop personalized stewardship strategies that demonstrate impact, strengthen donor relationships, and inspire continued and increased philanthropic support.
  • Collaborate with Research, Advocacy, Patient Support, Marketing, and other teams to create meaningful opportunities for donors to experience and understand the impact of NPF’s work.
  • Connect donors with NPF leadership, researchers, health care professionals, programs, and volunteer leaders based on their interests and engagement goals.
  • Ensure timely and appropriate donor recognition, impact reporting, and stewardship for portfolio donors and prospects.
  • Serve as a collaborative partner across the Advancement team, sharing donor insights and identifying opportunities to strengthen relationships and maximize philanthropic engagement across NPF.

Strategic Planning & Administration

  • Partner with the Vice President of Advancement on individual giving strategy, prospect development, portfolio management, and campaign readiness.
  • Contribute to Advancement planning, budget development, revenue forecasting, and the establishment of annual fundraising goals.
  • Monitor portfolio performance, pipeline activity, donor engagement, and fundraising outcomes to identify opportunities, assess progress, and inform strategy.
  • Maintain accurate and timely donor records, engagement plans, moves management activity, and opportunities within NPF’s CRM.
  • Use donor and fundraising data to strengthen portfolio strategy, inform decision-making, and support a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Ensure fundraising activities reflect industry best practices and NPF policies, procedures, and standards.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Five to seven years of successful nonprofit fundraising experience in major gifts, planned giving, or individual giving.
  • Demonstrated success securing and closing five- and six-figure gifts
  • Experience managing a donor portfolio and moving prospects through the cultivation and solicitation cycle.

jobs.description:
About Reserv

Reserv is an insurtech creating and incubating cutting-edge AI and automation technology to bring efficiency and simplicity to claims. Founded by insurtech veterans with deep experience in SaaS and digital claims, Reserv is venture-backed by Bain Capital and Altai Ventures and began operations in May 2022. We are focused on automating highly manual tasks to tackle long-standing problems in claims and set a new standard for TPAs, insurance technology providers, and adjusters alike. We have ambitious (but attainable!) goals and need people who can work in an evolving environment. If building a leading TPA and the prospect of tackling the long-standing challenges of the claims role sounds exciting, we can't wait to meet you.

Location Requirement

Candidates must reside in an eligible U.S. state throughout employment. We are unable to hire candidates residing in California, Alaska, Hawaii, U.S. territories, or outside the United States.

About the role

Reserv’s book is growing fast — and fast growth stress-tests everything: file quality, reserving discipline, assignment logic, and the processes underneath them. We’re standing up a small rapid-response function inside Claims Performance to get ahead of it, and we’re staffing it with four of our own.

  • Deployments will range across the full complexity spectrum of the book — from high-complexity GL and liability files to high-frequency APD inventory. The common thread isn’t the line of business; it’s a book under pressure that needs senior claims hands in it now.
  • You’re a licensed, tenured adjuster who will embed inside a claims team under pressure, dig into the inventory, and take direct corrective action in files — because you hold the licenses to do it. You diagnose like an auditor and operate like an adjuster.
  • You will also act as a requirements pipeline for embedding quality and compliance controls directly into our platform: every problem you find, fix, or coach to gets written up as a spec for an embedded check in Glance. Put plainly: your job is to work yourself out of a job. When the book stabilizes and the platform checks ship, you haven’t made yourself obsolete — you’ve made the fix permanent.

**This is a 6-12 month rotational tour, not a permanent position — and the same is true of the function itself. This program exists to close the gap while quality and compliance controls are built into Glance; as those embedded checks ship, the need for manual intervention shrinks, and the program sunsets with it. That’s not a risk to the role — it’s the definition of success. At the end of your tour you return to a guaranteed equivalent-or-better seat, carrying skills and visibility very few adjusters get.

You’ll sit on the Claims Performance team. The VP of Claims Performance and claims leadership point you at the book, set the priorities, and re-aim you as conditions change — you bring the file-level judgment on how to get there. Before your first deployment, the QA team will train you on Reserv’s AI-assisted review tooling — MAG (multi-agent review), Batch, and Copilot — so you’re diagnosing with machine leverage, not just a legal pad.

What you'll do

  • Embed in an assigned book of business. Review the claim inventory end to end and surface what’s actually wrong: aged and stalled files, miss-assigned claims, under-reserved exposures, and authority breaches.
  • Fix what you find. Where licensed and authorized, take corrective action in the file: documentation, reserve recommendations, reassignment flags, and escalation. You don’t write a finding and walk away; you leave the file better than you found it.
  • Shape the action plan, then work the clean-up through Claim Health. Provide direct input into claim action plans, then use Claim Health to drive the clean-up: prioritize the inventory, work it down, and verify the improvement is real. A known failure mode is files being “moved” without actually advancing — you’ll distinguish genuine file progression from superficial touches, and call out the difference.
  • Route what you can’t fix to the leader who can. Some findings belong to a desk, not a file — training gaps, assignment logic, authority practices. Those get documented and handed to the accountable claims leader through Claims Performance, and you track whether they’re actioned. You illuminate; line leadership enforces.
  • Provide direct coaching and feedback to adjusting staff. Every corrected file is a coaching opportunity. Deliver specific, file-grounded feedback to the adjusters behind the inventory — directly, constructively, and in the moment. The goal isn’t just a cleaner file; it’s a desk that doesn’t produce the problem again.
  • Turn every fix into a platform check. Each problem you correct by hand gets written up as a structured requirement/spec for an automated control in Glance, so the platform catches it next time and no human has to. Rinse, repeat, scale.
  • Be the technical claims brain for claims leadership. As leadership pressure-tests processes across the book, you supply the file-level expertise: what’s really happening in the inventory, and why.
  • Keep the lines clean with QA. You are first-line: you work files and you fix them. The independent QA team trains you, audits behind you, and picks up the audit-worthy patterns you hand off. You never audit your own work — that separation is what lets your file actions stand up to carrier and regulator scrutiny.

What You Bring

  • Senior adjuster experience with genuine range. GL/liability complexity is mandatory — that depth transfers to everything else — but you’re equally willing to grind through a high-frequency APD inventory. Deployments will demand both.
  • A completed licensing footprint. You’ve finished the licensing process and are maximally licensed — this role starts deployed, not in a licensing queue. You’ll maintain the footprint with company-supported CE.
  • Airtight file documentation discipline. Your corrective actions live in files that regulators, carriers, and QA will read.
  • Comfort with AI-assisted claims tooling — or strong aptitude and appetite to learn it. You’ll be trained on MAG, Batch, and Copilot before deployment.
  • Comfort operating in a directed, high-tempo model. Claims leadership sets the target and re-aims you as the book demands; you own how the work gets done in the file. If you need six months of runway on one desk, this isn’t your role.
  • The rare temperament this role demands: the diagnostic mindset of an auditor, the willingness to get your hands dirty in files, and the credibility to coach peers directly — including delivering feedback the recipient may not want to hear.
  • A sense of urgency — at all times. (That does not mean working at all hours.)

Why This Role

Visibility. You’ll work directly with the VP of Claims Performance and senior claims leadership, on the problems they care most about, with your findings shaping how they run the book.

Leverage. Fixing one file helps one claim. Writing the spec that becomes a Glance platform check helps every claim, forever. Very few adjuster roles let you build the system instead of just working inside it.

Trajectory. Your job is to work yourself out of a job — and so is the program’s. Rotation alumni return to the book as the adjusters who know the AI tooling, think in platform checks, and have run point for senior claims leadership. As this function sunsets, that experience is what you keep — and it’s the profile we expect to draw on for what comes next.

Working hours are aligned to claims leadership (US hours).

Benefits

  • Generous health-insurance package with nationwide coverage, vision, & dental
  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer matching
  • Competitive PTO policy – we want our employees fresh, healthy, happy, and energized!
  • Generous family leave policy after 8 months of continuous work
  • 100% remote (home-based) role designed to support your work-life balance
  • Apple laptop, large second monitor, and other quality-of-life equipment you may want. Technology is something that should make your life easier, not harder!

At Reserv, we value diversity in backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences and believe that diversity in viewpoints and critical thinking drives innovation, first-principles thinking, and success. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and encourage those from all walks of life to apply. If you believe you are a good fit for this role, we would love to hear from you!

jobs.excerpt: Who we are: Through a partnership-based approach, Coterie helps insurance professionals unlock untapped revenue in the small commercial space.
jobs.description:
Who we are:
Through a partnership-based approach, Coterie helps insurance professionals unlock untapped revenue in the small commercial space. With an innovative quoting platform that delivers accurate pricing and bindable quotes in less than one minute, Coterie makes small business insurance effortless.

We are on a mission to build and foster a world-class team to bring speed, simplicity, and service to commercial insurance. We value integrity, humility, passion, and intelligence. If you want to push yourself and reshape a $200B+ market, we’re excited to talk to you!

Position Summary:

The VP, Customer Care is the leader responsible for building and running the Service Center and the scalable Care Center around it: the organizational structure, leadership team, operating model, sourcing strategy, and technology foundation required to support the company’s growth. Reporting to executive leadership, this role ensures agents and policyholders receive consistent, high-quality experience while the operation grows efficiently and predictably.

This leader owns the Care Center budget and end-to-end service delivery across calls, chats, emails, and digital channels, supporting policy changes, endorsements, payments, renewals, claims inquiries, and escalations. A core part of the role is determining the right blend of in-house teams, outsourced partners, automation, and AI to deliver that service, in close partnership with Sales, Underwriting, Claims, Product, Technology, Procurement, and Compliance.

At Coterie, service is part of how we grow. Thousands of independent agents, brokers, and digital partners rely on us to make small business insurance easy, and every call, chat, and email either strengthens that relationship or puts it at risk. When an agent gets a fast, knowledgeable answer, they send us their next submission. When a policyholder who bought coverage through a partner has a smooth experience, they renew. The Care Center serves two audiences, agents and policyholders, each with different needs. Its performance shows up directly in retention, partner loyalty, and revenue.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design and implement a scalable Care Center operating model, including organizational structure, support tiers, specialized queues (agent vs. policyholder, billing, claims inquiries, escalations), spans of control, and service level standards.
  • Define roles, career paths, and the leadership hierarchy needed to grow volume and headcount without degrading service.
  • Establish workforce management practices, including forecasting, capacity planning, scheduling, and staffing ratios, that flex with growth, seasonality, and new product launches.
  • Build, lead, and develop a high-performing leadership team of directors and managers, including identifying talent, setting accountability through scorecards and goals, making difficult personnel decisions, and building succession plans for key roles.
  • Build and launch the Service Center inside the Coterie Care Center, owning site and channel setup, systems readiness, and go-live, and hiring and training the founding team.
  • Run day-to-day Service Center operations against clear performance standards (service level, handle time, quality, first-contact resolution, satisfaction), including real-time queue management, quality and coaching programs, and readiness for volume spikes from renewals, billing cycles, catastrophe events, and new product launches.
  • Develop and maintain standardized processes, SOPs, escalation protocols, and knowledge management practices that keep the operation consistent across teams, locations, and partners.
  • Establish KPIs, reporting frameworks, and executive dashboards, with a regular cadence of weekly operating metrics, monthly business reviews, and quarterly strategy reviews.
  • Own the Care Center budget and serve as its primary point of accountability to executive leadership, reporting on performance, cost-to-serve, customer experience, emerging risks, and investment priorities.
  • Develop and execute outsourcing strategy, including deciding which work stays in-house and which is outsourced (overflow, after-hours, seasonal peaks, back-office processing) based on complexity, regulatory risk, cost, and customer impact.
  • Lead BPO partner selection, contracting, onboarding, and transition with Procurement, Legal, and Compliance, and hold partners to internal standards through SLAs, scorecards, business reviews, and audit rights.
  • Identify and lead opportunities to apply self-service, automation, and AI to high-volume contact drivers, and measure the impact on containment, handle time, quality, cost-to-serve, and customer and agent satisfaction.
  • Partner with Technology, Product, Security, and Compliance to evaluate and implement CRM, telephony/CCaaS, workforce management, and AI solutions with appropriate human oversight, testing, and controls.
  • Develop business cases and multi-year roadmaps for staffing, outsourcing, technology, and AI investments, with clear ROI and success measures.
  • Drive continuous improvement and root-cause analysis to improve first-contact resolution and reduce avoidable contact volume.
  • Collaborate with Sales, Underwriting, Claims, Product, and Technology to ensure operational readiness for new products, initiatives, and system changes.
  • Ensure Care Center operations and outsourced partners meet licensing, regulatory, security, privacy, and audit requirements, partnering with Legal, Compliance, and Internal audit.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Operations Management, or related field required; MBA preferred.
  • 10+ years leading large, multi-channel contact center organizations, including senior leadership roles with budget ownership and a proven track record of scaling an operation through significant growth.
  • Insurance industry experience, ideally in property and casualty.
  • Demonstrated experience designing organizational structures and hiring, developing, and when necessary, exiting leaders at multiple levels.
  • Hands-on experience evaluating, contracting, and managing outsourced/BPO partners, including vendor governance and SLA management.
  • Experience selecting and implementing contact center automation and AI solutions (e.g., conversational AI, agent assist, speech analytics) with measurable implementations

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Strong strategic and operational leadership capabilities.
  • Working knowledge of policy servicing, billing, renewals, claims, and the regulatory standards that govern them.
  • Deep expertise in workforce management, forecasting, capacity planning, and service level management.
  • Proficiency in continuous improvement methods such as Lean or Six Sigma.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate data into actionable insights.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and initiatives simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Proven ability to build scalable processes and drive operational improvement.
  • Executive presence, with experience presenting business cases, performance, risk, and investment recommendations to executive leadership.
  • Problem solving mindset.

Our interview process:

Our hiring process generally consists of 4 phases. The goal is to provide an opportunity for us to learn more about our candidates while allowing them to get to know us as well!

  • Phase 1: Qualified candidates will first meet with a member of our People Operations team for a phone interview. This discussion is a high-level conversation to understand more about your background and interests and for us to share more about Coterie and the position.
  • Phase 2: Selected candidates will be invited to meet with our Hiring Manager for a 2nd interview via Teams video. This interview is designed to be more detail oriented and allows you to learn more about the role and expected to be 30 minutes in length.
  • Phase 3: Top candidates will be invited to participate in an experiential interview exercise, which includes a project provided in advance. During the interview, candidates will have a 1-hour session with the hiring manager to present and discuss their project, followed by additional 1:1 interviews with team members. The full interview series is expected to take approximately 2-3 hours.
  • Phase 4: Final candidates will receive an invite to our final interview that will include a 1:1 interview with a member of our senior leadership team. The final interview is roughly 30 minutes.

What's in it for you:

Coterie has excellent benefits for all full-time employees. We offer the following:

  • 100% remote
  • Health insurance through Aetna (we pay 100% of premiums)
  • Dental and vision insurance through Guardian (we pay 100% of premiums)
  • Basic life insurance (we pay 100% of premiums)
  • Access to flexible spending account (FSA) or health savings account (HSA) (for those using HSA eligible plans)
  • 401K plan (up 4% match with immediate vest). Must be 21 years of age or older to participate
  • Flexible PTO is expected to align with business needs and generally does not exceed approximately 5 weeks per calendar year.
  • 12 company-paid holidays each year
  • Continuing education annual stipend
  • Annual base salary is estimated between $170,000-$200,000 based on national data. This position is also eligible for an annual Short-Term Incentive (STI) bonus based on company performance. Candidates who meet all the minimum requirements and possess additional relevant experience, as outlined in the job description, may be considered for a salary above the midpoint of the above range. Salary is based on internal equity; internal salary ranges; market data/ranges; applicant’s skills; prior relevant experience; degrees or certifications, etc.

Work Authorization:
At this time, Coterie Insurance is unable to consider candidates who require current or future visa sponsorship. Applicants must have authorization to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future. Falsification of an application, including work authorization status, is immediate grounds for dismissal from consideration.

Job Title: Director of Donor Engagement and Communications

Department: Advancement

Location: Remote

Reports To: Deputy Chief Advancement Officer

Supervises: 2-6 Direct Reports

Context: At the Sierra Club, we believe in the power of interdependence. Together, we remain committed to the fight for a healthy climate built on a foundation of environmental, racial, economic, and gender justice – a future where all people benefit from a healthy, thriving planet and a direct connection to nature. As the climate crisis and deeply entrenched systemic racism all fuel injustice, we will continue to fight for a bold, transformational agenda that recognizes the interconnectedness between our planet, our humanity, and our future. By recognizing that our destinies are tied, we continue to name that all things are fundamentally connected, and the overlap between ecology, race, gender, and representative government will move to either advance our collective humanity or to oppress it. Sierra Club has close to 700 staff across the country and a network of 64 local chapters that are led and fueled by thousands of volunteers. We are also proud to be a unionized employer, with three labor unions representing more than half of our employees.


Scope: The Director of Donor Communications & Engagement leads the development and execution of a comprehensive communications, stewardship, and engagement strategy for Sierra Club's major gifts program. This role is responsible for creating meaningful, strategic touchpoints that deepen donor relationships, strengthen donor understanding of Sierra Club's mission and impact, and inspire increased philanthropic investment, with a particular emphasis on unrestricted support.


Working in close partnership with frontline fundraisers and colleagues across Advancement, Membership Growth, Communications, and program teams, the Director will develop an integrated annual calendar of donor communications and engagement opportunities that advance fundraising priorities and respond to donor interests. The role will translate Sierra Club's organizational priorities, campaigns, and impact into compelling donor-facing materials, experiences, and stories that demonstrate the value of philanthropic investment.

The Director will oversee a team of two staff and ensure that major donors experience thoughtful, coordinated, and high-quality communications, engagement and stewardship throughout their relationship with Sierra Club.

Job activities include but are not limited to:

    Strategic Donor Communications

  • Develop and lead an annual strategic communications calendar for major and principal gifts donors, in partnership with frontline fundraisers, ensuring consistent, relevant, and compelling engagement throughout the year.

  • Establish communications strategies that reinforce Sierra Club's organizational priorities and philanthropic case for support, with a particular emphasis on building understanding and enthusiasm for unrestricted giving.

  • Partner with frontline fundraisers to identify donor interests, communication opportunities, and strategies for deepening donor engagement and increasing philanthropic investment.

  • Develop and oversee the production of compelling donor-facing materials, including cases for support, campaign collateral, pitch decks, presentations, impact reports, proposals, and other fundraising resources.

  • Translate complex programmatic, advocacy, and organizational work into accessible and inspiring narratives that demonstrate the impact of donor support.

  • Ensure consistency, quality, and alignment of donor communications with Sierra Club's brand, voice, and fundraising priorities.


    • Donor Stewardship & Engagement

  • Develop and implement a comprehensive stewardship strategy for major and principal gifts donors that strengthens relationships, demonstrates impact, and supports donor acquisition and retention and growth of a diverse pipeline of donors, including households and organizations.

  • Design and execute a portfolio of meaningful donor engagement opportunities, including virtual briefings, small-group conversations, in-person gatherings, programmatic experiences, and other opportunities to connect donors with Sierra Club's leadership, experts, and work.

  • Partner with frontline fundraisers to develop tailored engagement strategies for priority donors and prospects.

  • Identify opportunities to leverage organizational milestones, campaigns, programmatic achievements, and timely issues to create meaningful donor touchpoints.

  • Establish stewardship practices that demonstrate the impact of unrestricted contributions and reinforce the importance of flexible philanthropic support.

  • Develop systems and processes to ensure timely, consistent, coordinated, and personalized donor recognition and stewardship.


    • Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Supervise, coach, and develop a team of two staff, establishing clear priorities, expectations, and accountability for high-quality execution.

  • Build strong working relationships with frontline fundraisers and colleagues across Advancement, Communications, Marketing, and program teams.

  • Collaborate with program and organizational leaders to identify compelling stories, expertise, and engagement opportunities for major donors.

  • Establish effective workflows and processes that enable the team to anticipate fundraising needs and deliver timely, high-quality materials and experiences.

  • Foster a collaborative, donor-centered culture that prioritizes relationship building, responsiveness, and continuous improvement.

The successful candidate must demonstrate the following skills, experience and competencies:

  • Extensive senior-level experience or equivalent combination of experience and education in fundraising communications, donor engagement, stewardship, major gifts, or a related field.

  • Experience creating compelling fundraising materials, including cases for support, proposals, presentations, and pitch decks.

  • Strong storytelling and writing skills, with the ability to translate complex issues and organizational priorities into clear, persuasive donor-facing communications.

  • Experience developing donor engagement strategies and executing both virtual and in-person events and experiences.

  • Demonstrated ability to partner effectively with frontline fundraisers and translate fundraising priorities into actionable communications and engagement plans.

  • Experience managing, coaching, and developing staff.

  • Strong project management skills, with the ability to work in a deadline-driven environment, manage multiple priorities, coordinate across teams, and deliver high-quality work on deadline.

  • A commitment to Sierra Club's mission and values.

  • Proficiency with fundraising databases and Google platform.

  • Committed to evolution. You are aware of your group identities and how they have shaped your life and experiences at work. You have an analysis of how racism and other forms of oppression in society impact relationships, systems, and culture. You bring experience and skills for working effectively with colleagues across group identities and position/role.

  • Uplifting and additive. You see mistakes as opportunities for growth; problems as catalysts for solutions, and inspire others along the journey. You carry a constructive approach, can-do attitude, a sense of humor, and authentic kindness wherever you go.

The strongest candidates will also demonstrate the following skills, experience and competencies:

  • Passion for the Sierra Club’s commitment to environmental and social justice.

  • Positive energy and good humor that engenders enthusiasm and collaboration.

To Apply

The Sierra Club provides equal employment and advancement opportunities to all staff members. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, lived experience and skills. As an Account Manager, you will develop the French seller market and act as the main point of contact for new and existing sellers. jobs.title: Senior Manager, Business Intelligence & Analytics
jobs.excerpt: About Donorbox Donorbox is a leading fundraising platform and donor management system for nonprofit organizations.
jobs.description:
About Donorbox

Donorbox is a leading fundraising platform and donor management system for nonprofit organizations. Our mission is to accelerate positive impact worldwide by helping nonprofits become highly effective at raising funds and managing their supporter base. Since 2014, we have powered more than 100,000 global organizations to raise over $4 billion in donations. 🚀

Our fast-growing company is profitable and bootstrapped with a healthy run rate. We have a fully distributed and diverse 150-person team based in 16+ states and 23+ countries. In 2026, Donorbox was named by Built In as one of the Best Places to Work in Washington, DC.

🏅 Donorbox is rated the #1 software for fundraising, donor management, and nonprofit payment on G2 based on hundreds of verified customer reviews — a reflection of the care our team puts into building products that nonprofits trust.

The Role

Donorbox is looking for a Senior Manager, Business Intelligence & Analytics to lead our BI team and shape how the company uses data to make decisions. Reporting to the Director of Data Strategy, you’ll own the BI roadmap, partner with executives and department heads across Finance, Marketing, Sales, Product, and Customer Success, and help teams get trusted answers faster, both from your team and through self-service tools. This is a player-coach role. You’ll develop a team of analysts, drive consistent, trusted metrics across reporting, and stay hands-on in SQL and data modeling when the work calls for it. You’ll also help us bring AI and automation into how we analyze data.

Responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, and develop the BI team, providing direction, prioritization, feedback, and career growth for analysts at different levels
  • Own the BI roadmap and backlog, prioritizing requests and initiatives based on business impact and alignment with organizational goals
  • Serve as the primary BI partner to executive leadership and department heads (e.g., Finance, Marketing, Sales, Product, Customer Success), understanding their goals and translating them into analytics priorities
  • Oversee the delivery of dashboards, reports, KPIs, and analyses, ensuring they are accurate, well-documented, and meet stakeholder needs
  • Build and scale self-service analytics through reusable data models, curated datasets, templates, and training so teams can find answers independently
  • Drive metric standardization and data quality within BI, ensuring reporting uses agreed definitions from the Business Glossary and applying the governance standards set by the Data team
  • Manage BI delivery practices, including requirements and user stories, QA and validation of reports and data, release processes, and documentation
  • Partner with Data Engineering to define data sources, models, and pipelines that support reporting and analytics needs
  • Partner with RevOps and other operational teams to keep reporting consistent across tools and to clarify which team owns which reports
  • Deliver data literacy and enablement programs, including training, data desk, and documentation that help stakeholders interpret and act on data
  • Identify opportunities to use AI and automation in analytics, such as AI-assisted analysis and natural-language querying, in partnership with the Business Systems & AI team
  • Measure and communicate the impact of BI work, including adoption of dashboards and self-service tools, stakeholder satisfaction, and business outcomes supported
  • Remain hands-on as needed, contributing to complex analyses, SQL, and data modeling to support the team and maintain technical credibility

What We're Looking For:

  • 7+ years of experience in business intelligence, analytics, or data roles, including 2+ years managing analysts or a BI team
  • Strong SQL and data modeling skills, with hands-on experience in a cloud data warehouse (such as BigQuery) and BI tools (such as Superset, Tableau, or Power BI)
  • A track record of building self-service analytics and driving adoption of dashboards and data tools
  • Experience partnering with executives and translating business questions into analytics priorities and clear recommendations
  • Experience applying metric definitions, data quality practices, and data governance in day-to-day BI work
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex data clearly to non-technical audiences
  • Experience in SaaS, fintech, or the nonprofit sector is a plus

Details

  • Fully remote based in US or Canada
  • Hours: Core hours of 9am–5pm ET, with flexibility to 8am–5pm or 9am–6pm ET
  • Salary: $147,000–$175,000 USD (US); $124,000–$152,000 CAD (Canada)

Benefits & Perks

  • Fully remote work from the comfort of your home
  • Generous time off policy of 21 days (birthday included 🎉), 8 designated/floating holidays, 2 paid volunteer days, and 5+ sick days (dependent on state)
  • Employer-sponsored health insurance plan through TriNet, including medical (United Healthcare), dental, vision, and life
  • 401(k) retirement plan via TriNet's partner, Empower, with an employer match of up to 4%
  • Reimbursement package for home office expenses and professional development, up to $1.5k
  • Eligibility for employee equity plan (stock options)
  • Wellness program with fitness and mindfulness classes
  • Love your work and our mission of serving nonprofits!

The Application Process

We have 7 stages:

  1. Apply here and fill out our questions to tell us about you!
  2. Prescreen Call with the Talent Team
  3. Interview with Hiring Manager
  4. Technical Interview
  5. Assignment
  6. Panel/Final Interview
  7. Background & Reference Checks

If this sounds like the right role for you, please apply today and let us know why. We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.description:
Overview

The Project Manager is responsible for the end-to-end delivery of technology initiatives including custom software development, third-party platform deployments, AI adoption, and workflow design. This role manages project scope, schedule, budget, risks, and vendor relationships, and keeps practice groups, firm leadership, and vendors aligned throughout delivery. The position works in partnership with the AI Architect and Business Analysts assigned to OD Labs and reports to the Director of OD Labs.

Responsibilities

These are the essential functions of the position. Successful job applicants will be able to perform these essential functions with or without requested reasonable accommodation:

  • Manage end-to-end delivery of OD Labs initiatives, including custom development, vendor platform deployments, AI adoption, and firm-wide rollouts, from initiation through active use.
  • Manage initiatives through the OD Labs delivery model of prototype, pilot, production, enhancements, and operational handoff, validating each phase before scaling, with a focus on the minimum viable product (MVP), the critical path, and no more than two active projects at a time.
  • Develop and maintain project plans, schedules, budgets, and resource plans, coordinate internal and external resources, and track status against scope, schedule, and budget, recommending adjustments as needed.
  • Plan and lead project team meetings, including setting agendas, coordinating attendees, and following up on action items.
  • Maintain risk, issue, and dependency logs, and escalate items that may affect schedule, cost, or scope with a recommended resolution.
  • Manage relationships with outside technology vendors, including forward-deployed engineers, holding them accountable to deliverables, quality standards, and timelines and keeping vendor scope aligned with the current MVP objective.
  • Support process mapping by capturing current and future-state workflows, facilitating working sessions, and translating practice group needs into actionable requirements, in coordination with Business Analysts.
  • Prepare and deliver project status updates to multiple levels of firm leadership, including senior leadership, identifying upcoming decisions and their impact.
  • Plan and support change management and adoption, including rollout planning, training materials and user guides, tracking of adoption metrics and user feedback, and operational handoff.
  • Identify project stakeholders and communicate project direction and upcoming milestones so that practice groups and team members remain informed.
  • Maintain the confidentiality of sensitive firm and client information.

Qualifications

Required Education and Experience:

  • Bachelors’ Degree preferred
  • 5+ years of experience working inside a law firm in a role connected to the delivery of legal work, such as legal assistant, paralegal, practice group coordinator, legal operations, or recruiting. Experience within or alongside practice groups is preferred.
  • 2+ years of experience managing technical projects, such as custom software development, systems rollouts, or technology adoption initiatives.
  • Experience owning project budgets, tracking project financials, and reporting status to stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify, track, and escalate risks and dependencies with proposed solutions.
  • Strong knowledge of project management practices, including scope, schedule, budget, risk, and change management.
  • Working understanding of how attorneys communicate and set priorities, and how decisions are made within a law firm.
  • Ability to drive work forward with incomplete requirements and changing priorities.
  • Ability to build alignment among attorneys, firm leadership, vendors, and technical team members.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present to senior leadership.

Preferred Experience:

  • Experience as a legal assistant, paralegal, practice group coordinator, or legal recruiting coordinator, particularly within a Labor & Employment practice, and familiarity with single plaintiff litigation or class action matter structures.
  • Experience in a legal innovation unit, legal technology function, or practice group technology initiative.
  • Experience in process mapping and business analysis, including capturing workflows, facilitating working sessions, and translating operational needs into requirements. Familiarity with tools such as Visio or Lucidchart is helpful.
  • Experience supporting or managing the adoption of AI platforms or similar emerging technologies in a legal setting.

Wage Transparency

Actual compensation is contingent on relevant experience, education, skills, and other job-related factors as permitted by law. This role is also eligible for performance-based bonuses and the benefits described below.

• California: Pay range $109,051 - $162,733• Colorado: Pay range $115,161 - $149,032• Connecticut: Pay range $115,161 - $155,970• Hawaii: Pay range $125,748 - $162,733• Illinois: Pay range $120,522 - $155,970• Jersey City, New Jersey: Pay range $125,748 - $162,733• Maryland: Pay range $109,051 - $149,032• Massachusetts: Pay range $125,748 - $162,733• Minnesota: Pay range $109,051 - $141,125• Nevada: Pay range $105,653 - $136,728• New Jersey: Pay range $125,748 - $162,733• New York City, New York: Pay range $125,748 - $162,733• New York State: Pay range $105,653 - $162,733• Ohio: Pay range $105,653 - $136,728• Rhode Island: Pay range $105,653 - $136,728• Washington, D.C.: Pay range $120,522 - $155,970• Washington: Pay range $120,522 - $155,970

Employment Type: Contract (6 Months)

Location: Remote (Global) — must be available to work EST business hours

Summary

We are looking for a Program Delivery Coordinator to join our Project Management Office (PMO), reporting to the Online Strategic Projects Lead in the Fundraising department. This is a coordination and execution-focused role that keeps our team's projects moving efficiently. We seek someone who will own the systems, documentation, and operational follow-through that make delivery reliable. You will be the connective tissue that holds information together on our team and in support of Fundraising, ensures nothing falls through the cracks, and makes it easy for others to do their best work. This role is a strong fit for someone who is highly organized, takes genuine pride in clean systems, and finds satisfaction in making complex work feel manageable.

Team Context

The PMO is a small, cross-functional team embedded within Fundraising. We serve as the connective layer between strategy and execution — keeping high-priority initiatives moving, improving coordination across teams, and ensuring that progress is visible and accountable. Our work spans project management, forecasting support, OKR reporting, and operational process design.

The Coordinator role is designed to assist with project management by supporting the operational and administrative layer that supports good project management.

You are responsible for:

Keeping project infrastructure organized and current

  • Maintain Asana boards and Phabricator tasks as directed by Sr. Program Delivery Specialist and Sr. Delivery Manager so that project status, owners, and timelines are always accurate.
  • Ensure all projects satisfy document requirements and/or processes outlined in Project Management Checklist.
  • Create and maintain suite of project management documents.
  • Flag when tasks are overdue, owners are unclear, or dependencies are at risk.
  • Identify opportunities to improve how we use project management tools (i.e. Asana, Phab) and processes, and propose improvements.
  • Organize and maintain shared documentation in Google Drive so information is easy to find.

Supporting meeting and communication logistics

  • Assist with meeting preparation and agenda creation as directed.
  • Schedule follow-up meetings and send calendar invites on behalf of the team.
  • Take and distribute clear, actionable meeting notes, and/or ensure any auto-generated notes are accurate.
  • Send documents, trackers, and updates to stakeholders as directed.
  • Manage routine team communications and follow-up reminders. Support PMO in compiling content and updates for bi-weekly team reporting.
  • Create major project completion countdown Slack updates for relevant teams.

Recurring operational tasks

  • Run established processes once they are set up and documented, including intake workflows, reporting cadences, and team templates.
  • Maintain library of project templates and ensure they stay current.
  • Assist with coordination across teams on assigned deliverables.
  • Follow up with stakeholders on missing deliverables.
  • Compile and share written summaries

Contributing to a high-functioning team

  • Bring a detail-oriented eye to everything you touch: catching errors, inconsistencies, and gaps before they become problems.
  • Ask good questions when something is unclear rather than guessing.
  • Look for ways to make recurring and process-related work more efficient over time.
  • Support a team culture of clarity, accountability, and continuous improvement.
  • Ability to run small projects independently.

The right person is better than the right set of experiences. These are the traits we’ve identified that make great additions to our team so far.

Skills and Experience:

  • 2–3 years of experience in a coordination, operations, or project support role.
  • Background in fundraising in non-profit or tech sectors
  • Strong organizational skills with genuine attention to detail.
  • Comfort managing multiple moving pieces at once without losing track of any of them.
  • Clear, professional written communication and discerning ability to match communication needs with medium (i.e. email, chat, messaging platforms).
  • Experience with project management or task-tracking tools (Asana, Jira, Monday, or similar)
  • Proactive follow-through.

Qualities that are important to us:

  • Attention to detail
  • Thorough communication
  • Orientation toward action
  • Data-driven adaptability
  • Collaboration
  • Team building
  • Sound judgment
  • Ability to operate independently
  • Diplomacy

Additionally, we’d love it if you have:

  • Experience working in an international organization that has a distributed workforce.
  • Experience working within a movement with strong culture and values.
  • Experience working with online communities, particularly as part of the free culture movement.
  • Fluency in languages other than English.
  • Experience contributing to Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia projects.
  • Global perspective, with significant experience living or working internationally.
  • Experience supporting a team through a period of growth or change.
  • Bonus for PMP Certification or desire to become PMP certified.

About the Wikimedia Foundation

The Wikimedia Foundation is the nonprofit organization that operates Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia free knowledge projects. Our vision is a world in which every single human can freely share in the sum of all knowledge. We believe that everyone has the potential to contribute something to our shared knowledge, and that everyone should be able to access that knowledge freely. We host Wikipedia and the Wikimedia projects, build software experiences for reading, contributing, and sharing Wikimedia content, support the volunteer communities and partners who make Wikimedia possible, and advocate for policies that enable Wikimedia and free knowledge to thrive.

The Wikimedia Foundation is a charitable, not-for-profit organization that relies on donations. We receive donations from millions of individuals around the world, with an average donation of about $15. We also receive donations through institutional grants and gifts. The Wikimedia Foundation is a United States 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization with offices in San Francisco, California, USA.

As an equal opportunity employer, the Wikimedia Foundation values having a diverse workforce and continuously strives to maintain an inclusive and equitable workplace. We encourage people with a diverse range of backgrounds to apply. The Wikimedia Foundation is a remote-first organization with staff members including contractors based 40+ countries*. Salaries at the Wikimedia Foundation are set in a way that is competitive, equitable, and consistent with our values and culture. The anticipated annual pay range of this position for applicants based within the United States is US$36.91 to US$56.47 with multiple individualized factors, including cost of living in the location, being the determinants of the offered pay. For applicants located outside of the US, the pay range will be adjusted to the country of hire. We neither ask for nor take into consideration the salary history of applicants. The compensation for a successful applicant will be based on their skills, experience and location.

*Please note that we are currently able to hire in the following:
US States: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, District of Columbia*, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Puerto Rico*, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia, Wisconsin and Wyoming (*US Territory or Federal District)

jobs.excerpt: Manager, Executive Operations Location: Remote, New York, Oakland Role Type: Full-time Compensation: $112,000 Visa sponsorship: Not available Hires remotely in: USA Experience: 3+ years in executive operations, executive support, chief of staff, consulting or a similar role Recidiviz is thrilled to be hiring a Manager, Executive Operations to join the Office of the CEO!
jobs.description:
Manager, Executive Operations

Location: Remote, New York, Oakland

Role Type: Full-time

Compensation: $112,000

Visa sponsorship: Not available

Hires remotely in: USA

Experience: 3+ years in executive operations, executive support, chief of staff, consulting or a similar role

Recidiviz is thrilled to be hiring a Manager, Executive Operations to join the Office of the CEO! Our CEO leads two mission-driven tech nonprofits, Recidiviz and Edovo, and their time is one of the most valuable resources we have. That's where you come in. We're looking for a highly organized operator, a clear writer and a trusted partner who will help our CEO go further, faster. You'll make sure their time goes to the highest-impact work, that they walk into every room prepared, and that their voice reaches the right people at the right moment.

About us

Recidiviz is creating safer, healthier communities by improving outcomes for people in the criminal justice system. We build technology to safely reduce the number of people in prison and to help criminal justice leaders embrace data-driven decision-making.

Using software tools and thoughtful product design, we've been able to safely and permanently reduce incarceration and improve outcomes. We work side-by-side with leaders of the criminal justice system, people in prison and on supervision, and ecosystem partners to build a better path forward. In addition to the revenue we earn from state partners, some of the most respected philanthropists and foundations support our work.

People who succeed at Recidiviz lead with kindness and humility, assume good intent, learn from failure, and fix problems when they see them. They are great listeners. They build deep relationships with and empathy for the people we work with and the people our mission serves.

About the role

This isn't a traditional assistant role. You'll own the CEO's calendar, travel and admin with complete reliability. You'll also use your judgment about what the CEO should be doing, who they should be seeing, and what their relationships need, without checking in every time. Our CEO's work spans funders, two boards, and state government relationships that take years to build. You'll quickly learn that network and handle each relationship with care.

Core responsibilities

  • Manage the calendar with intention, not just scheduling: Own the CEO's calendar across Recidiviz and Edovo. Decide which meetings she should attend and which should be delegated, swapped or pushed, while minding deadlines and stewarding every relationship. Protect deep-work time, and make sure the CEO's time matches each organization's priorities.
  • Track priorities and support prioritization: Track the CEO's tasks, deadlines and the many requests for their time from development, communications, and state engagement and growth teams. Help them focus on what matters most.
  • Prepare the CEO for every room: Work with our Development, Communications, Business Development and State Engagement teams to deliver accurate, relationship-aware briefs 24–48 hours before key meetings. Know what makes a great funder brief versus a great brief for a state corrections director, and hold teams to it.
  • Write as the CEO: Draft and edit the CEO's correspondence, including funder and government correspondence, batch emails such as year-in-review updates and event invitations, and replies in their voice. The bar is light edits.
  • Triage the CEO's inbound: Be the first line on meeting requests, contact forms and forwarded asks. Decide what the CEO actually needs to see, and make sure nothing sits longer than a day.
  • Treat travel as strategy: Plan and optimize travel, and propose every trip in advance: who the CEO should see, who's been waiting, what's happening in that city, and which meetings can be stacked.
  • Close the loop after meetings: Capture what the CEO and others committed to, route takeaways to the right teams, and track commitments to completion, including debriefs from summits and events.
  • Keep relationships warm: Make sure funders, board members and government partners hear from the CEO at the right cadence. That includes thank-yous after site visits, introductions the CEO promised, renewal milestones, board touchpoints between meetings, and thoughtful no-ask notes.
  • Keep the company in the loop: Work with the Operations team to run a predictable cadence of internal updates from the CEO.
  • Make admin invisible: Handle expenses, e-signatures and logistics completely, so they never reach the CEO's attention.

Wild success

Here are a few things you might accomplish in your first year that would demonstrate wild success in this role:

  • The CEO's weekly time consistently matches their stated priorities, not whatever is loudest or oldest.
  • Every consequential meeting starts with a brief that landed on time and covers relationship history, the meeting's purpose and what a good outcome looks like.
  • No important relationship goes cold: every funder, board member and key government partner is touched at the right cadence, through a system you built.
  • Every trip is fully stacked, and the CEO's commitments from meetings are captured and closed without them having to track anything.
  • You've built new systems for the Office of the CEO, such as a curated weekly briefing on key states, funders and policy news, or a workflow that turns the CEO's voice memos into drafts and action items.

Minimum qualifications

  • You're exceptionally organized: You bring order to chaos by being thorough and systematic. You love building systems that track many priorities, deadlines and stakeholders at once, and nothing falls through the cracks on your watch.
  • You have excellent judgment: You weigh competing priorities quickly and make good calls without a playbook. You know when to decide yourself and when to escalate, and you handle sensitive information with discretion.
  • You're a strong writer: You write clearly and concisely, adapt your tone for funders, government leaders, partners and internal teams, and can learn a specific voice and write convincingly in it.
  • You're a relationship builder: You're a warm, direct communicator who knows that how something is handled matters as much as what gets done. People want to hear from you, and your warmth never slows things down.
  • You're proactive and comfortable with ambiguity: You anticipate needs before they come up, fix problems when you find them, and are excited to shape a role across two organizations whose ways of working together are still developing.
  • 3+ years of experience in executive operations, executive support, chief of staff, project management, consulting or a similar role.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience supporting a senior executive: You've worked closely with a CEO, founder or other senior leader.
  • Familiarity with philanthropy or government: You've worked with funders, foundations, state agencies or elected officials, and you understand what a strong briefing for those audiences looks like.
  • A personal connection to the criminal justice system and/or a passion for doing work that matters: You have lived or working experience with the operations and consequences of America's criminal justice system. You don't need to know everything about the field, but the design and efficacy of our criminal justice processes should feel like issues you can't ignore.

Compensation

Compensation is standardized based on roles and responsibilities. This ensures equitable compensation and responsible stewardship of our resources. As such, we do not negotiate compensation offers.

The compensation for this role is $112,000.

What we offer

  • Effective, extremely thoughtful colleagues, working together on a mission that matters
  • 90% medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage for you and your dependents
  • Flexible time off, including 20 days of PTO, 3 days of paid volunteering time, and 13 paid holidays
  • 12 weeks of paid parental leave
  • 401(k) retirement plan with 5% company match and no vesting period
  • Complimentary One Medical membership (depending on location)
  • Partnership with Carrot to provide employees with inclusive fertility and family-forming benefits, as well as a small but growing number of hormonal health and gender-affirming care benefits
  • Monthly ClassPass credit for personal wellness
  • Free mental health support via Talkspace
  • Well-located offices in Oakland and Manhattan, with the flexibility to work remotely or go into either office as you choose
  • An annual company offsite and other ad-hoc gatherings

An important note

Lasting change is always built on diversity. Recidiviz recruits, employs, trains, compensates and promotes regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, disability, age, veteran status, ancestry, citizenship, marital status, gender identity and all protected status as required by applicable law. We consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. If you have a special need that requires accommodation, please let us know in your application. Even if you don't think you meet all the criteria above, drop your resume, and we'll take a look – you might be great for another role or another time!

jobs.description:
Who We Are:

TKO Group Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: TKO) is a premium sports and entertainment company. TKO owns iconic properties including UFC, the world’s premier mixed martial arts organization; WWE, the global leader in sports entertainment; and PBR, the world’s premier bull riding organization. Together, these properties reach 1 billion households across 210 countries and territories and organize more than 500 live events year-round, attracting more than three million fans. TKO also services and partners with major sports rights holders through IMG, an industry-leading global sports marketing agency; and On Location, a global leader in premium experiential hospitality.

Director - Data & Analytics Products


About TKO

TKO Group Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: TKO) is a premium sports and entertainment company. TKO owns iconic properties including UFC, the world's premier mixed martial arts organization; WWE, the global leader in sports entertainment; and PBR, the world's premier bull riding organization. Together, these properties reach 210 countries and territories and organize more than 500 live events year-round, attracting more than three million fans. TKO also services and partners with major sports rights holders through IMG, an industry-leading global sports marketing agency; and On Location, a global leader in premium experiential hospitality.


The role

We are hiring a Director of Data & Analytics Products to own one or more of our major data and AI products, starting with Athlete Intelligence. Athlete Intelligence gives business teams a trusted, unified view of the athletes at the center of our brands, and the analytics and AI to make better, faster decisions about them.

Many of those decisions still run on spreadsheets, decks and individual judgment. This role turns them into products: trusted data, a clear recommendation, a decision, and a read on whether it worked.

The work has executive sponsorship and early prototypes. What it needs now is an owner who defines the business outcome, sequences the build, and drives it to adoption. You will take it from prototype to products that business teams use every week, starting with one brand and expanding across the portfolio.

This is a builder role. You start hands-on, working with shared data engineering and data science partners, and grow your own product team as the portfolio scales.


What you'll own

  • The business outcome. For each product you lead, you define with business stakeholders what success is, in their terms (revenue, cost, time-to-decision, win rate), and you are accountable for hitting it.
  • The product breakdown. You decompose each product into releasable pieces, sequenced by business value against ease of build, so stakeholders see value every quarter rather than at the end.
  • Trusted data foundation. A governed, unified view of athlete that brings together performance, audience, commercial and contract data to build a single version of truth including data lineage, quality and governance baked into it
  • Core capabilities. A governed, unified view of each athlete (performance, audience, commercial, contract), plus the forecasting, scoring and recommendation models built on it. These are built once and reused across every surface.
  • Consumption platforms. Those capabilities delivered the way each team actually works: standard reporting, AI-generated insights and assistants, and purpose-built apps. You decide which tools fits which decision.
  • Measurement and learning. A closed loop that tracks the decisions teams make and measures the outcomes, so the business learns what works and invests accordingly.
  • Scale across brands and products. A platform and playbook that extend from the first brand to the rest of the portfolio, and from Athlete Intelligence to the next major product you take on.

What you'll do

  • Define the business outcome for each product with stakeholders, agree the metric and the target, and own delivery against it.
  • Own the product vision, roadmap and quarterly plan, and defend priorities with sponsors and stakeholders.
  • Break each product into a sequenced roadmap, trading off business value against build effort explicitly, and publish the reasoning so stakeholders understand why their item is in Q3 and not Q1.
  • Map the key decisions each business team makes, how they make them today, and where better data, analytics or AI would change the outcome.
  • Spend real time with talent, competition, partnerships, finance and leadership teams. Replace their spreadsheets and decks with products they choose to use.
  • Drive. Set the pace, remove blockers across engineering, data science and the business, and make the call when partners disagree.
  • Write clear product requirements and acceptance criteria. Work with data engineering, data science and BI partners through discovery, build and launch.
  • Set the quality, governance and access bar with engineering, legal, privacy and security, so the business trusts the numbers and sensitive commercial, contract and personal data is protected.

jobs.description:
PLEASE NOTE: At this time, we are only considering candidates located in and authorized to work in the United States.

JOIN OUR TEAM!
Bitovi is looking for a Senior PostgreSQL DBA to join us as we transform technology delivery. We help enterprise clients run critical data platforms reliably, and we’re looking for people with deep, hands-on PostgreSQL expertise to diagnose, stabilize, and tune large self-managed database environments. If you know Postgres internals well enough to explain why a database fell over and how to make sure it doesn’t happen again, we want to work with you!

Compensation: $120,000 to $190,000 annually, depending on experience, plus annual bonus opportunity.

WHO YOU ARE
You’re the person teams call when Postgres is misbehaving in production. You understand what’s happening under the hood, from MVCC and autovacuum to the planner and WAL, and you can turn that understanding into configuration and maintenance changes that keep systems healthy. You’re calm during incidents, rigorous in root cause analysis, and confident communicating findings and recommendations to both engineers and stakeholders.

You’ll excel in this role at Bitovi if you have:

  • Deep, production experience administering PostgreSQL on self-managed, on-premise infrastructure (not only managed services like RDS or Cloud SQL)

  • Expert knowledge of vacuum and autovacuum: tuning thresholds and cost limits, diagnosing and remediating table and index bloat, and preventing transaction ID wraparound

  • Strong indexing expertise: choosing among B-tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, partial, and covering indexes, identifying missing, unused, and duplicate indexes, and rebuilding indexes safely in production

  • Mastery of PostgreSQL configuration: memory settings, connection limits, checkpoints, WAL, and planner parameters, and the ability to audit an existing configuration and justify every change

  • Query performance analysis using EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS), pg_stat_statements, and the pg_stat_* views

  • Experience with replication and high availability (streaming and logical replication, Patroni, repmgr, or similar) and failover testing

  • Backup, restore, and point-in-time recovery experience (pgBackRest, Barman, or similar), including regular restore validation

  • Connection pooling with PgBouncer or Pgpool-II

  • Monitoring and alerting for Postgres (Prometheus postgres_exporter, pgwatch, Datadog, or similar) focused on catching problems before they become outages

  • Solid Linux administration skills as they relate to database hosts: storage, filesystems, kernel parameters, and resource contention

  • Incident response and root cause analysis experience, including writing clear postmortems and remediation plans

Other skills we value

  • Configuration management for database fleets (Ansible or similar) so settings are consistent, reviewed, and repeatable

  • Writing runbooks and maintenance procedures that client teams can own after an engagement

  • Capacity planning and performance baselining

  • Major version upgrades and schema migrations with minimal downtime

  • Working within change management processes in large, regulated enterprises

  • Security hardening: roles and privileges, pg_hba configuration, TLS, and auditing (pgAudit)

  • Running Postgres on Kubernetes (CloudNativePG, Crunchy Postgres Operator, or similar)

  • Scripting and automation in Python, Bash, or Go

  • Experience with other relational databases (Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL)

WHO WE ARE
Bitovi partners with companies to build outcome-focused apps and platforms. Our collaborative approach is driven by validation to deliver the swiftest route to the most valuable solution.

We design and build high-profile applications and the infrastructure and data platforms behind them, with tests, full docs, and a real deployment process. We discuss and design architectures, review code, and research new technologies. We talk to our clients, guiding them through the process, identifying potential problems and unknowns, and tackling challenges.

We help one another freely. We keep a Slack channel called ask-help, which is constantly used. We develop new skills, build better developer tools, and work on new types of projects regularly.

Our fully remote team comprises about 70 developers and designers. We welcome diversity and non-traditional paths into professions. We want the right person, not the right collection of tech keywords.

WHAT YOU’LL DO AT BITOVI
Stabilize critical systems. Audit configuration, maintenance, and indexing across enterprise PostgreSQL environments, identify the root causes of instability, and deliver fixes that measurably reduce incidents.

Tune for performance and reliability. Optimize vacuum strategy, indexing, queries, and configuration so databases stay healthy under real production load.

Prevent recurrence. Put monitoring, alerting, and runbooks in place so problems are caught early and client teams know how to respond.

Consult and manage. Consult with clients to build outcome-driven platforms, guiding them through the process, identifying potential problems and unknowns, and tackling challenges.

Travel. This is a remote, full-time position that requires the ability to travel. We travel an average of 3 to 5 days every quarter, and we’ll always do our best to work with your schedule.

Teach. We’ll discuss opportunities for you to present at conferences, attend and give training, plan and run meetups or local groups, and create various kinds of content in your expertise.

BENEFITS WE OFFER

  • Competitive salary and annual bonus opportunity

  • Completely remote work with flexible hours

  • 401(k) matching

  • 4 weeks of paid time off in addition to 8 paid holidays

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance offerings

  • Paid maternity and paternity leave

  • STD, LTD, and Life Insurance coverage

HOW TO APPLY
Please share a resume or LinkedIn profile and answer the additional questions. Yes, we read through all the answers!

Please note that we are not interested in working with recruiters. All job offers are contingent on passing a background check. Candidates must be located in and authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship at this time.

Director, Wholesale

Department: Wholesale

Reports to: VP, Retail and Wholesale

About Margaux

Margaux is a modern footwear brand rooted in duality, inspired by the ideas that style and comfort can coexist, that softness and structure aren’t mutually exclusive, and that everyday style translates for the big moments, too. Co-founders Sarah Pierson and Alexa Buckley Roussel launched Margaux in 2015, setting out to create a footwear wardrobe for women on the go, powered by thoughtful design and an innovative approach to construction. The collection began with a classic ballet flat and has since grown into a full range of silhouettes. Each pair of Margaux shoes is designed in New York City, handmade in Spain, and thoughtfully crafted to withstand the test of time. Margaux is based in downtown New York City, with a satellite office in San Francisco and a team at our family-owned factory in southern Spain. For more about the brand, visit us online.

The role

Margaux is growing its wholesale business across marketplace, dropship, traditional and U.S. department store partners, and we’re looking for a Director of Wholesale to lead it. You’ll be the primary point of contact for our department store partners, the person buyers and merchants call first. You’ll also run wholesale like a business: you own the P&L, set strategy across channels, and know the numbers behind every decision. Our first U.S. department store rollout sits at the center of the plan. You’ll partner closely with our Senior Director of Merchandising on line planning, and with our Senior Manager of Wholesale and Operations, who own forecasting, allocation, reporting, order administration, fulfillment and retailer compliance.

What you'll do

  • Be the primary point of contact for executive, buyer and merchant relationships at our department store, marketplace and international partners.
  • Lead our department store rollout: door selection, the pace of adding doors, and a business case for each door.
  • Run seasonal business reviews with each partner on sell-through, door productivity and growth plans.
  • Find, pitch and onboard new accounts, including international and luxury partners, and lead brand presentations to new and existing partners.
  • Lead line planning for each account with Merchandising: category, depth and price tiers.
  • Lead market and line-review meetings, sell-in, assortment negotiation and buy commitments, through delivery and sell-through.
  • Set brand presentation standards on partner floors and training priorities for partner staff.
  • Own the wholesale P&L, annual budget and revenue targets, partnering with Finance and managing to weekly sales against plan.
  • Grow profitability by managing stock turn, margin, markdowns and returns.
  • Negotiate commercial terms: vendor agreements, margin and fee structures, co-op, markdown allowances and returns to vendor (RTVs).
  • Manage the wholesale marketing and co-op budget, with clear accountability for return on spend.
  • Set channel strategy across marketplace, dropship, department store and traditional wholesale, consistent with our own ecommerce and stores on price and brand.

What you bring

  • 10+ years in wholesale, sales or account management for a fashion, footwear or accessories brand, including 5+ in a senior, account-facing role.
  • Experience as the primary point of contact for a major U.S. department store, including a multi-door rollout, ideally in a category with many SKUs like footwear.
  • Real commercial and financial depth: you’ve owned a P&L and budget and can walk through one line by line. A background in business operations, strategy, consulting or a general manager role is a strong plus.
  • Hands-on experience across dropship, marketplace, ecommerce and department store channels, and a point of view on how they fit together.
  • A track record of launching or scaling a wholesale channel and opening new accounts.
  • Experience with line planning, negotiating commercial terms, and managing a co-op budget to ROI.
  • You’re as comfortable in a spreadsheet as in a buyer meeting, fluent in sell-through, stock turn and door productivity.
  • A builder’s mindset: you turn plans into results, question what you’re told (including AI output), and pick up new tools quickly.
  • Executive presence, with the credibility to represent Margaux to partner leadership.

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation commensurate with experience
  • Comprehensive benefits for eligible roles, which may include medical, dental and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company match, and paid time off
  • Paid sick leave
  • Employee discount on all Margaux products
  • A close-knit, mission-driven team culture
