About the Team

DoorDash is seeking a Manager, Technical Revenue Accounting to support complex revenue arrangements, new product offerings, and accounting policy alignment across its businesses.

This is an individual contributor role with responsibility for leading technical revenue accounting assessments for assigned business lines, products, and transactions. You will partner with Business Development, Product, Sales, Legal, Finance, and operational accounting teams to evaluate proposed contract terms and product offerings, explain their accounting and financial statement implications, and help stakeholders assess alternatives.

About the Role

You will apply US GAAP, particularly ASC 606, to complex transactions; document clear, well-supported accounting conclusions; and translate those conclusions into practical implementation requirements. This role offers exposure to a broad range of revenue streams and business initiatives and requires strong technical judgment, independent project ownership, and effective communication with business partners, accounting leadership, and external auditors.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead technical revenue accounting assessments. Research and evaluate complex or non-standard arrangements under ASC 606 and other applicable US GAAP, including merchant incentives and rebates, revenue guarantees, material rights, promotional programs, contract modifications, and principal versus agent considerations.
  • Advise on commercial arrangements and new products. Review proposed contracts, deal structures, and product offerings early in their development. Clearly explain accounting implications and evaluate alternatives to support informed business decisions.
  • Document accounting conclusions. Prepare technical accounting memos and position papers that clearly explain relevant facts, applicable guidance, significant judgments, and conclusions.
  • Support acquisition integration. Assess accounting policies and practices at acquired businesses, identify differences, and support alignment with DoorDash’s accounting policies.
  • Support operational implementation. Translate accounting conclusions into requirements for billing, revenue recognition, financial reporting, and controls, partnering with operational accounting teams to support accurate execution.
  • Strengthen policies, processes, and controls. Develop and maintain revenue accounting policies, guidance, and training materials, and identify opportunities to improve contract review processes and related controls.
  • Support audits and financial reporting. Work with accounting leadership and external auditors to address technical accounting questions, explain significant judgments, and support quarterly and annual reporting as needed.
  • Manage projects independently. Balance competing priorities, communicate review requirements and timelines, and escalate significant accounting issues or unresolved judgments promptly.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or a related field.
  • Six or more years of relevant accounting experience, including substantial experience applying ASC 606 to complex revenue arrangements.
  • Strong knowledge of US GAAP and demonstrated ability to research unfamiliar accounting issues, exercise sound judgment, and develop well-supported conclusions.
  • Experience reviewing commercial contracts and identifying the accounting implications of non-standard terms.
  • Demonstrated ability to prepare clear, persuasive technical accounting memos and position papers.
  • Experience supporting external audits and discussing technical accounting matters with auditors.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex accounting matters to non-accounting stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently, manage multiple projects, and collaborate effectively across functions in a fast-paced environment.
  • Relevant experience in public accounting, industry technical accounting, or a combination of both

Preferred Qualifications

  • CPA, ACA, ACCA, or equivalent professional accounting qualification.
  • Big 4 public accounting experience.
  • Experience with technology, marketplace, e-commerce, SaaS, or platform-based businesses.
  • Experience supporting post-acquisition integration and accounting policy alignment.
  • Familiarity with SOX requirements, internal controls over financial reporting, and accounting process design.
  • Experience translating technical accounting conclusions into operational processes and system requirements.

About DoorDash

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.

DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

jobs.title: Senior Research Scientist
jobs.excerpt: CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country.
jobs.description:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We have trained 50,000+ students from 1,000+ universities, and our alumni work at more than 4,000 companies. Our partners include Amazon, Google, and Microsoft. After nearly a decade training technical talent, we just launched Claude Corps, a $150M initiative with Anthropic, building one of the most ambitious AI workforce programs in the world.

About the Role

Location: Remote (US)
Role Type: Full-Time
Reporting to: Head of Measurement, Evaluation & Learning
Compensation: $130,000-$160,000

The Measurement, Evaluation & Learning (MEL) team owns CodePath's outcomes data and its evidence base. We are adding a Senior Research Scientist to lead our longer-term evaluation work, which includes overseeing third-party evaluators, designing and critiquing causal studies of our programs, and keeping our methods grounded in the current literature. You will work alongside data engineering and data science colleagues who build our pipelines and run rapid-cycle analyses, and you will own the slower, more rigorous research that those analyses cannot support on their own.

This is the first dedicated research hire on the team and the one that shapes it. In the first year you will lead the process of selecting an independent evaluator of record under a multi-year contract, and you will help decide what the research function looks like as it grows, including who we hire next. Because much of our work now involves AI, both as something we teach and evaluate and as a tool our own team uses daily, you will also set the standard for how AI is used responsibly in research at CodePath.

Who Will Thrive Here

This role calls for a generalist with broad methodological range and depth in no single domain. We are not looking for a national authority in one area such as CS education or workforce policy. We need someone who can evaluate a program in whichever context it presents, assess whether a proposed external evaluator is doing sound work in a domain they may not have studied, and bring on the right specialists when a question calls for one. Experience across several sectors, methods, or types of organization is a strength for us.

You are likely to do well if you are established enough to exercise independent judgment about study quality and still close enough to the work to run an analysis yourself. You are comfortable telling a leader that a claim goes further than the evidence allows, and you can do it in a way that helps them find the claim the evidence does support. CodePath is a nonprofit with a startup pace, which means priorities shift as programs and funding change, and the research function will be built while the work is happening. The research function is a core part of CodePath's scaling plan. People who enjoy shaping a function from an early stage will find that appealing, and people who prefer a settled structure may not.

What You'll Do

  • Scope, procure, and manage external evaluators, including drafting the request for proposals, scoring responses, negotiating contracts, reviewing study designs and deliverables, and judging whether an evaluator's methods can answer the question we are asking
  • Design, lead and run evaluations yourself across a range of settings and methods, from surveys and qualitative work to quasi-experimental and randomized designs, choosing the approach that fits the question and the data we can realistically obtain
  • Evaluate CodePath programs that teach AI skills or use AI-assisted learning (with the aim of creating pathways for economic mobility), including whether students build specific skills, develop agency, and see their workforce outcomes hold up as the labor market for AI-era roles changes
  • Work with other cross-functional teams to identify, understand, and guide research implementation
  • Set and maintain norms for AI in our research workflow, such as where AI-assisted analysis is appropriate, what human review it requires, and how we check outputs before anything reaches a funder
  • Translate findings into claims the organization can defend externally, and flag claims that exceed the evidence
  • Work with data scientists on measurement problems such as survey design, attrition, and the limits of employment data, and help the team distinguish directional analyses from causal ones
  • Manage and work with independent third-party evaluators and research partners running quasi-experimental design (QED) studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to understand the causal effect of CodePath's programs
  • Track the evaluation, CS education, and AI-in-education literatures, and keep our theory of change and logic model consistent with them
  • Help define the research function as it grows, including the roles we add next and the standards we hold them to

What Success Looks Like

In your first 3 months you will learn our programs, our data, and our existing evidence, review the studies already underway with outside partners, and take ownership of the evaluator RFP with the Head of MEL. By month 6 the RFP is issued and you are leading proposal review with CodePath leadership. By month 12 an evaluator is selected and under contract, the first national quasi-experimental study is in design, and you are running at least 1 internal evaluation of your own, most likely a study of learning outcomes within a semester.

What We're Looking For

  • PhD in education research, economics, public policy, psychology, or a related field, or equivalent applied experience
  • At least 3-4 years of applied evaluation experience, enough to have run studies from design through reporting and to still do the analysis yourself
  • Experience designing and conducting program evaluations in more than one context, ideally including matching, difference-in-differences, or randomized designs, along with qualitative and survey methods
  • Experience working with or as an external evaluator, including scoping, procuring, and reviewing studies
  • Working fluency with R or Python, and comfort working with analysts who use AI coding and analysis tools, plus the judgment to review that work critically
  • Clear writing for both technical and funder audiences
  • Experience in workforce development, education, or AI, for example evaluating AI-assisted learning or AI-enabled programs. Candidates with experience in at least 1 of these areas will be prioritized

Nice to Have

  • Experience with institutional review board (IRB) approval processes
  • Experience designing and conducting research that is used directly for program improvement or informing organizational decisionmaking
  • Experience with administrative wage or employment data, including record matching and the problems of measurement error and missing data
  • Familiarity with preregistration and with evidence standards such as the ESSA tiers or the What Works Clearinghouse
  • Experience writing for or reporting to funders

Compensation

CodePath has standardized salaries based on the position’s level, no matter where you live. For this role, we’re hiring for a senior level position at an annual salary of $130,000 to $160,000. Salary is determined based on your relevant experience and skills as evaluated through our interview process.

Full-Time Employee Benefits

This is a remote position—work from anywhere in the US! CodePath prioritizes employee well-being with a competitive benefits package to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.

  • Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance (90% employer-covered for employees and dependents), employer-funded healthcare reimbursement, FSAs, and Employee Assistance Program
  • Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection
  • Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, paid holidays, 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave, and an annual year-end company closure (Dec 24 – Jan 2)
  • Professional Growth: $1,000 annual professional development stipend and home office setup support
  • ​​Student Loan Forgiveness: CodePath is a qualifying employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), helping employees manage student loan debt
  • Additional Perks: Pet wellness plans, legal services, home/auto insurance discounts, and exclusive marketplace savings

jobs.excerpt: What we do SmartCat designs, builds, and delivers software for clients across Europe and the US.
jobs.description:
What we do

SmartCat designs, builds, and delivers software for clients across Europe and the US. One of our larger engagements is a high-traffic platform that runs around the clock. It's dozens of services on Java and Kafka, and several teams from several companies build on it and ship into the same production environment.

A platform like that needs somebody who owns how it all fits together. You decide where a new product goes and what it's allowed to touch, you explain to the client what that decision costs and what it buys them, and then you sit down with the team and build the hard part yourself. We're not looking for an architect who draws the diagram and leaves.

What you'll own

  • Architecture and technical direction. You own the target architecture and the technical roadmap that gets us there from what's running today: service boundaries, data ownership, event contracts, integrations with third parties. You keep it written down, in ADRs and diagrams that stay current, so a new engineer can find out why something is the way it is.
  • Decisions in business context. Every architectural decision here has a price in delivery time, running cost and production risk. You put the options in front of the client with that price attached, recommend one, and stand behind it. Quite often the right answer is the boring one.
  • Client and stakeholders. You're our senior technical voice on the account. You talk with the client's technical and business leadership, with the leads from other vendors, and with our own account and program managers. You can explain a trade-off to somebody who doesn't write code and argue it with somebody who does.
  • Leading by example. You implement what you advise. You build the reference implementation, the first service on a new pattern, the proof of concept that settles an argument. When a delivery is in trouble or there's a serious production incident, you're on the front line with the engineers until it's sorted.
  • Technical leadership across teams. You run design reviews and set the standards teams build to, and you make sure those standards are followed because they make sense to the people using them. You mentor team leads and senior engineers, so that over time more people on the account can make these calls.
  • Discovery and estimates. New work starts with a discovery and ends as a scoped proposal. The team leads and delivery managers scope it, and you make sure the solution fits the platform: what has to be built, what it depends on, what could go wrong. We commit to the client on the basis of that estimate, so you challenge it until it holds.
  • Quality attributes. Performance, availability, security, data consistency, cost. You define what the platform has to meet, peak load and recovery targets included, you make sure it's measured, and you act when it isn't met.
  • Evolving a live system. The platform is never switched off, so nothing gets rewritten from scratch. You decide which technical debt gets paid down and in what order, and you plan migrations that don't stop the business.
  • Technology choices. You decide what comes into the stack and what stays out. Anything new has to earn its place against what it will cost us to run and to hire for.

Where you sit

On the engagement you work closely with the Engineering Manager, the Program Manager and the Account Manager, and on the client side with the business owners of each initiative and with senior stakeholders up to executive level. Every team owns a domain of the platform and has a team lead, and the team leads are your closest counterparts day to day. Architecture within our scope is your call. That includes saying no when something would hurt the platform, even if the client would rather hear yes.

What we work with

This is the stack. You don't need to have used every item on the list, but Java, Kafka and the data stores have to be home ground.

  • Architecture: event-driven services in a hexagonal layout, talking mostly over Kafka, with REST where a synchronous call is needed
  • Backend: Java 21, Spring Boot 3, Project Reactor
  • Messaging and streaming: Kafka, Kafka Streams, Avro with Schema Registry
  • Data: PostgreSQL, Cassandra, Elasticsearch and OpenSearch, Redis
  • Infrastructure: Oracle Cloud, AWS and on-premise, Docker, Kubernetes, Ansible
  • CI/CD: GitLab CI

Information Technology oversees the effective development, delivery, and operation of computing and information services. This function anticipates, plans, and delivers Information Technology solutions and strategies that enable operations and drive business value.

Reporting to the Director, Cyber Risk Services, this role serves as a primary engagement point for Cardinal Health’s solution owners and business stakeholders, facilitating intake, clarifying requirements, coordinating risk activities, and driving work from initiation through implementation and operational adoption.

Shift5 is building the data platform for onboard operational technology (OT). We deliver cybersecurity, predictive maintenance, and compliance capabilities that enable defense and commercial fleets to operate with greater readiness, resilience, and mission assurance.

Develop system context and preliminary architecture; identify interfaces, data flows, and top-level capability needs; and begin documenting assumptions, constraints, government-furnished equipment (GFE), risks, and commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) considerations. As opportunities mature, transition this context and supporting artifacts to the responsible Program and Engineering teams.

  • Technical validation and transition. For qualified opportunities, work with Engineering and Programs to validate feasibility, manage technical commitments, and enable a clean transition into execution. Remain engaged through the planning stage and consult thereafter as needed to preserve customer and mission context.
  • Reusable solution assets. Own and maintain modular proposal content, demonstration environments, customer win vignettes, and briefing packages for rapid reuse across the Account Executive team.

  • Produce credible, reusable technical content that improves customer discussions and reduces downstream rework.

Applications for this position will be accepted through December 14, 2026. Koniag Data Solutions, LLC a Koniag Government Services company, is seeking a Platform Administrator – Ansible / Security / Middleware to support KDS and our government customer. The position is remote. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) retirement plan, paid time off, paid parental leave, life and disability insurance, flexible spending accounts, commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement. The Platform Administrator will provide administration, maintenance, security remediation, automation, and operational support for enterprise middleware platforms and associated application environments. The position will have a primary technical focus on Ansible automation, platform security remediation, vulnerability management, and middleware administration. The administrator will work with Security, Infrastructure, and Application teams to identify and remediate platform vulnerabilities, implement automated configuration changes, and improve the security and operational stability of enterprise systems. Although automation and security remediation will be the primary areas of specialization, the administrator will be responsible for supporting all enterprise platforms managed by the Platform Support team. Essential Functions, Responsibilities & Duties may include, but are not limited to:

Ansible Automation and Security Remediation:

Develop, maintain, and execute Ansible playbooks and automation workflows to support enterprise middleware administration and security remediation. Implement automated configuration changes, patching activities, software updates, and security hardening across supported platform environments. Review vulnerability scan findings and coordinate remediation activities with Security, Linux, Windows, and Application teams. Investigate and remediate security vulnerabilities affecting middleware platforms, Java runtimes, web servers, application servers, and supporting software components. Support remediation of vulnerabilities identified through enterprise security scanning and compliance assessments. Evaluate remediation requirements, determine application and platform dependencies, and assess potential operational impacts before implementing changes. Develop and maintain repeatable automation processes for security remediation, patch deployment, configuration management, and platform maintenance. Validate security remediation activities through testing, vulnerability rescanning, and documented verification procedures. Assist with remediation of outdated software components, unsupported runtimes, insecure configurations, and SSL/TLS vulnerabilities. Support implementation of security configuration standards and hardening requirements across Development, Test, and Production environments. Maintain documentation of vulnerability findings, remediation actions, implementation procedures, and validation results. Coordinate security remediation activities through established Change Management processes. Identify opportunities to reduce manual administrative tasks through automation and standardized procedures. Support Git-based version control and change tracking for Ansible playbooks, configuration files, and automation scripts.

General Platform Administration:

Duties will include approximately 60% platform administration and 40% application support. Install, configure, administer, and maintain enterprise middleware platforms and related computing environments. Maintain platform services through patching, upgrades, configuration changes, and ongoing operational support. Diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve platform and application service issues. Support developer application deployments and perform Production application release deployments. Perform daily application health checks and monitor platform availability across Development, Test, and Production environments. Participate in the on-call rotation and respond to incidents, service requests, and production outages according to established SLAs. Manage assigned incidents, service requests, and change tickets, including troubleshooting, resolution, and documentation. Support SSL/TLS certificate installation, renewal, and troubleshooting. Assist with middleware upgrades, Java runtime maintenance, and application server configuration changes. Coordinate with Development, Infrastructure, Network, Security, Database, and IAM teams to resolve technical issues. Maintain architecture documentation, operational procedures, automation documentation, and knowledge-base articles. Participate in cross-training and develop working knowledge of all platforms and applications supported by the team.

Basic Qualifications:

Must be a U.S. Citizen with the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust security clearance. Hands-on experience using Ansible for configuration management, system administration, automation, or security remediation. Experience administering or supporting Linux and/or Windows Server environments. Experience performing software patching, configuration changes, security updates, or vulnerability remediation. Working knowledge of enterprise middleware platforms, application servers, or web servers. Experience with scripting and automation technologies such as Bash, Python, PowerShell, or YAML. Familiarity with Git and version control processes. Understanding of operating system security, application security, and vulnerability management concepts. Working knowledge of SSL/TLS, certificates, Java runtimes, and web application infrastructure. Experience troubleshooting system services, application logs, configuration errors, and connectivity issues. Familiarity with ITIL processes, incident management, and change management. Ability to support multiple enterprise platforms and learn new technologies.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience developing reusable Ansible roles, playbooks, inventories, and automation workflows. Experience using Ansible Automation Platform or AWX. Experience automating security remediation across Red Hat Enterprise Linux and Windows Server environments. Familiarity with vulnerability scanning tools such as Tenable Nessus, Tenable.sc, or comparable enterprise scanning platforms. Experience implementing DISA STIGs, CIS Benchmarks, or other enterprise security configuration standards. Experience remediating vulnerabilities affecting Oracle WebLogic, Apache HTTP Server, Tomcat, JBoss, Java runtimes, or other middleware technologies. Experience with automated patching, configuration drift detection, and compliance validation. Familiarity with Jenkins, Git, Nexus, and CI/CD automation. Experience with SSL/TLS configuration, Java keystores, certificate chains, and PKI. Familiarity with Broadcom SiteMinder, Okta, MuleSoft, Salesforce, or Oracle Siebel. Experience supporting security remediation activities in federal government environments. Strong troubleshooting, documentation, communication, and analytical skills. Experience administering, configuring, maintaining, and troubleshooting Relativity eDiscovery environments, including application support, system performance monitoring, upgrades, and security remediation.

Supported Platforms and Technologies:

The administrator will be expected to develop and maintain working knowledge of the team's supported technologies, including:

Automation and Configuration Management:

Ansible, Ansible Automation Platform, AWX, Git, Jenkins, Nexus, Bash, Python, PowerShell, WLST, YAML.

Security and Vulnerability Management:

Security scanning tools, DISA STIGs, CIS Benchmarks, SSL/TLS, PKI, DigiCert, Microsoft Certificate Services, HashiCorp Vault.

Oracle Middleware:

WebLogic Server, SOA Suite, Oracle Service Bus, Oracle ADF, Oracle HTTP Server, Oracle Portal.

Integration and CRM:

MuleSoft Anypoint Platform, CloudHub, Salesforce, Oracle Siebel.

Identity and Access Management:

Broadcom SiteMinder, Okta, SAML, LDAP, Active Directory.

Web and Application Servers:

Apache HTTP Server, Apache Tomcat, JBoss/WildFly, Microsoft IIS.

Operating Systems:

Red Hat Enterprise Linux and Windows Server.

Monitoring and ITSM:

ServiceNow, application monitoring, log analysis, and platform health monitoring.

BI Full Stack Developer

Location: India, Remote

Growth through diversity, equity, and inclusion. As an ethical business, we do what is right — including ensuring equal opportunities and fostering a safe, respectful workplace for each of us. What You'll Be Doing:

  • Data ingestion and Bronze layer (Databricks)
  • Ingest raw files (CSV, JSON, Parquet, Excel) from ADLS / S3 / landing zones into Databricks.
  • Build Bronze Delta tables from raw files using PySpark and Spark SQL, with schema handling, audit columns (load date, source file) and incremental loads (Auto Loader, COPY INTO or MERGE).
  • Register and manage tables in Unity Catalog (catalogs, schemas, permissions).
  • Silver and Gold layers (medallion architecture)
  • Design and implement the medallion architecture (Bronze → Silver → Gold) following Lakehouse best practices.
  • Create Silver views/tables: cleansing, de-duplication, type casting, standardisation, joins and business rules.
  • Create Gold views/tables: star-schema facts and dimensions, aggregates and KPI-ready datasets for reporting.
  • Write reusable, parameterised Databricks notebooks (PySpark + SQL) and orchestrate them with Databricks Workflows / Jobs.
  • Apply data quality checks, SCD handling where needed, and Delta optimisations (OPTIMIZE, Z-ORDER / liquid clustering, VACUUM, partitioning).
  • Power BI connectivity and consumption:
  • Connect Power BI to Databricks Gold views via the Databricks connector / SQL Warehouse, choosing Import, DirectQuery or composite mode based on volume and latency.
  • Configure gateways, scheduled refresh, incremental refresh and secure access (service principals, Unity Catalog grants).
  • Unity Catalog Metric Views and AI/BI Genie:
  • Define Unity Catalog Metric Views (YAML-based) on top of Gold tables: governed dimensions, measures and joins, so KPIs are defined once and reused across Power BI, SQL and dashboards.
  • Query and validate metrics with the MEASURE() function; manage ownership, comments and grants in Unity Catalog.
  • Set up and curate AI/BI Genie spaces over Gold tables and Metric Views: table/column descriptions, instructions, example SQL and trusted assets so business users get accurate natural-language answers.
  • Monitor Genie usage and feedback, and refine metadata and instructions to improve answer quality.

What We're Looking For:

  • 7+ years of overall experience in Business Intelligence, Data Engineering, or Analytics solutions.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Databricks and Power BI is mandatory.
  • Good experience with PySpark, SQL, Delta Lake, and building data transformation pipelines in Databricks.
  • Experience developing Power BI dashboards, data models, reports, and KPI-driven analytics.
  • Good understanding of Lakehouse/Medallion Architecture and end-to-end data flow from ingestion through reporting.
  • Experience working with cloud data platforms such as Azure/ADLS, with knowledge of data governance and performance optimization.

    • Nice to have:

    Certifications:

  • Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate (PL-300)
  • Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate / Professional.

  • Stable employment. On the market since 2008, 1500+ talents currently on board in 7 global sites.

  • Flexibility regarding working hours and your preferred form of contract.

Humana’s MarketPoint organization is seeking a collaborative and results-driven Senior Learning Design Professional to join the MarketPoint Training team. The Senior Learning Design Professional serves as a strategic learning and performance consultant, partnering with business leaders and cross-functional teams to identify performance needs, analyze root causes, and design targeted solutions that improve associate readiness, business performance, compliance, and member experience. This role supports complex and high-impact business priorities, including Stars and CTM initiatives, by translating business needs, performance data, quality insights, compliance requirements, and learner needs into effective learning and performance strategies.

The Senior Learning Design Professional leads work across the full solution lifecycle, including discovery and analysis, strategy, solution design, stakeholder alignment, development, implementation, measurement, and continuous improvement. This role works across multiple audiences and channels and helps determine when formal learning is needed as well as when performance support, communications, coaching, process improvements, or other interventions may provide a more effective solution.

  • Identify, manage, and escalate risks, dependencies, scope changes, resource needs, and decisions that could impact learner readiness or successful implementation

Instructional Design & Facilitation

  • Design and develop learning and performance solutions including assessments, eLearning, instructor-led and virtual learning, simulations, microlearning, job aids, FAQs, performance support, communications, and leader or coaching resources
  • Apply adult learning, instructional design, performance consulting, accessibility, and learner-experience principles to create effective and practical solutions

  • Prototype, test, and refine learning and performance solutions with target audiences, business partners, and subject matter experts when appropriate
  • Facilitate discovery sessions, workshops, learning sessions, and stakeholder discussions that support performance improvement and business readiness

  • Measure knowledge and performance improvement through pre- and post-assessments or other appropriate evaluation methods
  • Evaluate whether learning and performance interventions achieved the intended outcomes and recommend adjustments when results indicate additional support is needed

Change Management & Communication

  • Develop implementation and deployment strategies that prepare associates, leaders, and business partners for changes in processes, systems, products, benefits, tools, policies, or expectations
  • Assess business and learner readiness and identify adoption risks that could impact successful implementation
  • Develop stakeholder, leader, learner, and audience-specific communication strategies that support awareness, readiness, adoption, and sustainment
  • Coordinate with Learning Systems, Communications, Operations, Reporting, technology teams, and business leaders to support successful implementation across multiple audiences and channels
  • Provide clear project updates and executive-level summaries communicating progress, business impact, risks, outcomes, and recommendations
  • Capture implementation learnings and incorporate them into future strategies and repeatable processes


Use your skills to make an impact

  • Bachelor's degree in Education, Instructional Design, Organizational Development, Business, or a related field, OR equivalent related professional experience
  • 5+ years of experience in learning design, performance consulting, curriculum development, organizational effectiveness or learning strategy, preferably within healthcare, sales, service, or another regulated environment

  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional learning or performance initiatives from discovery and strategy through implementation and measurement
  • Expertise in adult learning principles, instructional design methodologies, performance consulting, and learning technologies
  • Experience using quantitative and qualitative data to identify performance opportunities, develop recommendations, and evaluate solution effectiveness
  • Experience establishing learning and performance measurement strategies and connecting learning outcomes to broader business objectives
  • Experience partnering with business leaders, analytics and reporting teams, compliance partners, operational teams, subject matter experts, and other cross-functional stakeholders
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple stakeholders, deliverables, workstreams, risks, dependencies, and competing priorities within complex initiatives

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience partnering with Business Intelligence and Reporting teams and using Power BI or similar reporting and data-visualization tools to support performance measurement and decision-making

jobs.description:
This is a hands-on role that requires balancing the needs of today with the architecture of tomorrow. You will move between operational engineering, business analyst, automation design, cloud planning, infrastructure as code, and longer-term technology strategy. Success means solving immediate problems without creating tomorrow's problems, building solutions that are secure, repeatable, supportable, and aligned with our direction.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own and evolve key parts of our Microsoft 365 environment, including SharePoint Online and Power Platform, ensuring services are well-designed, governed, and supported.
  • Design and build SharePoint, Power Automate, and Power Apps solutions that simplify business processes, eliminate unnecessary manual work, and make better use of the Microsoft capabilities we have and ones that we are not yet using.
  • Establish practical standards and reusable patterns for automation, workflows, governance, and solution lifecycle management. The goal is not simply to automate something once, but to create simple approaches we can confidently use again.
  • Provide technical leadership as we continue evolving our Azure and hybrid environment, assessing existing infrastructure and applications to determine where cloud migration, modernization, or hybrid integration creates meaningful value.
  • Work directly with end users to understand business workflows and create processes, solutions, and automations to make them more efficient.
  • Design, implement, and support Azure and hybrid infrastructure with security, reliability, governance, and supportability built in from the start.
  • Automate the provisioning, configuration, and maintenance of Azure and hybrid infrastructure, using infrastructure as code and repeatable deployment patterns to improve consistency, reduce risk, and make change easier.
  • Identify manual work hiding in our infrastructure and operations and find practical ways to eliminate it. We want automation that makes us faster and more reliable, not automation simply for the sake of automation.
  • Stay ahead of changes across the Microsoft ecosystem, particularly Azure, Microsoft 365, automation, and AI, and help us separate capabilities that can materially improve the business from those that are simply interesting.

Why this role Matters:

This role connects business productivity with the infrastructure that makes it possible. It is key to the company leveraging key Microsoft services such as Sharepoint Online, Microsoft 365, and Copilot, while enabling a stronger ability to leverage elastic cloud resources. Done well, the work reduces manual effort, improves consistency and resilience, strengthens security, and helps teams adopt cloud and automation capabilities with confidence.

Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of hands-on experience administering Microsoft 365 and SharePoint Online and building or supporting Power Automate workflows and Power Apps solutions.
  • 3+ years of experience improving Azure services, cloud infrastructure, and hybrid Microsoft environments, including cloud migration and infrastructure modernization.
  • Demonstrated experience creating scripts, automation, and infrastructure-as-code artifacts that solve real business and technical problems.
  • Proven knowledge of firewalls, VPNs, network segmentation, identity, access control, security, monitoring, and disaster recovery principles.
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot effectively under pressure, clearly document and communicate potential solutions, drive consensus, and create artifacts that support reliable, repeatable processes.
  • A track record of creating practical, reusable solutions that balance speed and immediate needs with longer-term modernization goals.
  • Additional experience that could add value includes relevant Microsoft certifications and experience with Azure networking, PowerShell scripting, Power Platform and Copilot/AI governance, business continuity design and implementation across hybrid environments, and co-location management and maintenance.

The Language You’ll Speak

You will not need to know every platform on day one, but you should be comfortable learning and working across the technologies that shape our Microsoft and infrastructure environment.

  • Microsoft 365 and productivity: SharePoint Online, Teams, OneDrive, Exchange Online, Power Platform, Power Automate, Power Apps, governance, and lifecycle management.
  • Cloud and automation: Azure, hybrid integration, PowerShell, Terraform, Bicep, ARM templates, source control, deployment automation, and infrastructure as code.
  • Infrastructure and operations: Nutanix, Windows Server, SolarWinds, monitoring, backup, disaster recovery, firewalls, VPNs, networking, patching, performance, and incident management.
  • Emerging capabilities: Microsoft Copilot, AI-enabled automation, cloud modernization, and practical adoption of new Microsoft services.

Your Success Metrics

Success in this role will be measured by the answers to a few practical questions:

  • Are our business and technology processes becoming simpler, faster, and automated?
  • Are we getting greater value from Microsoft 365 and SharePoint Online while making those environments more cost-effective, secure, reliable, and performant?
  • Are our Azure and hybrid environments becoming more scalable, resilient, cost-efficient, secure, and supportable?
  • Are we creating simpler, flexible, and reusable automation and infrastructure patterns instead of one-time solutions?
  • Are our cloud migration and modernization decisions producing clear business and technical value?
  • Are our monitoring, backup, recovery, business continuity, and operational practices improving resilience and reducing risk?
  • Are we advancing the team's knowledge and effective use of Microsoft technologies, particularly Azure, automation, and AI, including Copilot?

Location:

  • Position is remote and the location of candidate is flexible within the U.S.

Role Description

As an Offensive Security Engineer within Dropbox Security, you will investigate how attackers could compromise our products and infrastructure, including AI-enabled applications and agentic systems. You will help identify meaningful attack paths and improve the controls intended to prevent, detect or contain them.

This is a hands-on offensive security and threat research role with broad scope and meaningful impact. You will contribute to investigations and multi-phase red team exercises, help prioritize work based on risk, develop attack techniques, and build tooling and automation that expand the reach of our security testing. You will apply practical AI security knowledge alongside broader offensive security skills across applications, cloud infrastructure, and identity systems. Working closely with experienced researchers and partners across Product Security, Detection & Response, Threat Intelligence, Privacy, and engineering, you will help translate technical findings into clear business risk, recommend practical improvements, and validate their effectiveness through retesting. Sound judgment, clear communication, responsible execution, and ownership of your work are essential to the role. You will contribute to the Red Team’s tools, research methods, and testing practices while developing your own areas of expertise, investigating emerging technologies, and helping advance Dropbox’s offensive security capabilities. You will have opportunities to deepen your skills, publish research, take on increasingly complex projects, and see your work influence security decisions across Dropbox.

Our Engineering Career Framework is viewable by anyone outside the company and describes what’s expected for our engineers at each of our career levels. Check out our blog post on this topic and more here.

Responsibilities

  • Plan and execute offensive security assessments by defining objectives, scope, rules of engagement, and safeguards, adapting your approach as new evidence emerges.
  • Investigate unfamiliar applications, infrastructure, APIs, and trust boundaries to identify and trace meaningful attack paths.
  • Develop and safely demonstrate exploits and attack chains that clearly establish potential impact to Dropbox.
  • Build and improve offensive security tools, agents, automation, and testing harnesses, ensuring results are reliable, repeatable, and appropriately validated.
  • Assess security risks across AI-enabled applications, agents, tool integrations, and supporting infrastructure, including the responsible use of AI-assisted research techniques.
  • Partner with security, privacy, legal, and engineering teams to communicate risk, strengthen prevention and detection capabilities, address root causes, and verify improvements through retesting.

Many teams at Dropbox run Services with on-call rotations, which entails being available for calls during both core and non-core business hours. If a team has an on-call rotation, all engineers on the team are expected to participate in the rotation as part of their employment. Applicants are encouraged to ask for more details of the rotations to which the applicant is applying.

Requirements

  • 5+ years in offensive security, vulnerability research, red teaming or closely related security engineering, or equivalent demonstrated capability.
  • A track record of independently leading complex investigations or engagements and discovering and exploiting non-trivial vulnerabilities.
  • Understanding of application security, authentication and authorisation, cloud infrastructure, APIs and software supply chains, with deep practical expertise in one or more areas and the ability to trace attack paths across systems and trust boundaries.
  • Hands-on experience attacking or evaluating LLMs, AI agents, ML systems, AI-enabled applications, or agentic architectures.
  • Familiarity with security risks in AI-enabled applications, agents and tool integrations, and the ability to investigate unfamiliar technologies.
  • Ability to write code to build or adapt offensive tools and automation, and to read and investigate unfamiliar production codebases.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience developing novel attacks, repeatable security evaluations or testing frameworks for AI-enabled systems, or building and validating AI-assisted offensive research capabilities.
  • Expertise across multiple attack surfaces, or advanced specialist capability in areas such as exploit development, reverse engineering, endpoint security, cloud exploitation or software supply-chain attacks.
  • Experience developing automated vulnerability discovery, fuzzing, program analysis or evaluation systems across large codebases or complex environments.
  • Experience conducting coordinated exercises with defenders to measure detection and response effectiveness and validate improvements against realistic attack techniques.
  • Contributions through original research, vulnerability disclosures, open-source tools, technical publications, internal training or mentoring.

Durable Skills

AI fluency means using these tools to amplify human judgment, not replace it. We believe people with these skills will thrive as work and technologycontinue to evolve:

  • Awareness:Understand yourself and others.
  • Judgment:Evaluate information and make decisions in complex situations.
  • Adaptability:Learn, adjust, and stay effective through change.
  • Connection:Communicate, collaborate, and build trust.

To learn more about why these skills matter and what the data shows about thriving through change, read this blog postfrom our Chief People Officer, Melanie Rosenwasser.

Position Summary:

  • Generate potential site list from key stakeholders and drive site feasibility process
  • Identify potential risks to the enrollment targets based on feasibility analysis and site’s contracted commitment
  • Develop and finalize the country recruitment/retention strategy

  • Lead internal clinical team meetings and sets expectations for clinical team of CRAs and CTAs
  • Address all CRA and site questions and maintains Frequently Asked Question (FAQ) log as appropriate
  • Support in planning and conducting investigator meetings
  • Review and/or approve of IP release packages
  • Oversee, support and track all submissions and approvals to Competent Authorities and IRB/Ethics Committees in conjunction with regulatory departments as applicable

  • Generate and utilizes metric reporting (e.g., CTMS, DM Query Trends, Outstanding Monitoring Reports) to ensure that the study is conducted per plan and communicates issues to PM and CRAs as appropriate
  • Responsible for eTMF implementation and management

  • Accountable to assist sites, internal staff and CRAs with the preparation for GCP audits
  • Work closely with PM for project-specific resourcing issues
  • Escalate pertinent CRA performance and site compliance issues when necessary

Preferred:

Other Required:

  • Experience with Microsoft Office Products (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to effectively interface with others in a team setting
  • Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and a customer service demeanor
  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally including overnight stays

Competencies:

  • Demonstrates mastery knowledge of ICH-GCP, relevant Precision SOPs, and regulatory guidance, as well as the ability to implement
  • Working knowledge of clinical management techniques and tools
  • Direct work experience in a cross-functional environment
  • Proven experience in functional management including proven experience in delegating while fostering cohesive team dynamics
  • Proven experience in planning, risk management and change management
  • High level of integrity and must inspire and demand the highest standards from a professional and ethical perspective
  • Ability to lead and inspire excellence within a team
  • Ability to create an environment where employees have a sense of ownership that will lead to increases in productivity and efficiency
  • Results oriented, accountable, motivated and flexible
  • Excellent time management, negotiation, critical thinking, decision making, analytical and interpersonal skills
  • Excellent presentation, verbal and written communications skills

Job Details:

CLUB CADDIE

Every course, one move ahead

Head of Enterprise Sales (MCO)

Sales & Marketing | Reports to: President/Chief Revenue Officer | Travel: ~50% | Full-Time


ABOUT CLUB CADDIE

Club Caddie is a fast-growing golf course management software (GMS) company and a member of the Jonas Software family, a division of Constellation Software Inc. (TSX: CSU). Our platform is the operating system for golf — unifying point of sale, tee sheet, member management, food and beverage, and payments into a single connected system for public, semi-private, and multi-course operators.

We are built by operators, for operators, and our brand is anchored in four commitments: Unified Operations, Intelligent Action, Revenue Momentum, and Hospitality Memory. As Club Caddie scales its footprint with the country's largest multi-course operators (MCOs), we're investing in the enterprise sales leadership to match that ambition.


THE ROLE

The Head of Enterprise Sales owns Club Caddie's go-to-market motion for Multi-Course Operators (MCO) — management companies and ownership groups operating multiple golf facilities across the country. This is a hunting, value-building, and relationship-building role for a seasoned enterprise sales leader who knows how to navigate long, complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles and close large agreements.

You will report directly to the Chief Revenue Officer and work in close partnership with Marketing, Product, Implementation, and Customer Experience to build a durable pipeline of MCO logos, from first conversation through signed agreement and a clean handoff to post-sales. The base salary range for this role is between $110,000 - $120,000.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own the MCO Sales Motion

  • Build and execute a strategic account plan targeting the top multi-course operators in the U.S. and Canada, prioritizing accounts by fit, size, and strategic value.
  • Manage a complex, multi-stakeholder sales pipeline in the CRM with rigor — accurate staging, next steps, forecasted close dates, and clear next steps on every opportunity.
  • Lead the full sales cycle: prospecting, discovery, solution design, ROI/business case development, procurement, contracting, and close through an enterprise level sales methodology.

Build Executive Relationships

  • Develop value-based relationships with C-suite and operations leaders (CEO, COO, VP of Golf Operations, CIO) at management companies and ownership groups.
  • Represent Club Caddie at industry events — NGCOA, the MCO Retreat (MCOR), and other regional and national golf industry gatherings — to build pipeline and deepen existing relationships.
  • Act as a trusted advisor, bringing a point of view on how technology can solve real operational and financial challenges across a multi-course portfolio.

Negotiate and Close Complex Deals

  • Lead commercial negotiations on multi-year, multi-property agreements, balancing win rate, margin, and long-term account health.
  • Partner with Finance, Legal, and Implementation to structure deals that are commercially sound and operationally deliverable.
  • Manage competitive displacement deals against incumbent point-of-sale and tee sheet providers with a clear, defensible value narrative.

Drive Cross-Functional Alignment

  • Partner with Marketing and the Director of Digital on MCO-specific campaigns, collateral, and messaging that support the pipeline.
  • Work closely with the Executive, Product, Customer Experience, and Sales teams to translate enterprise buyer feedback into product improvements, market awareness, and competitor insights.
  • Ensure a clean, well-documented handoff from sales to implementation for every closed account, protecting the customer experience from contract to go-live.

Forecasting & Performance

  • Own MCO segment forecasting and pipeline reporting, contributing accurate inputs to company-wide revenue scorecards and QBRs.
  • Track and report on key metrics: pipeline coverage, deal velocity, win rate, average contract value, and sales cycle length.
  • Manage deals through a formal sales methodology e.g. MEDDIC, MEDDPIC, etc… to ensure internal and external alignment.
  • Continuously refine MCO sales playbooks, pricing strategy, and competitive positioning based on what's working in the field.
  • Achieve or exceed the annual targets for MCO sales including new logo and back-to-base revenue targets.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • 7+ years of enterprise or complex B2B sales experience, with a track record of closing large, multi-stakeholder agreements; SaaS, hospitality, or golf/club industry experience strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated success selling into complex organizations with long sales cycles and layered decision-making (procurement, ops, IT, finance, executive) leveraging enterprise sales methodologies.
  • Previous success creating value and desire across an entire organization including decision makers and deal champions.
  • Strong commercial negotiation skills, with experience structuring multi-year, enterprise-wide contracts.
  • Exceptional value-building instincts — comfortable and credible in a room with C-suite executives and front-line operators alike.
  • Highly organized and data-driven; disciplined about CRM hygiene, pipeline accuracy, and forecasting.
  • Willingness and ability to travel approximately 50% of the time for industry events, on-site customer meetings, and prospect visits.
  • Self-directed and resilient — comfortable building a territory and a pipeline largely from the ground up.
  • Genuine interest in or connection to the golf industry is a strong plus, but not required.

WHY JOIN CLUB CADDIE

  • Own a high-impact, high-visibility segment of the business, with a direct line to the CRO and executive team.
  • Sell a genuinely differentiated, unified platform into an industry that is actively consolidating around modern technology.
  • Competitive base plus uncapped commission, benefits, and the backing of Jonas Software and Constellation Software's scale and stability.
  • Be part of shaping the next chapter of Club Caddie's MCO strategy, not just executing an existing playbook.

Club Caddie is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Jonas Software is a leading provider of enterprise management software solutions, serving a wide range of vertical markets including hospitality, healthcare, construction, education, personal care, fitness, leisure, moving and legal services, to name a few. Within these markets, Jonas is comprised of over 65 distinct brands, each a respected leader in its domain.

Jonas’ vision is to be the branded global leader across these verticals and to be recognized by customers and industry stakeholders as the trusted provider of “Software for Life.” We are committed to technology, product innovation, quality, and exceptional customer service.

Jonas Software supports over 60,000 customers in more than 30 countries. We employ over 6,000 skilled professionals, including industry experts and technology specialists. Across our broader network, we support a global workforce of more than 30,000 employees.

Headquartered in Canada, Jonas Software has a global footprint with offices around the world. We’re a 100% owned subsidiary of Constellation Software Inc., based in Toronto, publicly listed on the TSX (CSU.TO), and a member of the S&P/TSX 60 Index.

jobs.title: Senior Mobile Engineer — Mobility Engineering
jobs.excerpt: About the Team/Role We are seeking an experienced Mobile Software Development Engineer with hands-on agentic AI experience to join WEX Mobility Engineering.
jobs.description:
About the Team/Role

We are seeking an experienced Mobile Software Development Engineer with hands-on agentic AI experience to join WEX Mobility Engineering. Our teams span the United States, India, and Brazil, delivering SaaS, mobile, and API solutions for fleet management and mobility payments across North America.

WEX Mobility products enable fleet companies and their drivers to make payments using WEX and cobranded cards at fueling stations and other participating merchants. Our solutions provide discounts and configurable spending controls across merchant acceptance, transaction amounts, and purchase frequency.

In this role, you will independently deliver mobile features from design through production, contribute to application architecture, and build AI-assisted experiences that connect customers with relevant information and actions. You will work closely with product, design, backend, and security teams to deliver secure, reliable, and intuitive solutions.


How you’ll make an impact:

  • Design, develop, test, and release mobile features using Kotlin and/or Swift.
  • Translate product requirements, designs, and wireframes into accessible, responsive, and maintainable mobile experiences.
  • Own features through implementation, testing, release, monitoring, and production support.
  • Build mobile integrations with backend AI agents that retrieve information, call tools and APIs, and execute defined workflows.
  • Implement agent workflows using structured outputs, tool calling, context management, and established orchestration patterns.
  • Apply authentication, authorization, input validation, and confirmation steps to protect sensitive data and actions.
  • Implement appropriate loading states, cancellation, timeouts, retries, and fallback experiences for AI-assisted interactions.
  • Develop automated tests and agent evaluation scenarios covering successful tasks, invalid inputs, tool failures, and unexpected model responses.
  • Use AI coding tools and engineering agents to improve development productivity, validating generated code for correctness, security, and maintainability.
  • Integrate REST APIs and collaborate with backend engineers on API contracts, error handling, and service performance.
  • Diagnose and resolve application crashes, network issues, memory problems, and performance bottlenecks.
  • Contribute to design discussions, conduct code reviews, and mentor junior engineers.
  • Improve CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, monitoring, and release practices.
  • Investigate production incidents, contribute to root cause analysis, and implement corrective actions.
  • Document technical designs, implementation decisions, and operational procedures.
  • Communicate delivery progress, dependencies, and risks clearly across a distributed team.

Experience you’ll bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Demonstrated experience independently delivering complex production mobile features and contributing to technical design.
  • Strong proficiency in Kotlin and/or Swift.
  • Strong understanding of the mobile development lifecycle, application architecture patterns such as MVVM, asynchronous programming, and state management.
  • Hands-on experience building an agentic AI application or feature using large language models, tool or function calling, and API integration.
  • Understanding of model limitations and practical approaches to validating outputs, restricting tool access, and handling failures.
  • Experience consuming REST APIs, handling JSON data, and implementing resilient network communication.
  • Experience writing unit, integration, and UI tests and troubleshooting issues across mobile and backend boundaries.
  • Understanding of secure mobile development, authentication, authorization, and sensitive data handling.
  • Experience with performance optimization, memory management, and background processing.
  • Familiarity with cloud platforms, mobile backend services, and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Strong foundations in data structures, algorithms, object-oriented design, and problem-solving.
  • Clear communication, sound technical judgment, and the ability to collaborate across teams and locations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in Android or iOS applications on Google Play or the App Store.
  • Experience shipping AI-assisted or agentic features to production.
  • Familiarity with an agent orchestration framework, Model Context Protocol (MCP), or retrieval-augmented generation.
  • Experience implementing agent evaluation, tracing, and monitoring.
  • Experience in payments, financial services, fleet management, or transaction-based applications.
  • Experience improving existing codebases and working within legacy system constraints.

The base pay range represents the anticipated low and high end of the pay range for this position. Actual pay rates will vary and will be based on various factors, such as your qualifications, skills, competencies, and proficiency for the role. Base pay is one component of WEX's total compensation package. Most sales positions are eligible for commission under the terms of an applicable plan. Non-sales roles are typically eligible for a quarterly or annual bonus based on their role and applicable plan. WEX's comprehensive and market competitive benefits are designed to support your personal and professional well-being. jobs.title: Senior Manager, WW Planning
jobs.excerpt: Who we are Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

We are looking for a strategic, results-oriented leader to drive Samsara’s NPI planning process and manage supply chain fiscal strategy to meet revenue and cost targets. You will lead a team that owns product lifecycle support and new product introduction, financial accountability, and strategic initiatives aimed at improving operational processes.

The ideal candidate for this role has a proven track record of managing product lifecycles, can translate operational complexities to cross-functional stakeholders, and is a strategic problem solver/influencer at all levels of the organization. You see the big picture and look holistically at how each piece fits into a larger customer lifecycle experience, understanding the financial impacts of decisions from a gross margin, COGS, cash flow, and accounting perspective. You excel at partnering across the organization and have the intellectual curiosity to deeply understand Samsara’s product suite and the solution set for customers.

This is a remote position based in the United States. This role is open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. Youwill be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will:

  • Own cross-functional communication on hardware product launch dates in conjunction with the sustaining Demand Planning and Supply Planning team, setting plans that consider go to market factors and minimize E&O exposure.
  • Own the hardware cash out forecast, with real-time views and clear explanations of the business drivers leading to deltas.
  • Translate the corporate revenue plan into an executable product / geo / segment view for the sustaining planning team.
  • Communicate to leadership regarding overall NPI program health, changes in business trends, and risks & opportunities to the plan of record.
  • Manage average selling price (ASP) forecasts, discounting trends, and deal cycle analytics that feed into sustaining planning team, collaborating on insights and areas of opportunity.
  • Identify synergies and areas of opportunity to drive revenue improvement by geography and sales segmentation.
  • Liaise with F&S team on long term financial outlook (i.e. revenue, cash flow, warranty, and E&O), aligning on budget specifics that support company objectives and managing operations within budget guidelines.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, providing data-driven insights to support strategic decisions and gaining buy-in from key executive stakeholders (e.g. Procurement cost drivers and Product roadmaps).
  • Scope and own high impact projects that don’t fit neatly within one team’s scope, ensuring holistic solutions that drive top and bottom line impact.
  • Establish a deep understanding of Samsara’s business, products, and company priorities to assist Demand Planners and Supply Planners with insights for new programs / features, customer trends, and continuous improvement.
  • Assist in developing the Planning strategic roadmap, measuring and reporting progress on programs in flight and improving processes based on a comprehensive understanding of Samsara's mission and strategic goal.
  • Cultivate long-term relationships with key stakeholders and customers, understanding their needs and how Samsara can meet them.
  • Automatically included - do not run through Bias Decoder:
    • All Roles: Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
    • People Manager Roles: Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant analytical field (e.g. finance / economics / mathematics / computer science / data science).
  • 10+ years experience in forecasting, demand planning, financial planning, or similar function, with at least 3+ years directly managing teams.
  • Proven ability to attract and hire top talent, with a passion for coaching, mentoring, and developing others, using a humble leadership approach to drive a high-performing team.
  • Exceptional communication skills, including the ability to quickly synthesize information in a digestible format for a wide variety of stakeholders, including senior leadership, across different media.
  • Excellent team player who values other views and can earn stakeholder confidence quickly, exerting influence to drive priorities and deliver results.
  • An inquisitive mindset to business challenges, looking to question assumptions and bring creativity to solve problems.
  • Familiarity with NPI launches and previous experience with Product and Engineering teams.
  • Overall understanding of levers that drive free cash flow and gross margin.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • MBA or other Master’s degree.
  • Passion for building a world-class customer experience (internal and external).
  • Prior experience using Databricks, NetSuite, Salesforce, and e2open.
  • Experience in high-growth, innovative and complex organizations in a startup or a public company.
  • Deep understanding of electronics products.

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary
$118,160—$189,900 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co.
