jobs.title: Senior Pharmacy Patient Advocate (2026-8112)
jobs.excerpt: The Senior Pharmacy Patient Advocate serves as the primary point of contact and dedicated case owner for specialty pharmacy patients from initial enrollment through ongoing therapy adherence.
jobs.description:
The Senior Pharmacy Patient Advocate serves as the primary point of contact and dedicated case owner for specialty pharmacy patients from initial enrollment through ongoing therapy adherence. Operating within a patient support services model, this role combines patient advocacy, manual and in-depth benefits verification, prior authorization management, and longitudinal care coordination to ensure patients can access, afford, and remain on their prescribed specialty therapy. The Senior Pharmacy Patient Advocate demonstrates the ability to guide patients and healthcare providers through every stage of the therapy journey, from first contact to long-term adherence, with empathy, urgency, and a strong commitment to accuracy and patient confidentiality.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Patient Enrollment & Onboarding

  • Serve as the first point of contact for inbound patient and healthcare provider calls, accurately identifying needs and routing or resolving accordingly.

  • Review, process, and complete patient enrollment applications and supporting documentation for manufacturer Patient Assistance Programs (PAP) and specialty patient support services programs with a strong sense of urgency.

  • Process enrollment forms and supporting documents for missing, inconsistent, or updatable information; obtain outstanding items through outbound correspondence. Knowledge/ability to leverage internet-based tools/technology to identify missing information prior to outreaching to patients/providers to obtain.

  • Pre-screen and verify patient eligibility based on PAP and other program criteria; communicate eligibility determinations to patients and authorized representatives daily.

  • Verify prescription information prior to processing, including prescriber, patient demographics, medication, dose, quantity, and refill authorization.

  • Notify patients, authorized representatives, healthcare providers of enrollment approvals, denials, and required next steps in a timely and professional manner.

  • Assist with coordination of shipment and medication fulfillment and delivery.

  • Explain program eligibility, services, and enrollment processes clearly to patients, caregivers, authorized representatives, and physician office staff.

  • Prioritize workload to ensure patient enrollments are processed within program-specified timeframes.

Benefits Verification & Payer Management

  • Perform comprehensive patient-level benefits verifications across commercial, Medicare (Parts A, B, C, D), Medicaid, and supplemental insurance plans.

  • Assess patients’ financial ability to afford therapy and provide hands-on guidance toward appropriate financial assistance programs and coverage options.

  • Identify and locate prior authorization (PA) templates per payer-specific requirements; track and follow through on all outstanding PAs to ensure timely coverage.

  • Identify and locate prior authorization appeal templates per payer-specific requirements and communicate requirements to healthcare providers. Track and follow through on all outstanding prior authorization appeals to ensure timely coverage.

  • Track payer and plan issues by region; identify trends and report changes or systemic issues to management promptly.

  • Research insurance options and explain available programs to patients, assisting them in selecting the best available coverage for their situation.

Longitudinal Case Management & Therapy Adherence

  • Maintain continuous ownership of each patient case from initial enrollment through active therapy, serving as the primary liaison for all parties — patient, caregiver, prescriber, pharmacy, and payer.

  • Conduct proactive outbound calls and correspondence to patients and providers to share enrollment status details and other program related details.

  • Update internal case statuses and coordinate with pharmacy partners to ensure accurate, real-time therapy and shipment status.

  • Provide patients with order availability, tracking, and shipping information as needed; schedule and coordinate treatment delivery to the patient or healthcare provider.

  • Perform problem-solving on refill-related issues, prescription changes (dose, medication, prescriber), and insurance transitions to prevent gaps in therapy.

  • Self-audit case activities regularly to identify errors, inefficiencies or adherence risks and correct proactively.

Communication & Escalation Management

  • Maintain accurate, detailed notations for every patient interaction in the appropriate case management system, ensuring a complete and auditable record.

  • Investigate unresolved issues at first contact and follow through to full resolution; provide first-call resolution wherever possible.

  • Concurrently manage multiple open cases and outstanding items, ensuring all are resolved within program-required timeframes.

  • Handle program-specific patient/provider escalations; determine mitigation strategies and communicate resolutions to all involved stakeholders.

  • Respond to program inquiries from patients, authorized representatives, healthcare providers, advocates, and caregivers in a prompt, courteous, and compliant manner.

Compliance & Regulatory Responsibilities

  • Maintain strict patient confidentiality in accordance with HIPAA regulations, applicable privacy standards, and all state and federal laws at all times.

  • Recognize and report adverse events (AE) and product quality complaints (PQC) received during patient interactions in accordance with standard operating procedures and current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP).

  • Follow program-specific business rules, timelines, and processing protocols; adapt quickly to changes in program requirements.

  • Accurately capture and update patient data and case information in all applicable systems; apply strong attention to detail in all data entry activities.

  • Prepare and maintain patient profiles, medication administration records, and related case documentation for pharmacist review where applicable.

The above duties are meant to be representative of the position and not all-inclusive.

MINIMUM JOB REQUIREMENTS:

  • High School diploma or equivalent required.

  • Minimum 5 years of experience in patient support services, specialty pharmacy, or a patient support hub environment.

  • Minimum 5 years of benefits verification experience across commercial, Medicare (Parts A, B, C, D), Medicaid, and supplemental insurance plans, including working knowledge of U.S. private and government payer policies.

  • Minimum 5 years of prior authorization submission, follow-up, and appeals processing.

  • Familiarity with HIPAA regulations and patient privacy standards.

  • Proven ability to manage a caseload independently, prioritize competing tasks, and meet deadlines in a high-volume environment.

  • Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and case management software systems.

jobs.description:
InfoTrust is a global, privately-owned products and solutions company dedicated to unlocking the power of data to drive marketing performance and business growth. We specialize in digital analytics, media enablement, and privacy-centric solutions that help Fortune 100–500 companies and the world’s largest brands optimize their marketing strategies. Our culture is built on passion, ownership, diversity, trust, respect, and continuous growth—values that have earned us multiple “Best Places to Work” awards, including a Great Place to Work certification 7 years in a row.

About the role

InfoTrust is growing a portfolio of enterprise SaaS products, and we want quality built into how we develop them, not checked at the end. As a Quality Engineer – Automation, you’ll join our quality engineering team inside R&D. You’ll own test planning and automated testing for your assigned features, and you’ll help build the shared frameworks, standards and CI/CD integration the whole team uses to test our products across the UI, APIs, services and data.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role reporting to Engineering leadership. Leadership sets your main product focus when you’re hired. You’ll work closely with other quality engineers, engineering managers, developers, DevOps and product teams. The goal is simple: catch defects before they reach production, not after.

In your first 90 days you’ll learn our products, architecture and shared frameworks. Then you’ll start building automated tests for your features. By day 90, your releases will ship against a complete test plan, with your tests running in the pipeline.

What you'll do

  • Write the test plan for every feature you own before it ships. You’ll document and plan test cases with engineering managers and developers so each release is fully covered.
  • Design, build and maintain automated functional, regression, performance and API tests for your features, using the team’s shared frameworks.
  • Validate and query data in SQL and NoSQL databases to set up test data, check results and troubleshoot.
  • Monitor test results, analyze failures and report issues with diagnostics clear enough for the team to act on quickly.
  • Help extend the team’s test automation frameworks so they stay scalable and maintainable as our products grow.
  • Integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines so every change is validated on its way to production.
  • Work with other quality engineers, developers, DevOps and product teams to cover microservices and cloud-based architectures without gaps or duplicated work.
  • Follow the team’s testing standards, propose improvements to them, and advocate for testability and engineering best practices across the development lifecycle.

Qualifications

  • 2-5 years of test automation experience on web, API or cloud-based systems
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field
  • Solid grounding in software testing principles, QA methodologies and the SDLC
  • Strong programming skills in JavaScript and Node.js
  • Experience with AWS or GCP
  • Strong knowledge of relational and NoSQL databases, including writing SQL
  • Hands-on experience with CI/CD and version control, including Git
  • Experience with test automation frameworks such as Selenium, Mocha, Jest, Cypress or Playwright; API testing tools such as Postman or REST Assured; and CI/CD platforms such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps (equivalent tools are welcome)
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and a drive to keep improving
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills
  • Bonus: experience with Docker or Kubernetes, infrastructure as code and cloud test environments, performance testing tools (JMeter, Locust), or observability tools (Datadog, Prometheus)

You’ll love this role if you’d rather catch a bug before release than explain it after, you like turning repeatable checks into automation that scales, and you see quality as part of engineering, not a gate at the end.

It may not be the right fit if you expect testing to start only after development is done, you want to stay in one layer of the stack, or you’d rather build everything your own way than work within shared team frameworks.

jobs.description:
Controller

Job Description

Employment type: Full-time, exempt | Department: Finance

Location: Remote (United States) | Reports to: Chief Financial Officer

Who we are

Herself Health provides primary care designed for women 65 and older. Our model addresses the needs of women later in life, including post-menopausal care, bone health, weight management, and mental, social and emotional well-being. We bring personalized care and meaningful relationships to the communities we serve.

Our Mission: We deliver exceptional, compassionate, and high value advanced primary care for the unique needs of maturing women, empower HER to live a healthier, fuller life.

How you will work

We look for colleagues who put patients first, collaborate across teams and take ownership of their work. You bring curiosity, sound judgment and a willingness to learn, using feedback and data to improve how we care for patients and support one another.

Our values guide how we work, make decisions and show up for our patients and one another. We bring them to life through our everyday actions:

Her, First — We center every decision on the women we serve.

Curious, Always Learning — We ask questions, seek feedback and keep improving.

Own it, Act — We take responsibility, follow through and solve problems.

Together, Unstoppable — We share knowledge and support each other to deliver better care.

About the role

The Controller owns Herself Health's accounting operations end to end: the monthly close, the general ledger, accounts payable, and payroll processing. This is a hands-on role for someone who can do the work and build the function at the same time. You will bring accounting in-house from an outsourced provider, shorten the close, and give leadership and the board financials they can rely on.

Herself Health is a multi-site women's primary care organization based in Minnesota. We operate under an MSO-PC structure and serve patients through both fee-for-service and value-based contracts, including Medicare Advantage. The finance team is small and growing, so the Controller will work directly with the CFO and the Director of FP&A and will have real influence over how the function is built.

What you will do

Monthly close and general ledger

  • Own the month-end close across all entities, including the MSO, the professional corporations, and intercompany activity, and deliver complete financial statements on a set close calendar.
  • Prepare and post journal entries, accruals, prepaids, fixed asset and depreciation entries, and the PTO accrual.
  • Reconcile all balance sheet accounts monthly, including cash, accounts receivable, accrued liabilities, and payer-related balances.
  • Record revenue from Athena and outside AR reporting, including contractual adjustments and value-based contract accruals, working with RCM and FP&A.
  • Maintain the chart of accounts, dimensions, and reporting structure in Sage Intacct.
  • Produce the monthly financial package and variance explanations for the CFO, and support board and investor reporting.

Payroll

  • Process payroll each pay cycle accurately and on time, including new hires, terminations, rate changes, bonuses, and off-cycle runs.
  • Partner with HR on employee changes, benefit deductions, and PTO balances so payroll data stays clean at the source.
  • Reconcile payroll to the general ledger every cycle and allocate labor cost by clinic and department.
  • Maintain compliance with multi-state payroll tax filings, withholding, and year-end reporting (W-2s, 1099s) in coordination with the payroll provider.
  • Document payroll procedures and train backups so coverage is never dependent on one person.

Accounts payable, cash, and spend

  • Oversee accounts payable in Bill.com and corporate card activity in Ramp, including coding, approvals, and timely vendor payment.
  • Manage the accounting mailbox and vendor correspondence.
  • Perform bank and credit card reconciliations and support weekly cash reporting.
  • Enforce the procurement, purchasing card, and capitalization policies.

Controls, audit, and compliance

  • Design, document, and maintain internal controls and accounting policies appropriate for a growing, investor-backed company.
  • Lead the annual financial statement audit and serve as the primary contact for external auditors.
  • Support tax compliance with outside advisors, including income tax, the MinnesotaCare provider tax, and sales and use tax.
  • Keep entity-level accounting clean across the MSO-PC structure as new entities and markets are added.

Building the function

  • Lead the transition of accounting from the outsourced provider to an in-house operation, including knowledge transfer, cutover, and the first independent closes.
  • Shorten the close timeline and automate recurring work wherever Sage Intacct, Bill.com, and Ramp allow.
  • Recommend staffing and process changes as the organization grows.

What you bring

Required qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in accounting or finance.
  • 8 or more years of progressive accounting experience, including at least 3 years as a Controller or Assistant Controller.
  • Direct, hands-on ownership of a full monthly close and multi-entity consolidation.
  • Hands-on experience processing multi-state payroll and reconciling it to the general ledger.
  • Strong working knowledge of US GAAP and experience leading an external audit.
  • Advanced Excel skills and experience with a cloud ERP.
  • Comfort working as a player-coach in a lean team where the Controller does the work personally.

Preferred qualifications

  • Active CPA license.
  • Healthcare provider experience, especially physician practice, MSO-PC, or multi-site clinic accounting.
  • Familiarity with healthcare revenue recognition, payer contracts, and value-based care arrangements.
  • Experience with Sage Intacct, Bill.com, and Ramp.
  • Experience moving accounting from an outsourced firm to in-house, or building an accounting function from the ground up.
  • Background in a venture-backed or private-equity-backed company.

Performance expectations

First 90 days

  • Accounting is fully transitioned in-house with no missed closes, payrolls, or vendor payments.
  • Payroll runs under the Controller's ownership, with documented procedures and trained backups.
  • A close calendar and reconciliation checklist are in place and followed.

First year

  • The monthly close is consistently completed in 10 business days.
  • Every balance sheet account is reconciled monthly with support on file.
  • The annual audit is completed on schedule with no material adjustments.
  • Core accounting policies and controls are documented and operating.

Location and schedule

Work arrangement: Remote (United States). Full-time, exempt position within the Finance department.

Equal opportunity

We support Equal Employment Opportunities (EEO). We are committed to an inclusive workplace. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender identity or expression, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, parental status, political affiliation, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Compliance expectations

All employees of Herself Health are expected to fully understand and abide by the practice's compliance policies and procedures. Employees are provided training upon hire and annually and regularly notified of changes as needed. It is expected that all employees will report any suspected violations of any federal or state laws to their direct supervisor, Human Resources, or the Compliance Officer.

About Us

At Onterris, we build careers grounded in purpose, responsibility and real-world impact.

“For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. Our scientists, engineers, field teams, consultants and professionals collaborate across disciplines and geographies, guiding industries and governments, ensuring that communities and environments thrive.

When you join us, you’re not just forging a career, you’re joining a movement. A movement for better thinking, smarter solutions and lasting impact.

Together, we will advance our way of life and protect the integrity of our environment every step of the way.

A Day in the Life

As an Environmental Health Scientist – Air Quality, you’ll report to the Director of Integrated Environmental Health within the Health Sciences division at Onterris. You will support a diverse portfolio of environmental projects involving air quality permitting, regulatory compliance, air dispersion modeling, and environmental risk assessment. The ideal candidate will have a strong technical background in air quality and environmental sciences, practical experience navigating federal and state environmental regulations, and the ability to manage projects and deliver high-quality technical work for clients across various industries. The successful applicant will be a well-organized self-starter with 3-5 years of experience in air quality and/or risk assessment including at least 2 years in a consulting environment. This is an excellent opportunity for an environmental professional who enjoys solving complex regulatory and technical challenges, working directly with clients and regulatory agencies, and contributing to the successful execution of consulting projects across the team. While the majority of day-to-day life will be completed in-office (or remote), opportunities to complete site visits and attend client meetings may arise.

The compensation range for this role is $100,000 to $120,000 in addition to eligibility for an annual bonus (up to 12%) based on personal, department, and company performance. The compensation range is commensurate with experience, skillset, and geographic location.

To thrive in this role, you’ll be comfortable taking ownership of the following responsibilities:

  • Manage the full life-cycle of air quality and health risk consulting projects within the Integrated Environmental Health team, serving a diverse portfolio of industrial and commercial clients. Coordinate project schedules, budgets, deliverables and resource allocation.
  • Prepare and manage air quality permit applications and interpret and apply applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations including Clean Air Act requirements. Evaluate regulatory applicability and compliance obligations for industrial facilities and other regulated sources.
  • Conduct air dispersion modeling using applicable EPA-approved methodologies, such as AERMOD. Translate the data into clear, defensible assessments of potential public health implications, partnering with toxicologists, risk assessors, and industrial hygienists to communicate findings to clients and regulators.
  • Collaborate effectively with project managers and multidisciplinary teams to communicate project status, identify technical challenges, manage priorities, and support the successful execution of multiple concurrent projects.
  • Develop and sustain strong, trusted relationships with clients, regulatory agencies, and internal team members through timely communication, technical support, and outstanding client service at every stage of the project life-cycle.

Your Expertise and Skills

These requirements reflect the knowledge, skills and abilities that help you do your best work here.

  • Ability to travel up to 15%
  • Ability to interface with cross-functional teams and all levels of personnel/management
  • Academic degree in Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Environmental Science, Chemistry, Toxicology, Public Health or other related engineering or science discipline
  • 3 – 5 years of related experience in air quality and/or risk assessment, including at least 2 years in a consulting environment
  • Working knowledge of federal, state and local air quality regulations and permitting programs, with experience performing emissions calculations
  • Proficiency in EPA-approved air dispersion models and health risk assessment concepts, with the ability to interpret modeled results against health-based criteria
  • Ability to work independently and with minimal supervision
  • ·Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships within a matrix reporting structure

Work Environment and Physical Requirements (Optional to Include)

We may provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities, consistent with applicable law, to support performance of the essential functions.

  • Lifting 50 pounds several times a day
  • Overhead lifting of over 20 pounds

NVIDIA Cosmos Curatoris an open-source, GPU-accelerated framework for preparing training data for physical AI. The platform is evolving around reusable components, multimodal sensor processing, metadata-rich datasets, and distributed execution that makes productive use of shared GPU infrastructure.


We are looking for a deeply technical Product Manager to lead high-impact initiatives across Cosmos Curator. Working with product and engineering leadership, you will connect customer needs and research advances to a focused roadmap, then drive delivery and adoption. This senior individual-contributor role combines platform product development, internal and external customer partnerships, and ecosystem growth. Your judgment will determine which capabilities to build, what to ship first, and how to turn successful experiments into repeatable production use.


What you will be doing:

  • Shape product strategy and own prioritized initiatives from discovery through release and adoption. Define requirements, minimum viable scope, success measures, and trade-offs that align engineering, research, and business stakeholders.
  • Build deep partnerships with external customers and internal NVIDIA teams across robotics, autonomous vehicles, and world models. Work with Solutions Architects and Developer Relations to identify adoption blockers, validate solutions, and move trials into production.
  • Expand multimodal and model capabilities with engineering and research. Prioritize sensor formats, timestamp alignment, calibration handling, model integrations, and data-processing algorithms against concrete customer needs and measurable output quality.
  • Own product priorities for performance, reliability, and hardware support. Establish benchmarks for throughput, cost, annotation quality, and recovery; guide investment in observability, efficient model execution, and orchestration across shared GPU infrastructure.
  • Develop partnerships with external parties. Turn integrations & feature requests into reusable product capabilities and help build an open-source ecosystem that extends sensor, model, and pipeline coverage.
  • Partner with engineering, research, marketing, and Developer Relations in exploring new use cases and bringing them to market through validated examples, deployment mentorship, technical content, and launches grounded in customer results.

What we need to see:

  • BS/MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Physics, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • A record of taking complex technical products from customer discovery to shipped capabilities and sustained adoption, with clear ownership of requirements, prioritization, and outcomes.
  • Deep expertise in at least one relevant area, such as physical AI, multimodal data, large-scale data processing, or GPU infrastructure, with the ability to make sound product decisions across adjacent areas.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

jobs.excerpt: Company Overview Our client makes inspection software for property managers.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Our client makes inspection software for property managers. It has a mobile field app, a web dashboard, reports and integrations, plus an AI that turns a spoken walkthrough into a report. The app captures geotagged photos, video and voice offline and syncs later.

The founder started the company in 2014, after trying to capture thousands of photos fast during mass move-outs in a college town. It's bootstrapped and profitable, and it grows through direct sales, referrals and partnerships. The team is fully remote and writes things down, and the CEO sets priorities with you directly.

Your Role

As Product Specialist, you'll own the path from a customer's problem to a tested release and its written notes. You'll write requirements, test features by hand, and keep engineering work on dates through clear follow-up.

You'll report to the Head of Product Engineering and work with Support, Customer Success, Marketing and the CEO. This is an individual contributor seat with no direct reports. The role is fully remote, with overlap with Pacific hours.

Success means engineers build from your requirements and their questions are about edge cases. Every roadmap item you follow has an owner, a date and a written decision. Within 6 to 12 months, you run the whole path from customer problem to release notes on your own.

You'll

  • Talk with customers and read Support trends to find where workflows break
  • Write requirements with edge cases for engineering to build from
  • Test each feature on a phone, from capture and offline sync to the final report
  • Send findings to engineering as steps, expected result and actual result
  • Trace repeated support tickets to their root cause, then confirm the fix stopped them
  • Prepare releases with Marketing and Support and check draft notes against the feature
  • Ask engineering for dates, check progress and raise risks as soon as you see them
  • Use AI to summarize customer feedback and draft first versions of requirements

You Bring

  • 3+ years in SaaS product, product ops, program or project management, QA, or implementation
  • Hands-on testing of a mobile or web product, and writing up what broke
  • Written requirements, specs or user stories with edge cases that developers built from
  • Daily use of AI tools for real work, with something you built and can demo
  • Clear written English for a US team
  • A tracker you kept current across several teams, chasing late items yourself
  • Self-direction in a small remote team with little process
  • Availability for Pacific hours

Bonus Points

  • Time in property management, field service or inspections
  • Release notes, help articles or FAQs you wrote for customers
  • A prototype you built with an AI coding tool
  • Testing a mobile app that captures offline and syncs later

What's Offered

  • Compensation based on experience and where you're based. Share your target range and we'll go from there.

Interview Process

1️⃣ First call: 30 minutes with us at atomic✳HR on what you have built, working terms and what you want next.
2️⃣ Practical exercise: you analyze a workflow and write the requirements for it, the same work the seat does each week. It shows how you find edge cases and how clearly you write for an engineer.
3️⃣ Team interview: a conversation with team members on how you would work across customers, Support, Marketing and engineering, and how you follow up when work stalls.
4️⃣ Conversation with the Head of Product Engineering: your future manager, on how you would work with engineering as it moves toward services, how you hold delivery to dates, and how you write down decisions.
5️⃣ Final with the CEO: what you would own, how you keep work moving, and how you use AI day to day.

Team Leadership

Job Description Summary

This role sets the standard for paid search across Global Markets and delivers it hands-on. Building on the strong foundation our zones and agencies have established, you will work with zone marketers, agencies, and corporate and segment teams to raise the quality and consistency of search marketing across our markets. For some zones you will design and run campaigns. For others you will guide the zone or its agency.

You will also partner closely with Corporate Marketing and business teams to run test-and-learn programs in answer engine optimization (AEO) and generative engine optimization (GEO).

Job Description

Core responsibilities

  • Search standards. Define and maintain global standards for paid search, including account structure, keyword and bidding approach, structured testing, campaign taxonomy, UTM and conversion tracking, and brief and intake requirements. Drive adoption across zones that use different delivery models.
  • Enablement. Train zone marketers and agencies on the standard, share best practices and run a search community of practice.
  • Hands-on execution. For campaigns you run, lead advanced keyword strategy, ad creation, bidding, structured A/B and multivariate testing, audience targeting and landing page optimization. Quality-check tracking and ad delivery.
  • Measurement. Define search performance reporting. Work with analytics teams to apply attribution models and track key performance indicators (KPIs), including click-through rate, conversion rate, cost per acquisition (CPA) and return on ad spend (ROAS). Present results clearly to stakeholders in and outside marketing.
  • Budget stewardship. Own and forecast central search budgets. Manage zone- and business-funded budgets for campaigns you run, and advise on those you guide. Track pacing and planned-versus-actual spend across budgets, and flag over- and underspend. Optimize for return on investment and scalability. Identify wasted spend through negative keyword and audience refinement, and reinvest the savings in higher-performing search.
  • AEO and GEO. Lead test-and-learn programs and document what you learn. You will influence, but not own, site and content decisions.
  • Multi-market delivery. Adapt search strategy across languages, currencies and regional platform behavior.
  • Collaboration. Work with Corporate Marketing (SEO and web), segment and product teams, and agencies to connect search to customer lifecycle programs. Coordinate with other digital channel teams, such as social, to support a multichannel approach.
  • Trendspotting. Track platform changes, AI capabilities in search and industry best practices, and bring them into the standard.
  • Additional responsibilities as assigned.

How you will work with zones

Zones activate search in different ways: some locally, some through their own agencies. You will adapt to each zone's model, working in one of two modes agreed with the zone.

•Lead execution. You design, launch and optimize search campaigns for one or more zones, applying the global standard directly.

•Guide and support. The zone or its agency runs its own campaigns. You provide the standard, review, benchmarking and expert guidance.

In both modes, you are accountable for the search standard and for measuring performance against it.


Qualifications

Required

  • 6–8 years in paid search, with at least 3 years in a strategy role (Mandatory)
  • Advanced English proficiency
  • Bachelor's degree in marketing, business or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Evidence of leading adoption of AI-enabled bidding or campaign types on Google and Bing.
  • Advanced proficiency in Google Ads and GA4, and experience with an enterprise bid-management platform and an enterprise analytics or business intelligence tool.
  • Track record of improving cost per acquisition (CPA), return on ad spend (ROAS) or conversion quality, and of linking search to revenue outcomes.
  • Experience influencing senior stakeholders without formal authority.
  • Clear communicator who can present to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Working knowledge of SEO and how paid and organic search complement each other.
  • Experience managing and activating paid search campaigns across multiple countries, languages and currencies, with an understanding of how local regulations, privacy requirements and market differences influence campaign setup and execution.
  • Current Google Ads Search and Google Ads Measurement certifications.

Preferred

  • Business-to-business, healthcare or other regulated-industry search experience.
  • Current Google AI-Powered Performance Ads certification.

jobs.title: Principal Systems Engineer
jobs.excerpt: We are seeking a Principal Systems Engineer to lead the architecture, engineering, and evolution of our enterprise Backup-as-a-Service (BaaS) and Disaster Recovery-as-a-Service (DRaaS) platforms.
jobs.description:
We are seeking a Principal Systems Engineer to lead the architecture, engineering, and evolution of our enterprise Backup-as-a-Service (BaaS) and Disaster Recovery-as-a-Service (DRaaS) platforms. Having recently consolidated our data protection footprint from Azure Recovery Services Vault onto Veeam, you will serve as the primary technical authority for our Veeam Backup & Replication (VBR) servers, SQL workloads, and Veeam Backup for Microsoft Azure appliances. You will own the end-to-end maturity of our BaaS and DRaaS offerings, driving cyber-resilience, intelligent automation, and scalable recovery strategies across our Azure and hybrid environments.

Key Responsibilities

  • BaaS & DRaaS Architecture & Service Delivery:
    • Design, standardize, and govern tiered BaaS and DRaaS service catalogues (e.g., Gold/Silver/Bronze tiers) mapped to business-criticality, SLAs, Recovery Time Objectives (RTO), and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO).
    • Build repeatable onboarding frameworks, policy templates, and tag-based protection rules so new Azure VMs and SQL workloads are seamlessly enrolled into BaaS/DRaaS.
    • Architect cross-region Azure disaster recovery topologies, replication pipelines, network remapping, and automated failover/failback orchestration.
    • Own periodic DR drills, chaos/recovery testing, and executive SLA compliance reporting to validate end-to-end business continuity.
  • Veeam & Azure Platform Engineering: Own the architecture, performance tuning, and lifecycle management of Veeam Backup & Replication (VBR) servers, Veeam Backup for Microsoft Azure appliances, worker configurations, and Azure Blob storage repositories.
  • Database & Application Protection: Design and optimize application-aware backup and recovery workflows for Microsoft SQL Server (transaction log backups, point-in-time recovery, and Always On Availability Groups) and mission-critical Azure VMs.
  • Ransomware Resilience & Security: Implement Zero-Trust data protection standards, including Azure Blob immutability, air-gapped cross-region copies, role-based access control (RBAC), encryption, and automated recovery verification (SureBackup).
  • Visibility, Automation & AI Initiatives: Eliminate manual operational overhead by building automated workflows, compliance reporting, and asset discovery using PowerShell, Veeam REST APIs, and Azure Resource Graph. Drive AI-assisted operational initiatives (such as predictive capacity planning, intelligent anomaly detection, and automated incident triage/root-cause analysis).
  • Capacity & Cost Optimization (FinOps): Continuously optimize backup storage consumption, retention policies, cross-region egress traffic, and Azure Blob tiering (Hot/Cool/Archive) to control cloud spend.
  • Technical Leadership: Act as the highest escalation point for complex backup/recovery incidents, establish engineering standards, author architecture documentation, and mentor senior and mid-level engineers.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience: 7+ years of hands-on experience in enterprise IT infrastructure, with at least 5+ years focused on enterprise backup, disaster recovery, and cloud data protection.
  • Backup & DR Platform Expertise: Deep architectural and operational mastery of enterprise backup and disaster recovery platforms—primarily focused on Veeam (VBR and Veeam Backup for Microsoft Azure)—with strong transferable expertise from comparable enterprise solutions (such as Commvault, Rubrik, Cohesity, Zerto, or Azure Site Recovery).
  • BaaS & DRaaS Engineering: Proven track record designing and operating service-oriented BaaS and DRaaS platforms—including SLA tiering, automated workload onboarding, cross-region replication, failover/failback execution, and DR testing across enterprise DR tools.
  • Microsoft Azure: Strong understanding of Azure core infrastructure (Azure VMs, Virtual Networks, Storage Accounts/Blob, Managed Disks, Entra ID/RBAC, Private Endpoints) and Azure Resource Graph for inventory tracking and backup coverage auditing.
  • SQL Server Backup & Recovery: Proven experience configuring and troubleshooting SQL Server backups, transaction log shipping/truncation, and granular database restores within Veeam or equivalent enterprise backup tools.
  • Automation & Scripting: Strong proficiency in PowerShell (including Veeam PowerShell modules and Azure Az modules) and REST APIs to automate job management, health checks, and reporting.

Preferred Qualifications (Plus, Not Mandatory)

  • Proficiency in KQL (Kusto Query Language) for advanced Azure Resource Graph queries, Log Analytics dashboards, and automated gap/compliance detection.
  • Veeam Certified Engineer (VMCE) or Veeam Certified Architect (VMCA) certification.
  • Experience applying AI / AIOps tools or LLM-driven workflows to infrastructure operations (e.g., automated log analysis, self-healing runbooks, or predictive storage forecasting).
  • Experience with Veeam Recovery Orchestrator (VRO) or comparable DR orchestration platforms for automated DR testing and compliance documentation.
  • Experience migrating workloads off legacy cloud backup tools (such as Azure Recovery Services Vault) and decommissioning legacy infrastructure cleanly.

Core Competencies

  • Service-Oriented Mindset: Treats backup and DR as reliable, measurable internal products with clear SLAs and seamless onboarding.
  • Architectural Ownership: Ability to balance recovery speed (RTO/RPO), security, and Azure cloud costs when designing large-scale topologies.
  • Calm Under Pressure: Decisive, methodical troubleshooting approach during high-severity outages or critical data recovery events.
  • Cross-Team Collaboration: Ability to partner effectively with Cloud, DBA, Security, and Application teams to enforce data protection standards.

Responsible for developing, integrating, and deploying autonomy and artificial intelligence algorithms for mission systems, supporting the technology development life cycle from requirements generation through development, integration, and testing, as well as research in some organizations.Develops, integrates, and implements algorithms to enable perception, motion/mission planning, controls, etc. functionality in LM products and platforms; Translates requirements and applies requirements to development code, integrating autonomy, AI or machine learning algorithms to LM products and platforms; Determines software methods to best acquire and execute knowledge; Implements algorithms into software to train systems to recognize patterns and perform specific functions; Responsible for various phases of developing and maintaining autonomy software from requirements generation, software design and development to integration, testing, troubleshooting and debugging, and implementation; Review test outcomes, conducts troubleshooting, and works to debug issues; Develops human-machine interface scenarios, breaking missions into tasks; Documents interface requirements and implements human-machine interfaces

Join our team as an AI Engineer building AI agents and the software around them for our enterprise data platform. Our current focus is an AI-driven factory that turns business data needs into governed, tested data products on Databricks. You will also work on the team’s other AI and software projects, including CI/CD automation.

You will build AI features, evaluations, and data checks from written specs, with review from senior engineers. You will learn to tell, with evidence, when AI output is good enough to use, and grow from following specs to writing them.

This role is ideal for an early-career engineer who has built software with large language models (LLMs) and wants to grow in AI engineering. It offers strong mentorship, hands-on learning, and fast skill growth.

Responsibilities include:

  • Build LLM-based components, including prompts, tool use, structured output, and validation.
  • Chain model calls and tools into multi-step agent workflows, following established patterns for retries, fallbacks, and error handling.
  • Write evaluation cases, test data, and expected results, and add scenarios to the team’s benchmark suites.
  • Run repeated evaluations and model or prompt comparisons, and report what the results show.
  • Check AI output against real data and metadata before it is used, such as confirming that the tables and columns it names exist.
  • Build retrieval and context features that ground model responses in accurate, cited sources, following senior engineers’ designs.
  • Follow the team’s guardrail patterns, so that AI output cannot approve itself or expose restricted data.
  • Build application features and APIs that show the AI’s inputs, outputs, and evaluation results.
  • Write automated tests, build and maintain CI/CD pipelines, and help diagnose failures using logs and traces.
  • Use AI coding assistants daily, write clear acceptance criteria for their work, and review everything they generate before it ships.
  • Document prompts, workflows, evaluations, and design decisions.

Basic Qualifications

  • A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, or a related STEM field, or equivalent experience.
  • 1-2 years of experience building software. Internships, co-ops, academic projects, and professional work all count.
  • Proficiency in Python.
  • Experience building software that uses an LLM API, including structured output and validation.
  • Experience writing automated tests or evaluation cases.
  • Understanding of software fundamentals, including APIs and version control.
  • Experience using AI coding assistants, such as Claude Code or similar tools, including reviewing the code they generate.
  • Strong communication skills and a collaborative, eager-to-learn approach.

Desired Skills

  • Experience with agent orchestration frameworks, such as LangGraph or LangChain.
  • Experience with Claude or other models through Amazon Bedrock.
  • Experience evaluating LLM output with test sets, repeated runs, or model and prompt comparisons.
  • Experience with retrieval, embeddings, or vector search.
  • Exposure to guardrails for AI systems, such as prompt-injection defense.
  • Exposure to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers or agent-facing APIs.
  • Experience with SQL and data engineering, such as on Databricks or Spark.
  • Experience with web application development using FastAPI, React, or TypeScript.
  • Experience with Git, CI/CD pipelines such as GitLab, and containers such as Docker.
  • Experience working on a team that uses Agile practices.
  • Completion of AI-related training programs, coursework, or certifications.
